500215|2026-06.headline: Sundrop Brands Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY (11% QoQ) with EBITDA steady at about 7% of sales, net of ESOP.
500215|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY and 11% QoQ, with B2B up 18% and e-commerce up 32%. Gross margin improved about 110 bps despite commodity and packaging inflation, and EBITDA held at about 7%, the same level as Q4 FY26. A&P was reported about 12% lower YoY, but management says about 5% lower on a like-for-like basis after reclassifying trade spends as contra-revenue. Management reiterated a target of 300 bps annual margin expansion and about 12% EBITDA by FY30, with 200 bps from Del Monte-Sundrop synergies over 18 months.

financial_highlights.value: Up about 110 bps (stated as overall margin improvement)
financial_highlights.change: Material cost efficiency +40 bps; other expenses +70 bps
Same as Q4 FY26; ESOP-burdened about 5.66%

financial_highlights.value: About 12% lower YoY as reported; about 5% lower like-for-like (21.4 vs 22.9 as % of sales)
financial_highlights.change: Reclassification of trade spends to contra-revenue; like-for-like growth about 12% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: About 56% of total business, growing about 16%
About 44-45% of total business, growing about 14%

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 share of business about 62%

segments.name: Popcorn
segments.commentary: Growing about 18% with about 12% volume growth; Ready-to-Eat growing about 39% (vs 33% last year) while Ready-to-Cook grows about 9%. Management says it holds about 85% category share.

segments.name: Culinary (ketchup, mayo, dressings)
segments.commentary: Growth accelerated to 15% from about 10% last year, with volume growth of about 8%; B2B and exports to Southeast Asia contributing.

segments.name: Premium staples / edible oil
segments.commentary: Value growth about 16% and volume growth about 7%, with about 9% of growth from price pass-through; oil is about 20% of total business. Management targets 4-5% volume growth.

segments.name: Italian (olive oil, pasta, RTE olives)
segments.commentary: Value growth returned to about 8% and volume to 15-17%; olive oil volume grew close to 20%, pasta about 10%. Q1 realisations fell due to prior-year commodity deflation pass-through.

segments.name: Peanut butter / spreads
segments.commentary: Decline narrowed to about 3% in value and volume from 8-10% last year; e-commerce returned to 16% growth. Market is about 85% value-added; company holds about 33% of standard and 3% of value-added peanut butter.

segments.name: Juices
segments.commentary: Investment dropped; management says it was not core and did not show good results.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for mid-teens to high-teens revenue growth, with about 10% volume growth, 4-5% value growth from pricing and 4-5% from innovation as the long-term mix.
EBITDA target of about 12% by FY30 (about three years), from about 7% ESOP-adjusted today; ESOP cost to stay front-loaded for 18-21 months.

Overall ambition of about 300 bps annual margin expansion, split half reinvested in growth and half returned to shareholders; about 100 bps a year from scale, 80-100 bps from premiumisation and about 100 bps a year from synergies over two years.
Del Monte and Sundrop synergies estimated at about 200 bps, delivered over about 18 months; about 8 CFA consolidations targeted by end of this year, leaving 2 of Del Monte's 10 unique CFAs.
Italian business: value growth expected to move closer to 15% if volume growth of 15% is sustained; price stabilisation expected from Q2.
Single ERP for both businesses to be decided soon, with migration expected within about 12 months, before sales-force integration.
capex_capacity: Shift to a capital-efficient model: using third-party manufacturing and outsourced systems in place of own capex; management also says it is actively looking at inorganic opportunities.
Popcorn facilities at Kashipur and Kothur are running at rising utilisation, adding to profitability on instant popcorn.
Ready-to-Eat assorted manufacturing is improving plant utilisation and freight efficiency; direct factory-to-distributor shipping cuts freight and shelf-life packaging cost (4.5-5 month shelf life).
Salesforce automation: about 80% of outlets now billed on the platform, up from about 75% at the end of Q4 FY26.
demand_pricing: Edible oil: volume 7%, value about 15-16%, with about 9% from pass-through of per-kg price increases; management is now growing volume and aims for 4-5% volume growth.
Peanut butter: management says the market has moved to about 85% value-added formats (protein, chocolate, natural) where it has about 3% share; competition includes PE-backed brands.
Popcorn Rs. 10 RTC/RTE packs are expanding into East, West and South; e-commerce growth is led by Rs. 25-50 MRP packs, with bigger packs now about 36% of RTE mix (from about 33%).
Premium staples: management says it has a lower-priced variant (Sundrop Lite and Sundrop Heart Plus) as a safety net if sunflower oil inflation drives consumers down.
Italian realisation down about 6-10% in Q1 due to higher old-price inventory being sold after last year's commodity deflation; not quick-commerce discounting per management.

qa_highlights.question: Navin (Ithought PMS): Is the YoY dip in A&P a genuine efficiency gain or a shift in focus across brands/segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said focus stayed on core categories invested since Q4 FY25 (Sundrop) and Q1 FY26 (Del Monte); Juices was dropped as non-core. Reported A&P down about 12% YoY, but after reclassifying trade spends to contra-revenue it is 21.4 vs 22.9 of sales, about 5% lower.

qa_highlights.question: Navin: Post the 4700BC acquisition by a large player, is there more competitive aggression in popcorn and what differs from ACT II's offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management holds about 85% popcorn category share and has not seen a significant shift in category behaviour since the acquisition. It has raised investment, is pushing Sweet Popcorn, and has added Cheese popcorn to e-commerce.

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Chheda (Lucky Investments): What are the blended volume and value growth rates for core and non-core?
qa_highlights.answer: Core (about 60% of sales) grows about 14-15% in value and 9-10% in volume. Edible oil (about 20% of business) grew about 16% in value and 7% in volume. The remaining ~20% grows about 15% in value and 8% in volume, helped by CP manufacturing such as energy drinks. Overall, about 80% of the business grows 15-16% in value and 8-9% in volume.

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Chheda: What are the key growth pillars and the expected value and volume mix?
qa_highlights.answer: For Popcorn, Ketchup and Mayo the pillars are distribution, media investment ahead of curve, and innovation; Italian is driven more by innovation and investment, and peanut butter by innovation. Management sees about 4-5% volume growth in most categories and aims for about 10% volume, plus 4-5% price and 4-5% innovation, targeting mid-teens to high-teens growth.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath (Nafa Asset Management): Is the 6-10% Italian realisation decline due to quick-commerce discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Kapoor said no. Q1 is running on higher-cost inventory bought before last year's commodity deflation, with price pass-through having started only in Q2 last year. Prices are now stabilising and the effect should end from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath: Is GT/MT growth likely low single digit given B2B at 18% and e-commerce at 32%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Popcorn, Italian and oil are primarily retail. Culinary is the only mixed retail and B2B business. B2B grows faster than retail, and retail is roughly 10-12% if B2B is at 18%. The company did not give a specific GT/MT number.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath: How much of the 15% edible oil growth is price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Asheesh Sharma said about 9 points is price pass-through (per-kg increase passed on almost fully) with 7% volume, giving roughly 16% value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki (IIFL Capital): What is the status of the Del Monte and Sundrop integration, and what savings are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is under a single operations team. Del Monte had 10 unique CFAs, with 2 already consolidated and a third underway; about 8 consolidations are targeted by year-end, leaving 2. ERP migration to a single system is expected within about 12 months, before sales-force integration. East distribution of Del Monte already runs through the Sundrop team. Synergies are about 200 bps over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki: EBITDA goes from about 7% to about 12% in three years. What is the breakup beyond the 200 bps synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP cost (about 5.66% after ESOP) is front-loaded for 18-21 months, adding roughly 100 bps after that. Scale is worth about 100 bps a year, premiumisation 80-100 bps a year, and synergies about 100 bps a year for two years. Management aims for about 300 bps of margin expansion a year, split half to growth and half to shareholders. FY30 12% is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Shirish Pardeshi (Motilal Oswal): What is the economics and sustainability of the Rs. 10 popcorn RTC/RTE packs and their supply chain?
qa_highlights.answer: Assorted manufacturing and direct factory-to-distributor shipping cut freight and packaging cost, with a 4.5-5 month shelf life. RTE Rs. 10 has moved from margin-dilutive to margin-accretive over 18 months. Bigger packs are about one-third of the RTE mix (from one-fifth/one-third earlier), growing 42% against 33% for the rest, and e-commerce is growing about 55%.

qa_highlights.question: Shirish Pardeshi: Will premium staples volume (7%) hold if sunflower inflation drives price up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to lower-priced variants as a safety net: Sundrop Lite and Sundrop Heart Plus, with a new Sundrop Heart blend using less-inflated commodities. It targets 4-5% volume growth in the category, which is growing about 3-4%. The Sundrop Heart Jodi pack will continue through the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Nachiket Kale (Emkay): What is the strategy for peanut butter given competition from new digital-first and PE-backed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lost the protein, natural and chocolate variant race because it lacked those products. The market is about 85% value-added and 15% standard. The company holds about 33% of standard and 3% of value-added peanut butter. It is launching new variants, investing in digital consumer acquisition, and aims for double-digit growth in the near term.

risks_watch: A&P optics: reported A&P is down about 12% YoY, but like-for-like is about 5% lower after the contra-revenue reclassification. Watch whether reclassification distorts sales and margin comparisons.
Input cost inflation in edible oil (sunflower), packaging and commodities. Management says price pass-through has so far protected margins, but B2B and some contracts have lagged price increases.
Peanut butter: still in decline at about 3% in value and volume, with only 3% share of value-added formats against 85% of the market. Competition from digital-first and PE-backed brands.
Italian business: realisation down 6-10% in Q1 from old inventory. Management expects stabilisation from Q2 and value growth of about 15% if volume growth holds at 15%.
Integration execution: CFA consolidation (about 8 targeted by year-end), ERP migration within about 12 months, and sales-force integration. Synergies of about 200 bps over 18 months.

Margin path to about 12% EBITDA by FY30 depends on ESOP cost rolling off after 18-21 months and on premiumisation and scale. Juices has been dropped as non-core, and any further portfolio exits or inorganic moves are open questions.
key_quotes: So, we are a tad higher, I would say sharply higher also than 4%, which we used to be about a year and a half back.
We have lost out that race because we did not have any of that product in the portfolio.
Our overall endeavor is to improve our margins by 300 basis points every year, of which we would want to deploy half back to the business and half back to the shareholders.
Our stated position on this category will be to protect volumes.
So, we will have to play the game as it is being played, that we are cognizant of.
500215|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on top-line momentum, B2B, e-commerce and popcorn. More cautious and evasive on peanut butter recovery, the Italian realisation dip, and the detailed bridge from 7% to 12% EBITDA, which management frames as a three-year target. Management often answered questions by restating broad ambitions rather than giving precise numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: over next 2-4 quarters, ramping toward FY30
rows.why: Management targets ~300 bps annual margin expansion and ~12% EBITDA by FY30 from ~7% today, with ~200 bps from Del Monte-Sundrop synergies over 18 months and gross margin up ~110 bps, though the bridge is only partly quantified and ESOP cost (~5.66% post-ESOP) stays front-loaded for 18-21 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management is shifting to a capital-efficient model using third-party manufacturing and outsourced systems in place of own capex, and cited no new plant, line or store commissioning dates.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Core portfolio (~60% of sales) grew 9-10% in volume and edible oil 7% with a 4-5% volume target; Italian olive oil volume ~20% and B2B 18% / e-commerce 32% growth support momentum, and about 80% of the business grows 8-9% in volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management emphasises asset-light capex and third-party manufacturing, with Kashipur/Kothur utilisation rising but no utilisation figure given that would force a new capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue grew 15% YoY and 11% QoQ and management aims at mid-teens to high-teens growth, but the Italian realisation dip (down 6-10%) and peanut butter still declining ~3% cap the near-term upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Italian realisation down 6-10% in Q1 (expected to stabilise from Q2), peanut butter still in decline at ~3%, and edible oil inflation and packaging costs could squeeze the ~7% EBITDA margin if pass-through lags, especially in B2B.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is launching new peanut butter variants (protein, natural, chocolate), a new Sundrop Heart blend, and expanding Rs. 10 popcorn packs into East, West and South, with bigger packs at ~36% of RTE mix.

rows.label: Del Monte-Sundrop integration: CFA consolidation and ERP migration
rows.when: about 8 CFA consolidations by year-end; ERP migration within
rows.why: Del Monte has 10 unique CFAs with 2 already consolidated and a third underway, and about 8 consolidations are targeted, underpinning ~200 bps of synergies over 18 months.

rows.label: Italian realisation reset
rows.why: Realisation fell 6-10% in Q1 on old high-cost inventory after last year's commodity deflation; management expects price stabilisation from Q2 and value growth nearer 15% if 15% volume holds.

rows.label: Popcorn Rs. 10 packs expanding to East, West and South
rows.why: Rs. 10 RTC/RTE packs are rolling out in these regions, RTE grew ~39% and popcorn holds ~85% category share, with e-commerce growth led by Rs. 25-50 MRP packs.

tone.note: Management was confident on popcorn, B2B, e-commerce and the 12% FY30 margin ambition, but cautious and often broad on peanut butter, the Italian realisation dip and the 7%-to-12% EBITDA bridge; analysts pressed on A&P reclassification, the Italian decline, GT/MT split and the margin breakup.

500215|2026-09.headline: Sundrop Brands Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR463 crore, with normalized EBITDA margin up 240 bps.
500215|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 21% YoY to a run rate of INR463 crore, with H1 revenue at INR891 crore (up 18%). Normalized EBITDA margin expanded 240 bps; on an unadjusted basis the expansion was 370 bps because prior-year one-off project expenses were absent this year. Growth was led by ACT II popcorn ready-to-eat, e-commerce (up about 43%, now 19% of sales) and Italian pasta, while peanut butter stabilised but remained weak in volume. Operating cash flow was negative in H1 (about INR49-50 crore per the analyst), which management attributed to deliberate inventory build in corn and oats plus receivables rising with sales.

financial_highlights.change: Edible oil margin diluted; overall margin up about 20 bps

financial_highlights.value: Close to INR90 crore, 19% of company sales

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow (H1, as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Sundrop (core brand)
segments.commentary: Grew 19% in Q2 and 17% in H1. Management says core portfolio volume growth is about 10-12%, with value growth of about 18%.

segments.name: Del Monte
segments.commentary: Grew 26% in Q2 and 20% in H1. Italian pasta volume grew about 33% in Q2 (about 25-26% normalized, per management); olive oil volume grew about 15%.

segments.name: ACT II popcorn
segments.commentary: Ready-to-eat grew 38% in value and 23% in volume in Q2; ready-to-cook grew about 12% in value and 5-6% in volume. Blended franchise volume is about 10-11%.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Q2 volume grew about 5% and value about 19%, with a target of 4-5% volume growth. Margins are being protected rather than expanded.

segments.name: Peanut butter (spreads)
segments.commentary: Value stabilised and volume still under pressure. Decline rate improved from -8% in Q4 to -3% in Q1 to about -1% in Q2. E-commerce growth is about 18%.

segments.name: Culinary (ketchup, mayo, dips, pasta sauces)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume grew 13% (H1 11%) and value grew 21% in Q2 (H1 18%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume growth to stay around 10-11% for the portfolio, with about 3-4% from premiumisation and 6-7% from price increases (value growth is driven by price).
Edible oil volume target of 4-5% growth, with margins protected rather than expanded. Foods is expected to drive margin expansion.
Olive oil volume growth expected at about 12-15% in Q3; pasta momentum expected to continue into the festive season.
Peanut butter e-commerce growth targeted to move ahead of category growth within two quarters; entry into modern trade and general trade targeted for FY28.
Working capital: management expects inventory and receivable levels to normalise in Q3 as uncertainty stabilises.
Price increases in Del Monte annual export and key-account contracts are expected mainly in Q4 (December to March renewals), not Q1.
No significant input-cost-led margin impact or further price increase expected in the coming quarter; popcorn corn contracts for next year are secured with no significant inflation expected.
Management says it does not see an inflationary environment in the next 3-4 months, with recent edible oil moves in the range of plus or minus 5%.
capex_capacity: Growth model is shifting to capital-efficient use of third-party (3P) manufacturing sites alongside existing plants; management did not give capex amounts or capacity figures.
Popcorn sourcing is diversified: indirect contract farming with Indian growers in Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, with harvest by February, plus imported varieties for microwave packs.
Sales Force Automation completed; about 400,000 outlets directly covered, with about 80% of outlets ordering regularly in Q2 FY27.
24 new products launched in Q2 and about 120+ over the last two years; about 6% of sales come from NPDs launched in the last two years.
Advertising-to-sales ratio on core categories is about 9%, against a stated target of 9-10%, up from about 4-5% historically. Core categories are about 60-63% of the portfolio.
demand_pricing: Pricing: broad-based inflation in packaging and edible oil was passed to consumers through calibrated price increases. Price contributed about 6-7% to growth.
Edible oil pricing is calibrated to keep premium staples stable. Government cut edible oil duty in September, and management says the benefit was partly passed on.
E-commerce growth of 43% is driven by performance marketing, tech capability and upgrades to larger packs. The channel is growing about 18-25% overall, per management.
Quick commerce is a structural tailwind for snacking and impulse consumption, which is helping ACT II RTE growth.
General trade is expected to grow more slowly than e-commerce, modern trade and quick commerce, though sales force automation is improving ROI there.
Culinary export business in Southeast Asia is growing with new product introductions, and B2B key-account penetration is increasing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ready-to-cook volume growth in ACT II, and is e-commerce driving the popcorn volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: RTC volume grew about 5-6% and the blended popcorn franchise about 10-11%. E-commerce is upgrading consumers to larger packs; RTE large-pack growth was about 53% against 23% for small packs, for a blended RTE growth of about 37%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is peanut butter losing share, and what is the plan to win it back?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium value-added variants (chocolate, high-protein, zero-separation) rose from 8.3% of saliency in Q1 to 12.4% in Q2. Decline has narrowed to about -1% in Q2. The e-commerce target is to grow ahead of category within two quarters, with modern trade entry in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow negative in H1, and will Q3 turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to deliberate inventory build in corn and oats for supply security, plus receivables rising with sales. DSOs were stable. Management expects levels to normalise in Q3 as uncertainty eases.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Italian volume growth jump to 30%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Pasta volume grew about 33% and olive oil about 15%. Part of the jump is from a weak base after the September GST change; normalised pasta growth is about 25-26%. Olive oil growth is guided at 12-15% for Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of core versus non-core growth, and is the trend continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Core volume is growing about 12%, against 10% previously, and is about 2x non-core volume. Edible oil value grew about 15% on volume of about 5%. Core value growth is about 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin outlook and do you need further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no major input-cost pressure in the next quarter. Del Monte export and key-account contracts will be repriced mainly in Q4, which should help margins from then.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 21% growth split between volume, innovation and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume is about 10%, innovation and premiumisation add about 3-4%, and price increases add about 6-7%.

risks_watch: Negative H1 operating cash flow driven by inventory build and receivables; Q3 normalisation needs to be confirmed.
Peanut butter volume is still declining (about -1% in Q2), and the premium variants are only 12.4% of saliency. Recovery depends on e-commerce momentum moving into general trade and modern trade.
Edible oil margin is being protected rather than expanded. Commodity volatility of plus or minus 5% is manageable, but the outlook could change.
Advertising spend is down YoY in the quarter (management says it is up sequentially). Competitive intensity in spreads is rising.
E-commerce growth (43%) may not hold through the festive season, and quick commerce pricing and competition could affect it.
Del Monte price increases depend on contract renewals in December to March, so the benefit lands mainly in Q4.
500215|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth momentum and margins, with a clear focus on ROI-led marketing. Management was more guarded on peanut butter volume, edible oil margins and the timing of working capital normalisation. Some answers were long and repeated points, and the quantitative breakdown of cash flow was less precise than analysts wanted.
key_quotes: Our revenue grew by 21% year-on-year in Q2, which is supported with a very strong and healthy momentum of growth across our core categories and across our emerging channels.
In Edible Oil business, our strategy has been more calibrated increasing to keep our pricing premium stable constant.
So I would say a real way to look is to read this number is about 10% volume, 3% premiumization and 6% to 7% impact is coming on account of price increases.
Today, we have reached about 18% growth. Our ambition will be within next 2 quarters to put it ahead of category growth in e-commerce channel.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Normalized EBITDA margin up 240 bps in Q2 with Foods driving expansion, and Del Monte export/key-account price increases land mainly in Q4 (Dec-Mar renewals), though edible oil margins are only being protected and no input-cost pressure is seen next quarter.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capex amounts or capacity figures given; growth is shifting to capital-efficient third-party manufacturing, and modern and general trade entry for peanut butter is targeted for FY28, but no utilisation or plant additions were disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides portfolio volume growth of about 10-11% (3-4% premiumisation plus price-independent core volume ~12%), olive oil guided at 12-15% in Q3, and edible oil at 4-5%, though peanut butter volume is still about -1% in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; no utilisation level was disclosed, so the case for a new capex announcement cannot be read from this call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Growth of 21% in Q2 and 18% in H1 is running ahead of the ~10-11% volume plus 6-7% price framework, but management did not raise guidance and volume remains guided at 10-11%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative (about INR49-50 crore) and working capital normalisation in Q3 is not yet confirmed, while peanut butter volume remains at about -1% and e-commerce at 43% may not hold through the festive season.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 24 new products launched in Q2 and about 120+ over two years, with NPDs at about 6% of sales; premium peanut butter variants rose to 12.4% of saliency and Culinary export is adding new product introductions.

rows.label: Inventory and receivables normalise in Q3
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was about negative INR49-50 crore from corn/oats inventory build and receivables rising with sales; management expects normalisation in Q3 but gave no figures.

rows.label: Del Monte export and key-account repricing
rows.why: Price increases in annual export and key-account contracts are expected mainly in Q4, as December to March renewals come up, so the benefit lands after the next quarter.

rows.label: Peanut butter volume recovery
rows.why: Decline narrowed from -8% in Q4 to -3% in Q1 and about -1% in Q2, with e-commerce targeted to grow ahead of category within two quarters, but volume is still negative.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth momentum, margins and ROI-led marketing, but guarded on peanut butter volume, edible oil margins and working capital timing; analysts pressed on the cash flow breakdown and the sustainability of the Italian pasta jump.

500219|2026-03.headline: Jain Irrigation Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of quarterly sales.
500219|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR1,800 crore versus about INR1,750 crore a year earlier, with Hi-Tech up about 8%, Plastics down slightly and Agro Processing up about 6%. Consolidated EBITDA grew about 7% and margin rose to 13.2% from 12.8%, with Hi-Tech margin at 19.8% versus 17.5%. Management attributed the shortfall versus its earlier expectation to a polymer price spike in late February to March that made farmers postpone purchases. Reported PAT was negative at about INR40 crore, driven by one-time tax and non-cash items; management cited an adjusted PAT of about INR133 crore. Management said the debt repayment due in September and March FY27 will be met from internal accruals, with refinancing and equity as backups.

segments.name: Hi-Tech (drip irrigation, tissue culture, solar agri pumps)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 8% and EBITDA up about 22%, margin 19.8%; FY26 revenue up over 20%. Domestic business grew about 12% and retail about 13% (target above 15%).

segments.name: Plastics (pipes and plastic sheets)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue slightly down and EBITDA up 3.3%, margin 10.2%; FY26 revenue up only 2.4% and EBITDA declined. Pipes did not grow in FY26 and are expected to grow in FY27; overseas sheet business doing well.

segments.name: Agro Processing / Food
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 6% but EBITDA declined; FY26 revenue above INR2,000 crore (up 9%) and EBITDA up about 9%. UK food revenue rose to GBP68 million from GBP60 million, with cost headwinds; beverage lines started in Q4.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports about INR455 crore versus INR500 crore, down about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management plans to be PAT positive (after adjustments) in FY27, and says it expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet.

Standalone operating cash flow expected to rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore in FY27, helped by about INR450 crore of government receivables and about INR150 crore of government benefits.
Management expects the second half of Q4 to be better than the first and July onwards to be better, unless another price shock occurs.
Beverage: three more lines under discussion for FY27 investment. Tomato processing plant with a Japanese partner expected to start around January.
Management declined to give numeric FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty.
Management said a food IPO is not expected in the first half of FY27; it will reassess in the second half.
capex_capacity: Beverage bottling: about INR140 crore invested over December and March quarters; two lines started in February and March, with about INR27-28 crore revenue before end-March. Three more lines are under discussion, with investment possibly in December-January.
Tamil Nadu land asset sale: MoU signed; management expects closure within weeks to a month or two. Amount not disclosed.
Alwar plant in Rajasthan is being expanded to grow pipe sales in North India.
Management says the first big government projects are complete, but final milestones remain pending.
demand_pricing: PVC and polyethylene prices rose by more than 50% within about 20 days (polyethylene about 60%) between 20 February and 25 March. Late April and early May, PVC fell to about 10% above February levels, while polyethylene remained about 40% higher.
Farmers postponed purchases in March and April; management says PVC pipe demand has since returned. Monsoon is expected to be below normal, which management sees as supportive of irrigation demand.

Management says about INR200-250 crore of Q4 revenue was lost to the March shock; standalone Q4 revenue would otherwise have been about INR1,250 crore versus about INR1,000 crore, with EBITDA about INR25 crore higher.

500233|2026-03.headline: Kajaria Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR 1,373 crore with volume up 11% and EBITDA margin at 19.19% versus 10.01% a year ago.
500233|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 1,373 crore, with tiles volume up 11%, helped by sales-channel unification and a Morbi shutdown that cut industry supply. EBITDA margin expanded to 19.19% from 10.01%, and PAT rose to INR 136 crore from INR 43 crore. Production fell about 7% in the quarter as Morbi plants shut in March, and inventory was drawn down by roughly 1.5 million square meters. Management says all plants, including Morbi, have run at full capacity since 16 April, but outsourcing from Morbi remains uncertain. Management declined to give volume guidance and said it expects margins of 18% to 19%.

qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Kajaria said growth was not only due to Morbi, with January and February volume up 8% to 9%. Management would not split quarterly numbers but said the momentum has started. Sanjeev Agarwal said Q1 is historically weak and full-year FY27 will be much better.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes were taken and how do gas costs compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases of about 12% to 13% in North and 16% to 17% in Morbi and South, effective early March. Management said the hikes cover the gas cost increase with some margin. Further prices rose 1 April, and realisations may be partly offset by discounts.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12% to 15% price increase fully reflect in Q1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Rishi Kajaria said some realisation increase is definite. Sanjeev Agarwal said it cannot be quantified because the situation is dynamic and some discounts may be given.

500233|2026-06.headline: Kajaria Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20% to INR1,328 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.6%, driven mainly by fuel-cost-led price hikes.

Morbi gas-price dislocation has narrowed the price gap between Kajaria and Morbi peers from about 40% to under 20%.

500233|2026-09.headline: Kajaria Q2 FY27: volumes up 10% YoY, consolidated revenue up 24% to INR1,468 crore, EBITDA margin 19.5%, guided to stay around current levels.
500233|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,468 crore on 10% volume growth and price hikes taken in North and South plants (12-13%) and at Morbi (18-19%). EBITDA margin was 19.5% versus 17.94% a year earlier, and PAT rose to INR190 crore from INR133 crore. Management said export demand stayed subdued on freight and container constraints, while gas costs stayed high and are expected to remain tight. Management guided to double-digit volume growth over the next two quarters, stable margins, and new GVT capacity at Srikalahasti and Gailpur, with no further price hikes planned for now.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR124 crore, up 22% YoY. Margin is currently low because the new plant is under-utilised; management expects it to approach tile margins next year. Sanitary and faucet growth of 21% split about 50% price and 50% volume.

Propane is now only about 5% cheaper than gas after rising in recent days; Brent is about $116 and management expects propane to rise further over the next 15 days.
Management estimates market growth at 5-6%, with the rest from share gains. About 40-50% of Morbi's 400-500 plants are not operating.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes were taken and how much is year-to-date?
qa_highlights.answer: North and South plants raised prices about 12-13% across ceramic, PVT and GVT; Morbi about 18-19%. These are cumulative hikes to date, not Q2 only. Management said no price hike was taken in Q2 and none is planned for Q3 at present.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gas cost outlook and are price hikes needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Average gas cost in Q2 was about INR70/SCM (North ~INR70.56, South INR63, West INR75). Management expects a cost increase in Q3 for West, but targets a significant reduction from January through shorter firing cycles and cheaper sourcing. No further end-product price hikes are needed for now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Srikalahasti capex increase and why are they adding capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised to 12.5 MSM from 10 MSM, with capex rising to about INR240 crore from INR210 crore due to a larger shed and warehouse. Expansion is intended to support double-digit volume growth and gas advantage over Morbi.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth dilute margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blended margin will remain around current levels. Future margin gains are expected from operating leverage, lower freight costs, and cheaper GVT capacity, but management is not guiding above about 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and borrowing change?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses at INR138 crore are expected to stay at this level due to higher advertising. Management said borrowings were working-capital draws, partly to fund JV bank limits, and treasury loans of about INR155 crore went to NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the adhesives and bathware businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhesives revenue is guided to about INR240 crore in FY27 and about INR400 crore next year. Bathware margin is low now but should approach tile margins next year.

500238|2026-03.headline: Whirlpool of India Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR 2,181 crore, but PBT margin fell to 5% on e-waste and energy-change costs.
500238|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew high single digits to INR 2,181 crore, helped by washers, air conditioners (up about 50%) and Elica (up 30%), with March 2026 the highest shipment month in company history. Profit fell sharply: EBITDA was INR 121 crore (5.6%, down 33.7%) and profit before exceptional items INR 110 crore (5%, down 29%), mainly from incremental e-waste provisions and unrecovered BEE energy-upgrade costs. Refrigerator market share fell triple digits in direct cool and frost free due to the January 2026 energy-regulation phase-in/phase-out and deliberate non-matching of competitor pricing. For FY26, revenue rose 1.4% to INR 8,034 crore, EBITDA was INR 481 crore (6%), and reported PBT fell 19% including a INR 38.8 crore one-time wage code charge. Management gave no margin guidance and flagged FY27 as a difficult year.

segments.commentary: Gaining share: front load volumes doubled in Q4 with triple-digit share gains; top load strong double-digit gains with a number two position in Q4 (multi-brand outlet volume); semi-automatic number two, with Dynamix technology now nearly half of that business.

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Crossed 100,000 units in March 2026; Q4 growth above 50%, FY26 growth above 40%. ASP roughly 2x core products, and working capital is heavier, with a planned AC inventory and receivables build lifting Q4 networking capital.

segments.name: Elica (kitchen appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 30% (32% per CFO) and PBT up 48%; FY26 revenue up 12% and profit up 15%. Management wants to keep margins in the double digits.

guidance_outlook: No margin guidance given; management called FY27 difficult for the industry and the company due to energy changes, e-waste provisions, competitive pricing and the Middle East war.
Long-term ambition: high single-digit margins for refrigerator, washing machine and AC business; revenue growth ambition moved to early double digits.
Large-capacity frost free refrigerator launch planned for Q2 FY27, filling a portfolio gap.

No buyback under consideration at this point; cash to be deployed in organic or inorganic growth.
capex_capacity: CWIP of about INR 200 crore relates to the premium frost free refrigerator capacity, expected to be capitalised after the Q2 FY27 launch.

Automation across factories and cost-saving capex (factory, product, network) under evaluation, traded off against payback.

demand_pricing: Industry grew low single digits in Jan-Mar 2026 and was roughly flat for FY26; refrigerator industry declined for the year, led by direct cool.
Competitive pricing remained very aggressive; the company chose not to match it fully, which cost volume share.

Management flagged Middle East war impacts on oil-linked inputs, imported components (20-35% of components for industry players) and forex.

In March 2026 the company reached number two in refrigerator plus washing machine volume share in multi-brand outlets (for one month); it was number one in direct cool for four months from December 2025.

qa_highlights.question: What were the e-waste and energy-upcharge costs for Q4 and FY26, and will they recur in FY27? Is channel inventory normalising to allow recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify the split. E-waste is provided at the highest rate under discussion with the ministry and recyclers; any rationalisation would be a benefit. The energy upcharge is a permanent BOM cost increase, and the next energy change is about three years away.

qa_highlights.question: What scenarios could play out with raw material, freight and regulatory cost increases: competitive rationalisation or consumer downtrading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said anything could happen and called it a roll of the dice. It is focused on component supply through the Strait of Hormuz, forex (imported content 20-35%) and pricing, and it will protect volume if it is materially outpriced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 AC revenue contribution, the aspiration, and the capital needed?
qa_highlights.answer: AC revenue is not disclosed; refrigerators are over 50% of revenue and washers 25-30%. The AC aim is strong but responsible growth, offtake-led, with no aspiration to be number one in AC for now.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash balance be used, and is a buyback planned?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said cash will go to innovation, automation, cost capex, backward integration and possible inorganic deals; there is no dividend or buyback plan at present. Management said buyback has not been looked at yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the three-to-five-year strategy, and why not a buyback despite the stock price?
qa_highlights.answer: The vision is to become the number one in refrigerators and washing machines in under 10 years, probably more than five. Management said it is focused on the next 12 to 24 months of investment and said executives bought shares personally.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the refrigerator industry stayed flat, and could BEE ratings help demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a K-curve with the entry segment (direct cool and semi-automatic) lagging. Replacement demand is being postponed. It said higher star ratings raise cost and price, so the effect on demand is complex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin outlook for Elica and the rest of the business, and what adjacency is being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Long term, high single-digit margins are likely for refrigerator, washing machine and AC businesses; Elica is held in double digits and its penetration is below 5%. Adjacencies must be synergistic on go-to-market and profitable, not low-margin.

500238|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 11.4% to a record INR 2,582 crore, with management citing record Faridabad output, completed sell-in/sell-out of the new-regulation refrigerator and AC range, and gains in premium categories. Profitability was squeezed: EBITDA was about INR 120 crore at 4.6%, down roughly 377 bps, as oil-linked inputs, a roughly 10% rupee depreciation to 95-96 per dollar, Haryana minimum wage revisions and an e-waste accounting charge were only partly recovered through price. Consolidated revenue rose 12.1% to about INR 2,727 crore with EBITDA at 5.1%. Management guided that July-September will be the weakest quarter and gave no full-year numbers.

500241|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn, but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 13.7% amid SPP UK service-mix shift and Rs 389 mn labour-code charge.
500241|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn with EBITDA of Rs 2.093 bn (14.8% margin) and PAT of Rs 1.121 bn. Full-year revenue was flat-to-marginally up at Rs 45.380 bn (+1%), with EBITDA of Rs 6.213 bn (13.7%) and PAT of Rs 3.772 bn. Domestic revenue fell 3% for FY26 while Q4 grew 3%; international grew 7% for the year and 25% in Q4. Management attributed the year's shortfall to JJM funding delays, a foundry ERP transition, and a Rs 389 mn labour-code charge classified as exceptional. Order books grew strongly: domestic Rs 24.680 bn (+30%) and international Rs 14.808 bn (+21%).

segments.name: Domestic (standalone)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 28.281 bn (-3%); Q4 Rs 9.091 bn (+3%). Order growth led by building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power and water; JJM is about 4-5% of revenue but hit water-sector shipments.

segments.name: International - SPP UK
segments.commentary: EBITDA fell from Rs 95 crore to Rs 58.1 crore (Rs 37 crore drop), driven by a shift from high-margin services to products as UK industrial customers idled on power prices above Rs 30/unit.

segments.name: International - SPP US
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 540 crore versus Rs 300 crore in FY22; about 35% from fire pumps and 25% from data centres. EBITDA down about Rs 3 crore per management.

segments.name: International - other entities
segments.commentary: Dutch, South African and other entities grew; South Africa margin % lower but absolute EBITDA higher. Management said Q4 was a slower first quarter for some entities due to prior-year spillover timing.

guidance_outlook: Management will strive for double-digit revenue growth in FY27 in both domestic and international businesses, but cited war and gas-supply risks.
SPP UK margins expected to realign toward the target level by roughly the calendar Q3 2026, with full-year margins targeted back to desired levels.
Labour-code impact of Rs 389 mn in FY26 (Rs 258 mn in Q4) treated as exceptional; estimates may be revised as rules are notified.
Final dividend of Rs 7 per Rs 2 share (350%) recommended, subject to AGM approval.
Management expects JJM-related disruption to ease over the next few quarters; AMP8 inquiries are expected to convert from next quarter.
capex_capacity: Foundry ERP (SAP) transition at Kirloskarvadi caused temporary disruption; management says the system has largely stabilised.
Company has five foundries; the largest was the focus this year, and in-house electricity capacity was added to hedge gas shortages.
Eight US data-centre packages were on the shop floor at the US plant as of the call.
Nuclear: full-scale primary heat transport pump prototype is to be delivered to NPCIL on schedule; budgetary quotes given for all pump types; Bharat SMR (200 MW) quotes sought.
demand_pricing: Standalone order inflow growth came from building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power (coal and nuclear), and water and irrigation.
Company says it earns premiums against multinationals on lifecycle cost and efficiency, and enforces advance payment or LC for small and medium pumps; retail sold on cash.
Management says it can pass on raw-material price rises; Hormuz-related disruption raised costs.

SPP US competes with Amstel, Taco, Grundfos and Xylem in data-centre cooling; management says it is not cheaper but offers plug-and-play containerised packages with 18-24 month data-centre lead times.
US distributors rose to about 46 from 12 four years ago; roughly 10 states have no coverage.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the strong standalone orders coming from, and what else is disrupting execution beyond JJM?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power and water. Execution was hit by the foundry ERP transition and JJM fund-release delays at the state level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international margins fall despite strong order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said the SPP UK mix shifted away from services because UK industrial customers idled on power prices above Rs 30/unit. Margins are expected to realign by about calendar Q3 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Would FY26 have grown at double digits without the disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Kirloskar said Q4 sales exceeded last year's Q4 and growth should resume, but war and gas uncertainty remain. He declined to give a precise FY27 figure beyond striving for double digits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear opportunity and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Company has indigenously designed primary-side pumps, with budgetary quotes given. Orders are expected step by step as NPCIL and DAE constraints clear; SMR prototype orders are expected once the design is finalised.

qa_highlights.question: How diversified is the US business, and what is the 3-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Fire is about 35% of US business and data centres about 25%; the rest is municipal and booster packages. Focus is HVAC, municipal markets and AMP8-style programmes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall across international entities in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said Q4 is seasonally slower for some entities due to prior-year spillover, and that year-on-year all entities except SPP UK improved.

risks_watch: SPP UK service mix and margin recovery timing (calendar Q3 2026 target).
JJM second-phase tendering and state-level fund release; no meaningful tendering pickup yet.
Geopolitical shocks (Middle East war, gas and fertiliser supply), with management citing cost pressure.
Foundry ERP stabilisation and dispatch conversion of the Rs 24.7 bn domestic order book.
Data-centre demand, where management acknowledged a mild US delay; ECA financing is a dependency.
Further labour-code revisions could change the Rs 389 mn exceptional charge.

500241|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million, but EBITDA grew only 2% at an 11.8% margin.

International revenue grew 19%, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.1% on lower high-margin services revenue at SPP UK and weak Rodelta execution. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 on both standalone and consolidated bases, while acknowledging that a large order slipped and foundry modernisation delayed some dispatches.

500241|2026-09.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to Rs12,767 million, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.3% and order intake jumped 68%.

The international (SPP UK, SPP USA, Dutch group) business grew 24% in revenue but EBITDA margin was only 5.3%, as UK service revenue lagged and oil and gas, a lower-margin segment, ramped up. Management guided to margin recovery in H2 and to double-digit standalone revenue growth for FY27.

500245|2026-03.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q4 FY26 PBT rose to INR514 crore from INR432 crore, with FY27 casting volume target of about 1.85 lakh tonnes.

FY27 overall sales volume growth of at least 15%, conditional on commodity prices not falling again.
Tube volume growth of 10-11% targeted in FY27 via debottlenecking; management expects about half of the 10% realisation drop (5-6%) to be recovered.
EBITDA margin expected to be just above 12.5%; management comfortable only at 15%.
Solar and wind power: about 35 MW solar and 25 MW wind to be commissioned June-September 2026; FY27 benefit about INR 45 crore, rising to about INR 90 crore at full run-rate.
Capex of about INR 600-700 crore per year, including about INR 500 crore for a bigger-diameter tube mill at Baramati (completion in about 1.5 years).
Oliver merger into KFIL targeted within a couple of months, to count for FY26.
capex_capacity: Solapur foundry running at about 4,200 t/month against a 6,000 t/month minimum expectation (about 70% utilisation); target about 5,000 t/month and 55,000-56,000 t sales in FY27.
Oliver Rajpura run rate about 1,700 t/month in Jan-Mar; target 2,000 t/month average and 24,000-25,000 t in FY27.
Sixth large-casting foundry being commissioned; seventh foundry planning started. Long-term feasibility up to 3 lakh t/year castings.
Baramati seamless tube capacity to rise from 2.30 lakh t to 4 lakh t by adding 1.5 lakh t; 1.5-year project for bigger tube mill.
Hiriyur blast furnace upgrade for about INR 125-150 crore to 2.5-3 lakh t/year; Koppal oxygen plant of 150 t/day by year end, with oxygen enrichment to 5% from 2.5% and PCI to 160-170 kg from 130 kg.
Jambunath Gudda iron ore mines, beneficiation and pellet plant planned; 52 MW waste-heat power in operation; Jejuri at about 30% green power.
demand_pricing: Pig iron prices up INR 5,000/t vs October and INR 4,000/t vs December (per management); international pig iron at about $475/t. Q4 realisation lagged due to order-book lag and some spill into January, with further price correction in April.
Casting realisation about INR 125/kg in base; management expects it to go beyond INR 130/kg within two years, with INR 10-12/kg of commodity-linked reductions expected to partly flow back.
Three new casting customers added in Q4 (diesel engine maker, tractor and earthmoving exporters); export share rose from 20% to 28% and CV share from 12% to 16% (per analyst's figures).
Oliver machining value expected to reach about INR 100 crore within a year, with 22 HMCs installed.
Cost pressures: rupee at about INR 95/$ and coal up about $25/t, which management expects to be partly passed on.
Tube NSR about INR 1,13,000/t at FY26 end; management expects tube prices to rise in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 casting target of 1.85-1.9 lakh t still achievable given slower ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 1,80,000-1,90,000 t as target, with about 1.05 lakh t from Koppal, 60,000 t from Solapur and 25,000 t from Oliver; the 45,000 t/quarter run rate expected within a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory and backward integration plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects just above 12.5% EBITDA, aims for 15% and cited coke self-sufficiency, 52 MW waste-heat power, Jambunath mines and pellet plant as backward integration steps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 pig iron price hikes lag and how will Q1 FY27 spreads move?
qa_highlights.answer: Lag came from 15-day order books and monthly commitments to regular customers; price increase effect partly in April. Management said pig iron price increase is inevitable but coal and coke costs are rising, and it is still assessing spreads.

qa_highlights.question: How much power cost saving from solar, wind and captive power?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar delivered about INR 70 crore benefit in FY26; wind and solar commissioning June-September should add about INR 45 crore in FY27, with INR 90 crore possible at full run-rate after new Maharashtra regulations.

qa_highlights.question: Tube business order book and ONGC orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the pending order figure; expects new tenders this year and better domestic and export oil and gas demand. Targets 10-11% volume growth in tubes.

qa_highlights.question: Tube capacity expansion and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Bigger tube mill at Baramati about INR 500 crore, within a 1.5-year completion; total capex about INR 600-700 crore per year, with borrowings reduced.

risks_watch: Casting ramp-up at Solapur (about 70% utilisation) and foundry-process complexity could delay the 1.85 lakh t FY27 target.
Pig iron pricing recovery depends on realisation after cost increases in coal and coke and rupee at about INR 95/$.
Hiriyur blast furnace output and Koppal productivity gains (oxygen, PCI) need to show in Q1 FY27.
Solar and wind commissioning timing (June-September) and new Maharashtra regulations on green power utilisation.
Oil and gas tube orders (including ONGC) remain unconfirmed; management had no current order book figure.

500245|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q1 FY27: castings sales up 18% to 41,345 t, tube sales down 14% to 41,512 t, and power and fuel costs rose about INR58 crore YoY.
500245|2026-06.overview: Pig iron and castings output rose in Q1 FY27, while tube output and sales fell on weaker high-value oil and gas and export orders. Power and fuel costs rose sharply, with about INR58 crore of the INR100 crore YoY jump in other expenses coming from power and fuel, half of it from rate increases. A change in green-power rules (8 hours instead of 17) and the end of power trading (about INR10 crore a year) cut the expected solar and wind savings to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore. Management guided to recovery in pricing and volumes from Q2, and said Q1 EBITDA margin was 12-13%.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs 132,392 t; management attributed to higher internal consumption
Company level; steel and tube margins cited at 14-17%

financial_highlights.metric: Power and fuel cost increase in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: INR58 crore of ~INR100 crore YoY jump
financial_highlights.change: About INR50 crore sequential jump in other expenses; about INR30 crore from rate increases

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,345 t, up 18% YoY; pricing passed through to customers, with further price increases still being concluded. Rajpura foundry is fully sold out at about 2,200 t per month.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,512 t, down 14% YoY, with a weaker product mix as more line pipe was sold in place of high-realising export and oil and gas tubes. Management is in a wait-and-watch stance due to Chinese dumping and subdued demand.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Realisation improved YoY and QoQ (about INR42,400/t vs INR39,000/t base, as cited on the call); about 30,000 t exported at slightly better than domestic prices. Pig iron EBITDA is expected to support the company margin.

segments.name: Steel (alloy)
segments.commentary: Management expects external sales of 100,000-110,000 t this year vs about 84,000 t, but cost pass-through is still under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Castings volumes expected to rise to about 162,000 t gross sales and then about 188,000 t, implying roughly 17-20% growth.
Overall volume growth of at least 15% across products in the remaining three quarters, with tube volumes up at least 10% YoY and steel external sales up more than 20%.
Pig iron output close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less.
Price-increase and cost pass-through benefits expected from Q2 and Q3 onward.

Medium term: about INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration with 300,000 t castings, 300,000 t casting sales and 400,000 t tube sales. Management said castings reach 270,000 t realisable capacity in this year plus two more years, with tubes at 350,000 t in 3-4 years.
Capex of INR600-700 crore this year, rising in the following years; about INR3,000-3,500 crore over the next four years.
capex_capacity: 35 MW solar plant in commissioning stage; 12 windmills of 2.1 MW each; both expected to be commissioned between June and September 2026.
Solapur two-part (no-bake) foundry, 15,000 t per annum, with commissioning expected by October 2026. Management said it has capacity of about 1,250 t per month.
Rajpura expansion: first phase to 40,000-50,000 t per annum within about 8 months; second phase to 70,000 t per annum. Total realisable castings capacity across six foundries is 270,000 t per annum.
Koppal oxygen plant and enhanced pulverised coal injection in blast furnaces 1 and 2, expected to complete by February-March 2027. Hiriyur pig iron upgrade to 360,000 t, taking about nine months.
Jejuri rolling capacity to rise from 15,000 t to 25,000 t per month (about 3 lakh t per annum), with about 240,000 t saleable; about 18-month timeline.

Premium couplings plant in Baramati, order expected within weeks. Koppal steel plant (about 2 years) and Baramati expander mill (2 years to build) are at early stages. Iron ore mines and pelletisation at Koppal are in progress.
One blast furnace to move to steelmaking, with government clearances in place; decision expected within 2-3 months, commissioning in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Castings demand described as strong across tractors, automobiles, earthmoving equipment and stationary engines; management expects realisation improvement.
Tube demand subdued by oil and gas slowdown and export disruption; Chinese dumping is pressuring pricing. Management expects the tube market to recover.
Coke dumping into India has reportedly eased, which supports domestic pig iron prices. Pig iron exports are running at about 30,000 t.
Fuel costs rose sharply: LPG cost in Solapur roughly doubled versus pre-war levels. Coking coal cost is expected to peak in June-August because of a three-month coal inventory.
Monthly pig iron sales plan of about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external); foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t of that.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal (Unique PMS): what drove the ~INR100 crore YoY and ~INR50 crore QoQ jump in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR58 crore of the increase is power and fuel, split roughly INR28-29 crore rate-driven and INR28 crore volume-driven, with Rajpura castings volumes and a full-month Jejuri run versus last year's shutdown. Power trading (about INR10 crore a year) has stopped and green power use is now limited to 8 hours instead of 17.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: does the regulation change hit the solar and wind savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, savings fall to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore, and payback stretches from 3 years to 3.6-3.7 years. Battery storage at MW scale is being examined, with some power expected through batteries shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: what is the INR350 crore contingent liability for forest development fee?
qa_highlights.answer: Karnataka levied forest development fees in 2016; the company won in the High Court, the state appealed to the Supreme Court, and the matter is sub judice after hearings with orders reserved. The company provides at 8% and discloses it as a contingent liability.

qa_highlights.question: Vipul Mody (individual investor): will the company move into subassemblies, machined components and high-end castings, and what is the status of 3D printing?
qa_highlights.answer: Machine shops at Koppal, Solapur and Rajpura already supply fully machined components, including a 6-cylinder head to an OEM. Maximum casting size after expansion is about 3 tons, the 2-part foundry is about 1,250 t per month, and the company is not yet in mining or wear-resistant parts. Prototyping is near serial production, with 50 cylinder blocks bought via the proto route.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): what is Q1 EBITDA margin and how will it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q1 company EBITDA at 12-13%, with steel and tube margins at 14-17% and pig iron weighing on the blend. Castings target about 15% plus or minus 1%, with pricing upside, and tubes are in a wait-and-watch phase due to Chinese dumping. Management expects company margin to improve on pig iron support and pass-through from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: what are current pig iron realisations and how much did raw-material costs absorb?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation moved from a base of about INR39,000/t to about INR42,400/t QoQ. Management said dollar rates and coal costs are pressuring costs, but realisation still improved slightly net of cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruvesh Kanakia (Antique): what volumes are expected for the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Pig iron close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less. Castings gross sales to rise from about 162,000 t to about 188,000 t (17-20% growth). Steel external sales of 100,000-110,000 t vs about 84,000 t, and tube volumes up at least 10%, with overall volume growth of at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Manish Goyal (Thinkwise): timeline for INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration, seventh foundry, and ONGC/OIL tube order execution?
qa_highlights.answer: Castings realisable capacity of 270,000 t is targeted in this year plus two years, with 300,000 t in 3-4 years; tubes to 350,000 t in 3-4 years after the expander mill (2 years to build); steel external sales of 240,000 t in about 2 years. Blast furnace 1 conversion to steelmaking is expected to be decided within 2-3 months, with commissioning in about 2 years. The 23,000 t tube order should complete in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi (Monarch): will coking coal costs rise further next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company holds about 3 months of coal stock, so the high-cost coal flows through June-August, which will be higher than April-June. Peaks may be partly mitigated as coal prices ease and blending improves.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi: is pig iron realisation a blend of foundry and steel grade, and what is capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly pig iron sales plan is about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external), a mix of grades with foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t. Capex is INR600-700 crore this year, rising in later years, with about INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years. Green power capex is set to slow, with battery storage starting at 50-70 MW.

qa_highlights.question: Anurag Patil (Quest): what is the net impact on annual power cost after solar, wind and power trading changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 70 MW solar to yield INR70-80 crore a year, the 35 MW solar about INR30 crore, and the windmills (equivalent to 55 MW) to add more, with the combined solar and wind benefit at about INR70-80 crore. Seasonal wind benefit is about 70% in June-September. Koppal is self-sufficient on waste-heat power, but Maharashtra fuel costs need a strategy and power trading is not likely to return without battery storage.

risks_watch: Power and fuel cost inflation: about INR58 crore of YoY increase, LPG in Solapur roughly doubled, and coking coal peaking June-August; watch whether castings and alloy steel price pass-through actually lands in Q2-Q3.

Tube volume recovery: tube sales down 14% YoY with a weaker mix; Chinese dumping and subdued oil and gas and export demand; the INR100 crore-ish order book from ONGC/OIL is expected to finish within two quarters.

Green power economics: regulatory limit cut from 17 to 8 hours, power trading (about INR10 crore a year) stopped, and solar and wind savings cut to about INR80 crore from about INR100 crore; payback moved to 3.6-3.7 years.

Execution of capex: INR600-700 crore this year against INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years; Solapur 2-part foundry by October 2026, solar and wind commissioning June-September 2026, Koppal oxygen and PCI by February-March 2027.
Pig iron pricing and exports: realisation up to about INR42,400/t from INR39,000/t; about 30,000 t exported; a dollar and coal cost squeeze could offset gains.
Contingent liability of about INR350 crore on Karnataka forest development fee, sub judice at the Supreme Court with no timeline.

I think we are on this direction though still the aggregates could be a little far away.
So I would say that I'm optimistic and we should look for improved performance in the coming quarters.
We can't push too much of line pipes into market.
There is a negative impact, but we continue to progress because still there is benefit.

500245|2026-09.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rs 2,057 crore, while PBT of Rs 138 crore was held back by tube margin pressure and casting rejections.
500245|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 topline was Rs 2,057 crore versus Rs 1,755 crore a year earlier (+16%), with PBT of Rs 138 crore against Rs 120 crore. Casting sales of Rs 633 crore (+30%) and pig iron of Rs 581 crore (+20%) led growth, while tubes grew only 0.5%. Realisations rose across pig iron (+12.4%), castings (+6.8%), steel (+7.6%) and tubes (+1.6%), though management said margins remain under pressure in castings and tubes. Management flagged a casting rejection problem at Solapur and an expected tractor-segment slowdown.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 120 crore a year earlier

financial_highlights.metric: H1 pig iron hot metal production

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 581 crore (+20% YoY); external pig iron volume about 1,34,000 t vs 1,28,000 t (+3.5%). One export cargo of 31,000 t was shipped at better realisation than domestic. Realisation Rs 43,054/t (+12.4%).

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 633 crore (+30%); gross casting sales crossed 50,000 t for the first time, net sales 47,888 t (+20%). Realisation Rs 1,30,000/t (+6.8%). Solapur about 15,000 t/quarter; Rajpura about 6,000 t+ in a quarter.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: External steel sales Rs 206 crore (+48% YoY); realisation Rs 77,500/t (+7.6%). Steel production H1 up about 14%.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales growth only 0.5% in value; volume 48,547 t (about -2%). Realisation +1.6%. Management said margins are under pressure, with Q1 volumes weak on delayed oil and gas projects.

guidance_outlook: Tube volumes targeted above 1,00,000 t in H2 FY27 to show growth over last year.
Casting net sales targeted to stabilise at about 1 lakh t in each of the next two quarters; management said casting capacity and rejections are being addressed to reach this level.
Solapur utilisation to rise to 6,000 t/month (18,000 t/quarter) across both foundries, with a 70,000 t/annum target for Solapur.
Pig iron domestic volume expected to be better than last year, at about 6.6-6.7 lakh t; oxygen enrichment and PCI at Koppal blast furnaces 1 and 2 due by year-end.
Medium-term target of 15% volume growth per year in castings; long-term pig iron sales target of 0.5 million t.
Machining value to cross Rs 100 crore annually within a year or two, with about 60% expected as contribution.
capex_capacity: Solapur second foundry line (two-part/no-bake, large castings up to 2 t): phase one and two nearly complete; commissioning expected by January 2027; total foundry capacity 15,000 t/annum (1,250 t/month).
Rajpura phase two targeted by March 2027 to take capacity to about 4,000 t/month; phase three needed for 70,000 t/annum; Rajpura stabilised at about 2,200 t/month with rejections falling.
Koppal alloy steel plant: technology partners engaged; equipment ordering and commercial negotiation under way; about 20 months execution after a 2-3 month start.
Jejuri rolling mill expansion, Baramati expander mill and Ahmednagar small piercing mills: execution stage; timelines not specified.
Machining capex about Rs 200 crore to date (per management correction from Rs 240 crore); annual machining value about Rs 50-60 crore (about Rs 5 crore/month).
Only 35 MW of wind power commissioned at Solapur; other windmills not yet commissioned.
Hiriyur mini-blast furnace upgrade planned; all three mini-blast furnaces together could give 8.5-9 lakh t of pig iron output before conversion to steel.
demand_pricing: Casting demand strong from automotive, earth-moving and stationary engine segments; foundries fully loaded in Q2 and October. Management flagged possible small corrections in tractor demand.
Casting contracts use a quarter-on-quarter price pass-through, so some further price increases are still to be realised.
Pig iron is priced on a monthly spot basis; coking coal is the main cost driver, while iron ore costs have been broadly stable.
Tube demand held back by delayed oil and gas projects; Chinese dumping expected to ease after anti-dumping duty was extended for five years; US exports hit by the war situation.
Pig iron exports were uneconomic for internal plants at current prices, per management; export opportunities will be taken only occasionally.
Rejections at Solapur about 10-11%, expected to fall to 7-8% next quarter; Rajpura rejections expected below 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Solapur phase two demand visible, and where is the Jejuri steel project and the Koppal alloy steel plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Solapur phase one and two are nearly complete and ramping up (about 15,000 t/quarter). Koppal alloy steel ordering is under way, with about 20 months of execution after a 2-3 month start. Jejuri and other projects have seen delays but are in execution.

qa_highlights.question: Why did casting margins contract despite higher volume and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited quarterly price pass-through lags, unfinished windmill commissioning, and productivity and quality work still needed. Further price realisation is expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Was pig iron export a conscious choice, and what is the domestic run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export cargo was a short window of better prices that also eased domestic pressure. Volume is expected to be about 6.6-6.7 lakh t, rising as Koppal oxygen enrichment and PCI are added.

qa_highlights.question: How much casting volume will the large-casting line add in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects no meaningful volume in FY27, with meaningful volume in FY28 as some parts move from makeshift arrangements to formal production.

qa_highlights.question: Why are tube volumes flat and margins down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was weak because oil and gas projects were delayed, and Q2 margins were still under pressure from low-priced orders. Realisation improvement is expected from new orders, with one large export consignment slipping into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is machining revenue low relative to investment?
