qa_highlights.question: Why valves margin fell to single digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales together, and called it temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order intake not improve materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard business growing but new-market entry takes time (fire-fighting, marine, mining); project market, especially oil and gas and petrochemical, slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard cycle is 24–36 months; deliveries to NPCIL around 48 months from order; management confirmed about 4 years from groundbreaking to first supply.

qa_highlights.question: BP&CL run-rate and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: On track but slow due to PSU referencing and tender requirements; medium-term potential INR 40–50 crore a year.

risks_watch: Nuclear: NPCIL test-bed issues delaying GHAVP testing, which could push back deliveries and revenue recognition.
Gross margin pressure from fixed-price project contracts and foundry cost pass-through lag of 3–6 months.
Export recovery depends on the Middle East situation and shipment clearances; export inventory still held at end-June.
Solar: KUSUM 2.0 delay; solar receivables and state-government payment cycle may keep receivable days elevated.
S/4HANA cost allocation from FY28 onwards; amount not yet quantified.
Q2 results should show whether H2 recovery materialises and whether valves margins return to double digits.
500249|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities but defensive on the weak H1; management repeatedly says it expects H2 to recover, with few hard numbers on timing or magnitude.
key_quotes: So, we are looking for a good outlook, not short-term, but long-term.

But we expect a much better half in the second half, because as of today, we see that the issues related to supply chain, of course, have not been fully solved, but it is much better that we have now a bit of consistency in the supply chain after having agreed with them on the revised prices.
Our goal is to have a double -digit growth. This is what we are aiming for.
So I see these as temporary variations.
So whatever you see investment of INR 80 crores, INR 100 crores, INR 120 crores annually, we intend to do that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterates 13-14% EBITDA margin and good double-digit valves margin, but valves fell to single digits in H1 and fixed-price project margins remain under pressure with foundry costs up 12-15% and pass-through lag of 3-6 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Shirwal nuclear capacity is at 80-90% utilisation and a new 7,000 sq m shed adds about 20% plant capacity, under construction, though no commissioning date was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 10-15% volume growth for FY27 but Q1 sales grew only 2-3% and H2 recovery rests on Middle East export shipments and supply stabilisation at 85-90%, with no quantified timeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at INR 80-120 crore a year, with Shirwal nuclear utilisation at 80-90%, but no new plant or board-level capex plan was announced on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 sales growth was 2-3% against a double-digit full-year goal, and management has offered few hard numbers on H2 recovery, so an upgrade looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 growth of 2-3% against a 10-15% volume goal, the NPCIL test-bed delay pushing GHAVP testing to September, and the KUSUM 2.0 delay (solar H1 revenue INR 50-60 crore) all put the double-digit target at risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Reciprocating pumps under BP&CL technology await EIL approval needing a running pump within 12 months, and a 10,000 cu m/hr split-case pump is under development, but no launch dates were given.

rows.label: Nuclear primary coolant pump tender (about eight reactors)
rows.why: A new tender for about eight reactors (Mahi Banswara, ASHVINI) is expected in a few months and KSB is the approved supplier, against an order on hand of INR 1,235 crore.

rows.label: Order book growth from H1 order intake
rows.why: H1 FY27 order intake was INR 15,307 mn (excl. Nuclear) and the order book reached INR 27,445 mn in June 2026, with management citing a 14% intake CAGR.

rows.label: Standard market price hikes being phased in
rows.why: Foundry costs are up 12-15% and KSB standard price hikes so far are single-digit and being phased in, with a 3-6 month pass-through lag.

tone.note: Management was confident on nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities and on the double-digit full-year goal, but defensive on the 2-3% Q1 sales growth and vague on H2 timing; analysts pushed on the valves margin drop and nuclear test-bed delays.

500249|2026-09.headline: KSB guides EBITDA at 13-14% and says fixed-price cost pressure eases by Q1 FY28, while nuclear NPCIL tender turns competitive.
500249|2026-09.overview: Management at the institutional investor meet (17 Nov 2026, Q2 FY27 context) said margins are under pressure from commodity inflation on fixed-price contracts, with Valves EBIT margin cited at 2.9% by an analyst. Nine-month revenue was stated as ₹20,647 million, and YTD September orders on hand were ₹28,599 million per the slides, while Q&A referred to ₹2,600-2,800 crore order book including nuclear. Management expects price recovery in standard business over 6-9 months and says cost pressure could last at most until Q1 FY28. Nuclear: first reactor coolant pump testing has teething problems, and the 500-hour test may slip beyond FY27; the new NPCIL tender (about 32 pumps, roughly ₹4,000 crore across three sites) is now competitive with relaxed qualification.

financial_highlights.metric: ROCE excluding labour code one-time impact (last year)
Valves segment EBIT margin (per analyst question)

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: EBIT margin cited at 2.9% by analyst; management attributes compression to product mix shifting to project orders and commodity costs, with no volume leverage this year.

segments.name: Pumps - Standard and project business
segments.commentary: Price increases in standard business take 6-9 months to recover; project business waits for the next contract. Management said the cost squeeze should be over by Q1 FY28 at the latest.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Two pumps delivered to NPCIL, testing ongoing with teething issues; first 500-hour test may not finish in FY27. Motors and some casings invoiced, but motors are traded at low margin. Management targets up to four pumps next year.

segments.name: SupremeServ (aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Revenue growing about 12-15%; pure spares and service are roughly 12-13% of total revenue, excluding replacement pumps.

segments.name: Water and building services
segments.commentary: Targeting minimum 15%, possibly 20%, YoY growth in water/wastewater and commercial building services; new entrant in water projects, targeting 5-7% share in 3-5 years.

guidance_outlook: Management maintains EBITDA target of 13-14% and says it will not go to 15-16% as it enters new segments with lower initial margins.
Expects margin recovery via aftermarket, exports and volume; says cost pressure on fixed-price contracts should last at most to Q1 FY28.
Targets exports at 15-20% of revenue.
Expects KUSUM 2.0 solar tender to start early next year after MNRE specifications are finalised next month.
Dangote refinery boiler feed pump orders of similar size to the fertiliser project (about ₹218 crore) expected to materialise this month, per management hope.
S/4HANA ERP go-live planned for February; foundry gas supply now about 85-90% back to normal.
capex_capacity: Nuclear reactor coolant pump: first pump 500-hour test may slip beyond FY27; final test leg targeted to start December and finish in the first quarter of next year.
Foundry (Vambori) gas supply disruption largely resolved; management says it is 85-90% back to earlier levels.
Shirwal energy pump factory and Shirwal expansion referenced in company history slides; no capex amount disclosed.
Mining entry supported by a newly qualified in-house foundry for exports.
demand_pricing: Order intake growing: Dangote fertiliser boiler feed pump order about ₹100 crore plus ₹118 crore; ONGC offshore pumps about ₹850 million (₹85 crore).

Supercritical thermal: JSW Salboni boiler feed pump order near finalisation; further L&T, Adani and BHEL/DVC boiler circulation pump opportunities. Management targets roughly 50% share in boiler feed pumps against Sulzer.

Nuclear NPCIL tender for about 32 reactor coolant pumps (around ₹4,000 crore across three sites) is now competitive with KSB, Kirloskar Brothers and Flowserve; qualification criteria relaxed; pre-bid meeting held next day.
Competitive intensity in India described as fierce; management says it expects to hold EBITDA margins and defend price in standard business.
Market share about 10-11% of an estimated ₹28,000-30,000 crore pump market; leader in energy, top two in industry.

qa_highlights.question: Chances and share in the new NPCIL reactor coolant pump tender, and whether margins will be lower.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment on pricing or margins because specifications and commercial terms have changed; it sees competitive bidding and believes KSB's chances are good as a proven supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Why Valves EBIT margin fell to 2.9%, and how price increases will be passed on.
qa_highlights.answer: Product mix shifted toward project orders and commodity costs hit margins; standard business price increases take 6-9 months to recover; management expects a return to normal levels with higher volume and better mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~₹2,400 crore order book is fixed-price and until when margin pressure lasts.
qa_highlights.answer: All non-nuclear orders are fixed-price; management expects cost pressure at most until Q1 FY28, passing through price increases in steps to smaller suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Testing status of nuclear pumps and whether FY guidance of two to three pumps holds.
qa_highlights.answer: Testing has teething issues in control valves, thermowell and power cable; a further two weeks is needed; the first pump's 500-hour test may slip past FY27; next year could see more than two pumps, with a target of four.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity versus Kirloskar Brothers, which reported margin expansion and share gains.
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the Indian market remains fiercely competitive; margins will be defended through aftermarket and exports, with EBITDA target kept at 13-14%.

qa_highlights.question: Market share and segment growth targets.
qa_highlights.answer: Overall share 10-11%; leads energy, top two in industry, top three to five in building services, mining and petrochemical. Targets at least 15%, possibly 20%, growth in water and building services, and growth above market in energy and industry.

risks_watch: Valves and pumps margin compression from commodity inflation on fixed-price contracts; recovery timing (Q1 FY28 at latest per management).
NPCIL nuclear testing delays and possible margin dilution in the new competitive tender; nuclear receivables and working capital.
Solar pump business slowdown for six to nine months awaiting KUSUM 2.0; management caps solar at about 10% of revenue for working capital reasons.
S/4HANA go-live in February could create process disruption; watch for execution issues.
Order intake breakup not disclosed in detail; nuclear vs non-nuclear order book split not provided numerically.
500249|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on long-term order intake and thermal, data centre and export growth, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, nuclear pricing and testing timelines, repeatedly saying it is too early to comment.
key_quotes: So that's why I'm not commenting too much on that.
So we, for sure know what our costs are, and we are confident that we should get a share out of this business.
So that way, we want to continue to maintain an EBITDA level of 13% to 14%. This is our goal.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA target held at 13-14% with no move to 15-16%; Valves EBIT margin cited at 2.9%, and fixed-price cost pressure is expected to last at most until Q1 FY28, with standard-business price increases taking 6-9 months to recover.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or line is firmly dated; nuclear pump output is tied to testing that may slip past FY27, and utilisation is only given as foundry gas supply back at 85-90%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order intake is growing (Dangote boiler feed pump about ₹218 crore, ONGC about ₹85 crore, JSW Salboni near finalisation) and water/building services is targeted at minimum 15%, possibly 20%, YoY growth, though no quarterly volume figure was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond the Shirwal references with no amount disclosed, and utilisation was not quoted as a percentage.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 13-14% EBITDA target and called the nuclear tender pricing too early to comment, with competitive bidding and a fierce Indian market.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Nuclear 500-hour test may slip beyond FY27 and the NPCIL tender (about 32 pumps, roughly ₹4,000 crore) is now competitive with relaxed qualification, so margin dilution is a risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is entering water projects (targeting 5-7% share in 3-5 years) and mining via a newly qualified in-house foundry for exports, but no dated product launch was given.

rows.label: NPCIL reactor coolant pump tender (~32 pumps, ~₹4,000 crore)
rows.why: The tender is now competitive with KSB, Kirloskar Brothers and Flowserve, and management believes its chances are good as a proven supplier, but pricing is unresolved and the nuclear pump test may slip.

rows.label: Standard-business price recovery
rows.why: Management expects price increases in standard business to recover in 6-9 months, and cost pressure on fixed-price contracts to last at most until Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Exports at 15-20% of revenue
rows.why: Management targets exports at 15-20% of revenue and cites exports as a margin-recovery lever, with exports growing 22% CAGR per slides, though no quarterly export figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term order intake, thermal and exports but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, nuclear pricing and testing timelines; analysts pressed on the Valves EBIT margin falling to 2.9% and on nuclear tender pricing.

500252|2026-03.headline: LMW Q4 FY26 revenue rose to ₹854 crore (vs ₹789 crore a year ago) and TMD order book reached ₹3,300 crore, with ~₹2,300 crore active.
500252|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue rose to ₹3,353 crore from ₹3,137 crore and consolidated profit to ₹195 crore from ₹151 crore, with standalone PBT up 42% to ₹221 crore. Q4 standalone revenue was ₹854 crore, up from ₹767 crore in Q3 and ₹789 crore a year ago. Management said textile machinery (TMD) order intake rose sharply in Q4 as cotton spinners' profitability improved, while the machine tool division grew strongly and ATC revenue reached ₹207 crore. Management flagged rising raw material, logistics and commodity costs across the industry, with no price hikes taken in MTD yet.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹767 crore in Q3 FY26 and ₹789 crore in Q4 FY25
vs ₹440 crore in Q3 and ₹493 crore in Q4 FY25
vs loss of ₹15.64 crore in FY25
one-time, related to new labour code and VRS outgo
vs ₹1,003 crore; ~10% foundry, balance machine tools
vs ₹146 crore; loss ₹32 crore vs profit ₹1.9 crore
vs ₹67 crore; breakeven vs loss ₹6.8 crore

segments.name: TMD (textile machinery)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹1,801 crore (down ~2%) and profit ₹9.75 crore; Q4 revenue ₹485 crore. Order book ₹3,300 crore (about ₹2,300 crore active), all booked in Q4. FY26 sales mix domestic:exports:spares 66:8:26.

segments.name: Machine tool division (MTD)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 25-28% in FY26 to ~₹1,205 crore for machine tools plus foundry (~10% foundry). Management cited ~11.5% margin in Q4 and no price hikes. Customer mix ~50-52% automotive, ~48% non-automotive; capacity headroom of ~20% and utilisation of 70-75%.

segments.name: ATC (aerospace and precision components)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹207 crore (vs ₹169 crore); Q4 revenue ~₹56 crore with segment result ~₹11 crore (close to 20% margin). Order book ~₹360 crore to be executed over 18 months. About 90% of sales are exports; mix is ~78% metallics and ~22% composites.

segments.name: LMW Global and LMW China
segments.commentary: LMW Global FY26 turnover ₹184 crore with ₹32 crore loss and ₹44 crore order book. LMW China FY26 turnover ₹130 crore, breakeven, and ₹120 crore order book.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a much larger offtake of textile machines as cotton spinners' margins improve, but said it is too early to call a hockey-stick recovery like FY22.
ATC capacity additions are expected to start yielding higher turnover in the second half of FY27.
Management expects MTD margins to continue as turnover grows, and said it will invest for growth once utilisation nears 90%.
Management plans a new, larger ATC facility outside the city centre; ATC capex of about ₹150 crore over five years was referenced for infrastructure only, excluding machinery.
Management aims to rebuild exports to about 23-25% of sales over the next three years, from ~8% in FY26 (per the sales mix).
capex_capacity: Textile machinery capacity utilisation is about 50-55%; machine tool utilisation is about 70-75%, with ~20% headroom in MTD even after Q4 shipments.
Capex of over ₹300 crore was spent in the last three years, mainly for machine tool capacity and modernisation; about 50% of FY26 capex went to ATC.
ATC composites utilisation is about 50%, with headroom to grow.
ATC capex is project-specific and tied to order wins; the new facility is planned to be larger than the current one.
The company is considering an investment of up to US$30 million via a UAE holding company, partly for working capital and partly for export growth (GCC presence for two years).
demand_pricing: Management said the textile industry has improved over the last two months, with good cotton yarn spreads, while crude-based synthetics face challenges. Demand is recovering from Bangladesh, China-linked yarn demand and Turkey.
TMD order book of ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4, versus the previous quarter's figure.
No price hikes taken in MTD; margin uplift attributed to operating leverage, with some forex income.
Raw material, logistics, steel, plastics and commodity costs are rising industry-wide; management did not disclose the size of planned price increases.
Import content in machine tools is about 50% of materials, mostly sourced locally in INR, with some USD-linked sourcing.
ATC is about 90% export-driven; customers are Tier-1 aerospace suppliers, and it also supplies ISRO, HAL and defence.

qa_highlights.question: What is the textile outlook and order pipeline, and the MTD growth and ATC order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Textile order book is ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4. MTD is continuing to grow with automotive at ~50-52%. ATC booked ₹195 crore; its order book of ~₹360 crore is to be executed over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is ATC's business, customer qualification cycle, and profit potential?
qa_highlights.answer: ATC has metallics and composites divisions covering engine parts, sheet metal, structures, assemblies and special processes. It is about 90% export-focused. Management said the ~19 certifications required include NADCAP, ISO and customer-specific ones. It does not disclose growth numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why invest up to US$30 million in a UAE holding company, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds are for working capital, which is under pressure because of geopolitics, and for export growth in GCC markets. It cited turning-centre exports of ~₹20 crore and a target of 23-25% exports over three years. No payback period was given.

qa_highlights.question: How can ROCE improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said textile machinery is cyclical with an ~8-year cycle and the business is at a low point. It said ATC has much better ROCE, MTD will improve, and capex is heavy in textile. Management said it will keep investing through downturns.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book 3,300 crore total with 2,300 crore active? What price hikes are needed to offset raw material costs, and what is the imported content?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: ₹3,300 crore total, ~₹2,300 crore active. Management would not share the size of price increases. Machine tool import content is about 50%, partly sourced locally in INR.

qa_highlights.question: Could ATC scale to ₹1,000 crore in five years, given a ~₹150 crore capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹150 crore figure covers infrastructure only, excluding machinery, and that the new facility could scale beyond ₹300 crore of revenue. It did not give a ₹1,000 crore target.

risks_watch: Volatile crude and geopolitics are hurting synthetic fibre producers and pressuring working capital; banks may limit funding.
Raw material and logistics costs are rising, and availability is a concern (e.g., LPG and some industrial gases); pricing pass-through is unclear.
ATC order book depends on long-term contracts subject to push-outs or pull-ins, and the business is working-capital intensive because raw materials are imported.
Textile recovery may be cyclical and not a sharp rebound; management has not committed to a timeline.
Export contribution fell to ~8% of sales in FY26, against a historical 23-25% target.
500252|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book, MTD margins and ATC growth, but cautious on textile recovery timing and evasive on pricing, customer names, ATC targets and payback. It described the textile cycle as still at a low point.
key_quotes: We have actually got a significant increase in order book compared to the last quarter.
Whether this again would be, you know, a hockey stick recovery kind of what we have seen in 21-22 that is too early to be mentioned.
So, what you're seeing is pure operational the margin which is coming through because of consistently doing upwards of 100 crores or 300 crores per quarter.
But customer names and the projects would be difficult.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: MTD margin was ~11.5% in Q4 and management expects margins to continue as turnover grows via operating leverage, with ATC at close to 20% segment margin, but rising raw material and logistics costs and no price hikes yet cap the upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ATC capacity additions are under construction and management expects them to yield higher turnover in the second half of FY27, with a new larger ATC facility outside the city centre planned, though its timing is not dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: TMD order book reached ₹3,300 crore (about ₹2,300 crore active), all booked in Q4, and management expects much larger textile machine offtake, while ATC order book of ~₹360 crore executes over 18 months; TMD FY26 revenue was down ~2% at ₹1,801 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Machine tool utilisation is only 70-75% with ~20% headroom and textile utilisation is 50-55%, so a near-term MTD capex is not required; however, ATC capex is ongoing (~50% of FY26 capex), a new larger ATC facility is planned, and a up to US$30 million UAE holding company investment is under consideration, so further capex announcements are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Textile order book of ₹3,300 crore and MTD growth of ~25-28% support an upside, but management called the textile recovery too early to call a hockey-stick and gave no FY27 revenue growth figure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rising raw material, logistics and steel costs with no price hikes taken in MTD, plus crude-linked pressure on synthetic fibre customers and tight working capital from geopolitics, could squeeze margins or push out orders.

rows.label: TMD order book ₹3,300 crore (~₹2,300 crore active)
rows.why: Order book of ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4, versus TMD Q4 revenue of ₹485 crore, so roughly 6-7 quarters of revenue at the current run-rate is visible.

rows.label: Export rebuild to 23-25% of sales
rows.why: Exports were ~8% of FY26 sales versus the 23-25% target, and the proposed US$30 million UAE holding company is aimed at GCC export growth, but no payback or timeline was given.

rows.label: New labour code and VRS one-offs
rows.why: Exceptional items of ~₹11.5 crore and ₹1.68 crore were booked in FY26 for the new labour code and VRS, so these are one-time and should not repeat.

tone.note: Management was confident on the ₹3,300 crore TMD order book, MTD margins and ATC growth, but cautious on the timing of textile recovery and evasive on pricing, ATC targets and UAE investment payback; analysts pushed on pricing pass-through and ATC scale.

500252|2026-06.headline: LMW Q1 FY27 revenue flat QoQ at ₹891 cr (+24% YoY); PBT ₹85 cr, with TMD order book at ₹3,200 cr and ATC order book near ₹1,000 cr.
500252|2026-06.overview: Consolidated-level revenue was broadly flat sequentially at ₹891 cr against ₹889 cr in Q4 FY26 and up 24% YoY from ₹722 cr. PBT rose to ₹85 cr, up 18% QoQ and about 151% YoY from ₹34 cr. TMD revenue was ₹482 cr, roughly flat QoQ and up 16% YoY, while the TMD operating margin fell sequentially on lower turnover, which management attributed to volume and to rupee and commodity cost pressure. ATC revenue rose to ₹60 cr and margins improved, partly due to forex. LMW Global and LMW China losses narrowed QoQ, and China turnover fell sharply YoY.

financial_highlights.change: +24% YoY; flat vs ₹889 cr in Q4 FY26
+16% YoY (vs ₹415 cr); vs ₹485 cr in Q4 FY26

vs ₹57 cr in Q4 FY26; vs ₹46 cr in Q1 FY26

segments.name: TMD (Textile Machinery Division)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹482 cr; order book ₹3,200 cr of which ~₹2,400 cr active; mix 64% domestic, 10% export, 26% spares. Capacity utilisation ~75-80%, though a later answer put textile utilisation at ~60%.

segments.name: Machine Tool Division (MTD) and Foundry
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹343 cr, with Foundry ~8% of the total. Automotive ~56% of MTD revenue. Management said MTD operating margin fell on lower turnover, and capacity can grow about 15-20% without major capex.

segments.name: ATC (Air Texturing/Composite-related)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹60 cr, ~90% export. Order book ~₹1,000 cr for execution over 3 to 3.5 years, with composite ~20% of turnover and ~25% of the order book. Margin improved, partly on forex and a higher assemblies mix.

segments.name: LMW Global (Dubai) and LMW China
segments.commentary: Global turnover ₹51 cr with ₹22 cr order book and ₹5.6 cr loss. China turnover ₹11 cr (vs ₹76 cr YoY) with ₹128 cr order book and ₹7 cr loss.

guidance_outlook: Management expects gradual, not sharp, recovery in spindle absorption. State policies (Gujarat, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh) and FTAs are cited as demand triggers.
Raw material and logistics costs are up about 3-3.5% per management, and supply-chain availability has eased but is still monitored for 4-5 months of pipeline cover.
ATC needs ~₹150 cr of new land and building capex, with a 18-24 month timeline.
MTD margin recovery depends on turnover growth and capacity utilisation; no timeline was given. Management also flagged price revisions and India-sourced substitutes for imported parts.
Auto-winder product: orders expected to be booked around the last quarter of this year.
capex_capacity: ATC: ~₹150 cr for new land and building under an MoU; 18-24 month build timeline.
MTD capacity utilisation ~75-80%; capacity can add ~15-20% without new capex, with further capex needed beyond that.
Textile machinery utilisation ~60% per a later answer.
Factory ownership: the land for the ATC facility is owned by the company, per management.
demand_pricing: TMD order book ₹3,200 cr (active ~₹2,400 cr). Order book is secured by a 10% customer deposit, and delivery lead times have shrunk from 14-15 months to much shorter.
Order mix is ~70% projects and ~30% unitary machines, against a typical 60:40 in good years.
Export orders for ATC ~₹900-1,000 cr over 3-3.5 years; ~₹150 cr of Global/China export orders are LC-backed and short cycle.
ATC order book is ~25% composite and ~75% metallics. Composite share is expected to build as exports rise.
MTD order book is short-cycle (under 3 months) and cash-backed, so it is not in the headline order book.
Management cited steep order inflow in the last quarter (Q4 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for expansion into six new divisions, including pharma and specialty chemicals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an enabling board resolution covering multiple options (including EV and an advanced technology centre). Nothing is decided yet. Significant decisions will be disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How secure is the TMD order book and what is the domestic visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹3,200 cr is secured through 10% deposits. Demand is recovering gradually, with state policies and FTAs as triggers. Cotton spinning margins are good, while synthetics are under strain.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the order book by customer type and project versus unitary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose customer-level detail. The order mix is about 70% projects and 30% unitary machines, against 60:40 in good years.

qa_highlights.question: ATC capacity expansion, margin outlook, and whether forex helped?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~₹150 cr land and building plan is due over 18-24 months. Q1 margin was higher on mix (more assemblies). Forex was a positive, with the ATC margin range at 94-96% after a jump from 85 to 95 last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of USD and EUR appreciation on MTD costs and mitigation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the currency impact is real on MTD and textile costs. Mitigation includes India-sourced parts and price revisions, and ATC and foundry have contractual price-revision clauses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only ~4% YoY while revenue grew ~25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ongoing cost optimisation and a VRS cost booked in the last quarter, with a tight cost belt maintained as ATC, MTD and textile pick up.

qa_highlights.question: Path back to 12-14% MTD EBIT margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Requires turnover growth and higher utilisation on a much larger cost base; no timeline was given.

500252|2026-09.headline: LMW Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 30% to ₹1,153 crore and PBT reached ₹204 crore, with TMD order book near ₹3,400 crore.

PBT was ₹204 crore against ₹93 crore in the prior-year period. Textile Machinery Division (TMD) grew 38% YoY in Q2 to ₹639 crore, while the Machine Tool Division and Foundry H1 turnover rose to ₹794 crore from ₹555 crore. Management was cautious on textile demand because of input cost inflation and supply chain issues, and more positive on machine tools and ATC.

segments.commentary: H1 turnover ₹794 crore, of which Foundry is 9%. Utilisation 75-80%. Management expects around 50% growth this year and says it is adding capacity.

segments.commentary: H1 turnover ₹135 crore (+39%). Utilisation about 70%. Order book about ₹1,000 crore, roughly 70% metallics and 30% composites. Segment margin cited at about 22%.

segments.commentary: LMW Global H1 turnover ₹100 crore with order book about ₹163 crore; LMW China H1 turnover ₹36 crore with order book about ₹128 crore. Management cited a loss in the overseas holding last year (about ₹29.5 crore at LMW Global per annual report, which management did not directly confirm).

Capex for the year is planned to be broadly in line with depreciation, with some assets to come in on lease.
ATC: the ₹150 crore investment is planned under a Tamil Nadu government MoU, but there is no commissioning timeline yet.

Management said it will take only orders it can execute, adding capacity to match, because contracts carry penalty clauses.

MTD mix: about 76% turning centres and 23-24% machining centres; machining centres are growing faster.

TMD is on fixed-price contracts with no current price pass-through, though a price discussion is active and VAVE cost programmes are under way.
TMD order book about ₹3,400 crore; net order inflow up about ₹200 crore in the quarter; about 70% of orders are project orders.
MTD: order inflow is consistent. Demand is driven by China+1 and machine upgrades. Auto is still a little over 50% of MTD sales, with defence, EMS and tooling expanding.
Indian machine tool market about 17,000-18,000 machines and about $2-2.5 billion by value. Imports are about 40-45% by volume and 50-55% by value, and are declining as domestic makers grow.
Lakshmi Auto Winder: launched and sold to a few southern customers, with ramp-up expected next year. Market is roughly ₹1,500 crore-plus, since winding is about 25-30% of spinning mill capex.
Management said export markets like Bangladesh and Turkey are challenged, and overseas losses reflect low topline. ATC is 90% export historically; domestic defence is now being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: ATC capacity, peak revenue from current and planned capex, and commissioning timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 70%. The asset-turn rule of thumb is 1:1 to 1.3. No timeline has been given for the new investment, which will be announced at an appropriate time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for TMD EBITDA margin, given the textile tailwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tailwind is more apt for MTD. TMD is cautious because of cost inflation and supply chain issues. There is no price pass-through yet, and VAVE is under way.

qa_highlights.question: MTD capacity expansion of only 10% when demand grows about 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: The expansion is a repurposed unit and is statutory filing-driven, not a calibrated expansion. Management said it will keep adding capacity at 80-85% utilisation, and that the ₹10 crore figure understates the ecosystem.

qa_highlights.question: Overseas losses and LMW Holding investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas losses reflect weak topline in Bangladesh and Turkey, plus high-cost locations. qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name specific programmes. It said it covers structures, assemblies, special processes and machining, but not electronics. Management said it is not into forging.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cost control, digitisation and automation, and VAVE for better COGS. Capex will be broadly in line with depreciation, with some leased assets.

500257|2026-03.headline: Lupin Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% YoY to Rs 7,475 crore and EBITDA 68% to Rs 2,171 crore; FY27 guided to high-single-digit growth and ~25% margin.
500257|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the 15th consecutive quarter of YoY growth, with record sales and profitability; EBITDA margin was 29.4% (ex forex and other income), up 620 bps YoY. FY26 revenue rose 23% to Rs 27,958 crore and EBITDA reached Rs 8,160 crore at a 29.7% margin, above the 27-28% guidance. Q4 EBITDA moved down QoQ, which management attributed to the Mirabegron settlement payment to Astellas, forex and higher manpower cost booked in other expenses. Management guided FY27 to high-single-digit revenue growth (in rupee terms) and around 25% EBITDA margin, citing Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition, higher R&D (~8% of sales) and a 25-26% ETR.

segments.commentary: Europe, Canada and Australia: Q4 Rs 845 crore (+7.1%, 12% of sales); FY26 Rs 3,244 crore (+13.3%, 11% of sales). European sales passed USD 200 million; VISUfarma acquisition to be consolidated from FY27 Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance (high-single-digit growth, ~25% margin) factoring in Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, both Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition is factored in; the margin decline is attributed to these competitors and higher R&D.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher manpower cost, the Mirabegron settlement payment to Astellas booked in other expenses, and forex; the impact was in other expenses, not the US business itself.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US revenue outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 US revenue should be above USD 1 billion, with high-single-digit to low-double-digit erosion in base case, offset by launches; FY28 was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Mirabegron settlement affect margins going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Part is a variable per-unit cost in gross margin and part is a USD 75 million amortisation over about two years; the split depends on sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Ranibizumab and Pegfilgrastim?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranibizumab to launch later in FY27 with both pre-filled syringe and vial; Pegfilgrastim on-body filing this year with FY28 or FY29 launch; Pegfilgrastim partnered with Valorum.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biosimilar pricing outlook as more entrants arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management focuses on first-wave or limited-competitor products; it expects new entrants to help overall biosimilar economics rather than erode them further.

qa_highlights.question: How is Semaglutide launch in India tracking?
qa_highlights.answer: Early but solid; ranked number 2 generic and number 3 overall after about nine days, with April data pending; the company aims to be a top-3 generic player.

500257|2026-06.headline: Lupin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 8,277 crore and EBITDA hit INR 2,464 crore (30% margin), but management guided to a sharper US slowdown ahead.
500257|2026-06.overview: Lupin reported a record quarter with revenue from operations of INR 8,277 crore (up 32% YoY) and EBITDA excluding forex and other income of INR 2,464 crore (up 50% YoY, 30% margin, up 340 bps). Growth was broad-based across the US, India, Other Developed Markets, Emerging Markets and GIB, with ex-US organic growth above 20%. Net cash fell to INR 2,831 crore from INR 4,636 crore after the VISUfarma acquisition closed.

segments.commentary: Sales of INR 2,380 crore, up 13.9% YoY; diabetes grew 31.8% (1.8x category) and cardiac 1.2x category, while respiratory grew 6.9% vs category 11.3%. Chronic share rose to about 67% from about 65% in FY26; volume growth was 6.1%.

segments.commentary: Sales of INR 1,149 crore, up 48% YoY, with Europe up 83% YoY. VISUfarma consolidation began this quarter. Management guides 10-20% growth over the next couple of years.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 990 crore, up 52% YoY. Brazil grew 117% YoY in local currency on Dapagliflozin and Empagliflozin launches.

segments.name: GIB

500257|2026-09.headline: Lupin Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR 7,827 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 25.1% (from 31.3%) as US Tolvaptan competition intensified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Tolvaptan exit share and how many more entrants are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Lupin held about 50% share as sole generic in recent months; a couple more entrants are possible. Management expects pricing pressure to cut margin and revenue contribution significantly.

qa_highlights.question: Will Apixaban need investment before launch, and can it hold share after generics arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, extra commercial investment is planned over the next couple of quarters for market access and channel relationships. Management expects some share retention in liquid-dosage segments and a longer window than exclusive generics.

qa_highlights.question: What drives India growth acceleration in H2 given H1 at about 1.1x IPM?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Gupta said H1 was 16% ahead of market but short of the 20-30% target; respiratory inhaler slowdown is expected to ease in H2, and cardiac should recover.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 US revenue match FY27 and does it include Apixaban?

qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Swaminathan said 29-30% is possible by FY29-30 as 505(b)(2), biosimilar and specialty products scale, with FY28 a consolidation year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management would keep debt within twice EBITDA, about INR 16,000-17,000 crore of debt capacity plus INR 3,000-4,000 crore of balance-sheet cash, so up to about INR 20,000 crore. Priorities are specialty in Europe and US, and India at an appropriate cost.

500265|2026-09.headline: Maharashtra Seamless Q2 FY27: seamless EBITDA/ton fell to INR9,220 (Q1: INR15,660), which management attributes to a notional inventory-valuation hit.
500265|2026-09.overview: Management said Q2 margins were depressed by a notional Ind AS inventory-valuation adjustment, as steel billet prices fell below procurement cost on inventory held at 30 September 2026. Order book rose from INR1,700 crores (31 July) to INR2,200 crores, with execution lead time of 2 to 4 months. H1 seamless dispatches were around 200,000 tons, and management reiterated the 430,000-ton seamless FY27 target, requiring about 230,000 tons in H2. Other income was nil as treasury equity and gold/silver exposures marked down. Management also outlined a three-way demerger of the seamless business and a registered office shift to Gurgaon, with approvals expected by January-February 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did seamless EBITDA per ton fall to INR9,220 in Q2, and what is the underlying trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is an inventory-valuation effect under Ind AS, which is notional. Inventory rose by more than INR500 crores as the order book grew, and September prices were below procurement cost. Underlying EBITDA per ton is better than Q1's INR15,660, and margins should recover once the inventory is dispatched.

500280|2026-03.headline: Century Enka Q4 FY26 operating revenue Rs 484 crore (+9% YoY) with EBITDA margin up 948 bps YoY to 11.46%, aided by price pass-through and some low-cost inventory.
500280|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp YoY profit recovery: volume grew 14% YoY to 20,711 MT and EBITDA rose to Rs 55 crore, with price increases passed through after the Iran-related raw material spike from March. For FY26, revenue fell 15% to Rs 1,705 crore on 6% lower volume, but EBITDA (+29%) and PAT (+52%) improved. Management said the company has raised its indicative operating margin band to 7-10% from 6-8%, though it declined to guide quarterly numbers. Management indicated part of the gain came from consumption of lower-priced raw material, which will fade, and said the Rs 100 crore FY27 capex and renewable power additions will help margins only from H2.

rows.why: Performance is tied to client funding, approvals and right-of-way; receivables of INR 1,043 crore (UP JJM), INR 180 crore (Mission Bhagiratha, sub judice) and BharatNet cable-price pressure are the named risks, and Q1 consolidated PAT was flat at INR 216 crore vs 192 crore.

rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed in the call.

rows.label: Unbilled revenue conversion into billing
rows.why: About INR 780-800 crore of the INR 7,414 crore unbilled revenue was certified in early July, and management expects unbilled to smooth over two quarters, though conversion moves revenue from unbilled to billed rather than into the revenue line.

rows.label: Smart-meter capex completion and debt
rows.why: Cumulative smart-meter debt is INR 1,461 crore and consolidated net debt is INR 3,513 crore vs INR 1,574 crore a year ago; standalone debt is guided flat at INR 2,250-2,400 crore depending on collections, and no further equity is needed on about INR 460 crore invested.

rows.label: Q1 order inflows convert to turnover from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Q1 inflows were INR 3,889 crore and July inflows took the total to INR 4,542 crore, with management guiding that these orders contribute from Q3 FY27 onward against the INR 22,000-25,000 crore FY27 inflow guide.

500294|2026-09.headline: NCC Q2 FY27 consol turnover rose 32% to INR6,042 crore, with FY27 guidance of 8-10% growth retained.
500294|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 turnover grew 32% YoY to INR6,042 crore, the highest-ever Q2 revenue on a consol basis, and H1 turnover rose 21% to INR11,884 crore. Consol EBITDA margin was 8.79% in Q2 (8.66% a year earlier) and 9.1% for H1. Order book stood at INR80,167 crore at 30 September, up 11% YoY, with INR4,838 crore booked in the quarter and INR2,381 crore more in October. Management retained FY27 guidance (revenue growth 8-10%, EBITDA margin 8.5-9%, order inflow INR22,000-25,000 crore) but did not explain why H2 growth would slow, which drew sustained analyst questioning. Working capital eased, receivable days fell to 53 and JJM outstandings declined, while consolidated net debt rose to INR3,887 crore.

Standalone order book INR71,293 crore; subsidiaries INR8,874 crore (mining 5,923, transportation 2,431, smart meters 520).

FY27 capex to be about INR500 crore; INR253 crore spent in H1, so about INR250 crore in H2. FY28 capex expected to be similar, driven by the Amrapali mining project in Jharkhand.

Retention of Ken-Betwa contract value is about INR3,389 crore per NCC's share, with unbilled revenue to be recognised as work progresses.

Smart meter installation about 51% complete, 49% outstanding.

Bid pipeline unchanged at about INR2.5 lakh crore as shared in May; no segment-wise breakup given.
Retention money at INR2,547 crore (up about INR150 crore QoQ); contract retention 5%, up to 20% in some electrical contracts; can be partly replaced by bank guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Why retain 8-10% FY27 growth after 21% H1 growth, implying a sharp H2 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is for the full year, H1 was strong on mining and other projects, and Q3 is too early to comment; guidance was retained.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retention money high relative to revenue, and can it be released?
qa_highlights.answer: Newer contracts carry 5% retention, some electrical contracts up to 20%, and CC road contracts in Mumbai high; retention will persist, with partial bank guarantee substitution possible on some contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the JJM payment improvement sustainable, and what is the outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: JJM outstanding is INR2,246 crore; INR1,720 crore received in H1; JJM backlog excluding O&M is about INR5,412 crore, with UP legacy work largely done by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the unbilled revenue level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift to EPC milestone billing and BharatNet and AP Capital City work drive unbilled; it is expected to remain at a similar level and to be realised progressively.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance for order inflow achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inflow of INR11,108 crore including October is about 50% of the lower band; management retained the INR22,000-25,000 crore guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Hyderabad investment of INR107-108 crore under construction?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an investment in a stalled Hyderabad project under NCLT and RERA proceedings; management said it is fully secured and not at risk of non-recovery, though timing is uncertain.

Depreciation and finance cost trajectory as the TBM and mining projects enter service.

rows.why: Order book of INR80,167 crore (up 11% YoY) and Q2 consol turnover up 32% to INR6,042 crore support volumes, but guidance implies a sharp H2 slowdown and order inflow of INR11,108 crore is about 50% of the lower band.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, so there is no utilisation-based trigger, and management only signalled FY28 capex similar to FY27 (about INR500 crore) driven by Amrapali mining, which is already committed rather than a new announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of 8-10% revenue growth was retained, and order inflow of INR11,108 crore is only about 50% of the lower band of INR22,000-25,000 crore, so there is no basis for a raise.

rows.why: H1 revenue grew 21% against full-year guidance of 8-10%, implying H2 growth near zero or negative, yet management declined to explain the slowdown and order inflow is about 50% of the lower band, so a cut is a real risk.

rows.label: Receivable days fall and JJM outstanding declines
rows.why: Trade receivables fell to INR2,697 crore (53 days) from INR3,055 crore (68 days) in Q1, and JJM outstanding is INR2,246 crore with INR1,720 crore received in H1, though retention money at INR2,547 crore keeps working capital at 96 days.

rows.label: Order inflow to reach guidance
rows.why: Inflow of INR11,108 crore including October is about 50% of the lower band of INR22,000-25,000 crore, with half the year gone, so the guidance looks hard to meet.

rows.why: Consol net debt rose to INR3,887 crore from INR3,513 crore at Q1 and INR2,643 crore a year earlier, with finance cost steady at about INR166 crore a quarter, so debt reduction is not signalled.

500300|2026-03.headline: Grasim Q4 FY26: Birla Opus revenue up 52% YoY like-to-like, Pivot revenue more than doubled; paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27 on crude-linked input cost spike.
500300|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a record year, with consolidated revenue of INR1,75,431 crores and standalone revenue of INR41,039 crores. Birla Opus grew 52% YoY like-to-like in Q4 and crossed 10% revenue market share in March 2026 on its own, while Birla Pivot's Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY and is close to its INR8,500 crore annual guidance. Raw material costs linked to crude derivatives rose sharply, with management citing up to 20-25% of COGS, prompting two further paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27. Cellulosic fibre and cement (UltraTech) contributed strong profit growth, and Grasim announced a INR10 final dividend.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 revenue roughly doubled vs FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Caustic soda sales volume Q4 FY26

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Q4 like-to-like revenue +52% YoY; revenue market share up ~90 bps QoQ and 370 bps in FY26, now No.3 in organised decorative paints and crossed 10% share in March 2026. Installed capacity 1,332 MLPA (24% of industry); Kharagpur plant commercialised in Q3 FY26. Network at 11,500 towns, 50,000+ dealers, 1,200+ franchise stores; 218 products.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY; close to INR8,500 crore annual revenue guidance. Delivers to 5,000+ pin codes across 400+ cities. Management targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27, possibly sooner.

segments.name: UltraTech (cement, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Crossed 200 MTPA grey capacity in April 2026, targeting 240+ MTPA by March 2028. UltraTech declared INR240 per share dividend, implying about INR4,000 crore cash inflow to Grasim before tax.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR4,614 crores (+14% YoY), EBITDA INR588 crores. Harihar Lyocell Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa under way within a total 110,000 tpa expansion. China operating rates at 92% in Q4 versus 87% a year ago.

segments.name: Chemicals (CFI)
segments.commentary: Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA moving to 1,530 KTPA. Specialty chemicals revenue +5% YoY, but higher ECH input prices hit profitability. Specialty chemicals 27% and chlorine derivatives 22% of revenue mix.

segments.commentary: Board approved a INR4,000 crore preferential equity raise; Grasim to invest INR2,880 crores to keep its 52.3% fully diluted stake.

segments.commentary: Porcelain capacity held flat with productivity focus only; polymer long rods sold out after recent expansion; hollow composite expansion being evaluated. Sales and EBITDA no longer disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects industry paint growth to move from single-digit to double-digit in FY27, with Birla Opus targeting high double-digit growth.

Birla Opus priorities in order: become No.2 decorative paints player, reach INR10,000 crore revenue in the third year of full-scale operations (FY26 treated as year one), then profitability. Paint EBITDA losses to narrow quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year.
Birla Opus dealer network to exceed 15,000 towns by end of FY27 from 11,500 currently.
Birla Pivot targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27.

Capex guidance for FY27 to be shared next quarter.
Grasim intends to keep above 50% stake in UltraTech and Aditya Birla Capital (current position, not a long-term policy).

Harihar Lyocell: Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa in progress, total 110,000 tpa expansion; Phase 2 to be announced.
Birla Opus Kharagpur (sixth plant) commercialised Q3 FY26; average distance travelled per product down over 30%.
Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA to 1,530 KTPA; additional capacity under evaluation.

Paints: input costs rose to as high as 20-25% of COGS due to crude-linked raw materials, packaging and rupee depreciation; management says raw material prices remain unstable.
Paints: 10% free-paint consumer scheme continues despite price hikes; institutional channel grew 43% QoQ and 212% YoY, with a pipeline of 45,000 sites.
Paints premium and luxury products at 65% of value; 75% of products rated No.1 in blind tests by applicators (company claim).

qa_highlights.question: How much growth in paints will come from distribution expansion and tinting machines versus throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth from both numerical dealer expansion (11,500 towns to 15,000+) and throughput gains by adding product ranges to existing dealers. Older dealers over 18 months show 25-50% higher counter share and throughput comparable to legacy players.

qa_highlights.question: Is paint profitability improving from scale, and is FY26 the first full year for the INR10,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY26 as the first full operating year internally. Fixed costs (sales and service force, brand spend) were front-loaded and should be covered by growth; variable-cost levers include better procurement, plant and logistics optimisation, and adding second and third raw material suppliers. Paint contribution improved significantly in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How close is Birla Opus to the No.2 position in decorative paints?
qa_highlights.answer: Birla Opus plus Birla White putty is roughly at the level of the current No.2 on a decorative-only basis for Q4 FY26. The ambition is for Birla Opus alone to become No.2 in decorative paints, excluding industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Dealer throughput versus industry benchmarks?
qa_highlights.answer: Throughput is in line with market presence across A/B/C/D dealer classes. Top dealers stock 2-2.5x the bottom dealer and generate 4-5x its throughput. The market leader is estimated to have 20-25% more dealers and a richer A-class mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan after the UltraTech dividend, given about INR2,900 crores for ABC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the INR2,900 crore use (ABC stake maintenance) as a one-off for FY26. Cash is being used for Grasim's dividend, maintaining the ABC stake, and supporting the two new businesses. Capex guidance for FY27 will come next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Pivot profitability path and when will segment disclosure start?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot aims to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even and may get there sooner. Paints EBITDA losses are on a glide path to narrow each quarter. Management said segment reporting for paints and Pivot would start shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Will paint EBITDA losses (about INR300 crores per quarter) come down materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered 'Yes, it will come down' without quantifying the timing.

qa_highlights.question: Insulator capacity, sales and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Porcelain capacity is flat, with productivity focus; polymer long rods are sold out after expansion; hollow composite expansion is being evaluated. Insulator sales and EBITDA are no longer disclosed.

FY27 capex guidance is pending and will be shared next quarter; capital allocation (dividend, ABC stake maintenance, support for new businesses) was described as a one-off for FY26, not a long-term policy.

This VUCA situation makes demand forecasting difficult and we need to closely monitor the situation as impact of price rise will slowly be felt by consumers and contractors in second half of quarter one and entire quarter two FY '27.

500300|2026-06.headline: Grasim Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR48,716 crore, up 21% YoY, with standalone EBITDA more than doubling to INR1,094 crore.
500300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record INR48,716 crore (up 21% YoY), the 24th consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Standalone revenue rose 28% to INR11,795 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 107% to INR1,094 crore. Birla Opus revenue grew 64% YoY to INR1,661 crore after an 8.8% cumulative price increase to offset a raw material cost shock, and Birla Pivot grew 75% to INR2,548 crore. Management also disclosed a new 0.25% of standalone revenue brand royalty payable to Birla Holdings from June 2026, and a planned Renewables equity infusion below INR1,000 crore in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated net debt to TTM EBITDA

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,661 crore (+64% YoY, +17% QoQ); market share up 30 bps QoQ to a number-three position, with 8.8% cumulative price increase in Q1. Premium and luxury portfolio is about 65% of sales value; institutional sales up 85% YoY.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,548 crore (+75% YoY), annualised run rate above INR10,000 crore. Management reiterated EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27; private labels more than doubled YoY off a low base.

segments.name: Cellulosic fibres (VSF/CSF)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,530 crore (+12% YoY) on volumes down 4% YoY; specialty fibre rose to 27% of sales mix from 21%. EBITDA roughly doubled, helped by a low base and specialty mix.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,640 crore (+10% YoY); ECU realisation INR37,955/t (+6% YoY); caustic share of revenue fell to 49% and specialty chemicals rose to 30%. EBITDA INR491 crore (+16%). Volumes softer on plant maintenance.

segments.commentary: Sales volume 41.31 Mt (+12% YoY); gray capacity 205.5 Mt after adding 8.7 Mt in the quarter; EBITDA INR5,146 crore (+12%). Green power mix 45.6%; 5,802 retail outlets.

segments.commentary: Lending portfolio grew 32% to nearly INR2,20,000 crore; housing finance crossed INR50,000 crore (+50%). Grasim invested INR2,880 crore at INR356/share to maintain its fully diluted stake.

segments.name: Other businesses
segments.commentary: Renewables revenue +59% YoY; textiles +26% YoY; insulators serving the power sector expansion.

guidance_outlook: Birla Opus: continues to target INR10,000 crore revenue by FY28 and guides over 50% YoY revenue growth for FY27; expects to become profitable once it reaches INR10,000 crore.
Birla Pivot: on track for EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27 (earlier guidance tied break-even to about USD1 billion or INR8,500 crore revenue; timeline shifted slightly).
Standalone FY27 capex planned at INR3,157 crore (about 45% growth); Q1 spend INR375 crore (about 12% of budget).

Opus Q2 FY27 expected to be weaker on monsoon seasonality and reversal of Q1 dealer stocking; management expects market stock to normalise by Q3.

Lyocell Phase 2: INR3,094 crore, 110,000 TPA, approved and moving through environmental clearance.

demand_pricing: Birla Opus: raw material COGS up 20-25%, or 10-14% of revenue depending on month; price increases were phased, cumulative 8.8% in Q1 with part flowing into Q2. Management said Q1 was boosted by dealer channel stocking ahead of industry price hikes.
Birla Opus distribution: 12,100+ towns, 55,000+ dealers billed, 1,450+ exclusive franchise outlets, 228 products and 1,945 SKUs, about 11,000 institutional project sites billed in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Birla Opus's sequential growth of 17% in line with listed peers, and how should profitability and revenue be prioritised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 industry revenue was inflated by channel stocking ahead of double-digit price hikes; as a new entrant, Birla Opus lacks that stocking power. It will keep the INR10,000 crore revenue target and judge revenue over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Will Birla Opus turn profitable on a full-year FY28 basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stand is unchanged: profitability begins once Birla Opus reaches INR10,000 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 64% YoY growth give confidence on FY27 growth above 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to over 50% YoY revenue growth for FY27; annual dealer loyalty and year-end schemes are expected to add sales in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 0.25% royalty to Birla Holdings and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Applicable from 1 June 2026 on standalone revenue, capped at INR225 crore. Management estimated about INR100 crore impact for standalone; on INR50,000 crore revenue it would be about INR125 crore. Subsidiaries pay on their own revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How will Grasim fund the Renewables equity contribution and what is the net debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Grasim's contribution in FY27 is under INR1,000 crore, with a cash impact of less than INR1,000 crore; GIP is also investing. Net debt to EBITDA will stay below 2x through the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for chemicals margins and caustic pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margins will face pressure from higher-cost inventory bought in Q1, and it is pricing near daily against commodity prices. It sees domestic caustic trading at import parity and new PVC-linked capacity as small.

qa_highlights.question: Are VSF margins sustainable, and what is the impact of Lenzing exits?
qa_highlights.answer: VSF operating rates in India are close to 100% excluding maintenance. Management said competitor exits are small, high-cost capacity and that Indonesian capacity cuts help global supply-demand balance.

qa_highlights.question: When will Birla Pivot break even, and what share of sales comes from UBS stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot is set to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even, slightly later than earlier guidance. Retail is 15-20% of mix, and UBS is 70-75% of retail revenue.

risks_watch: Paints margins and share: price differential vs industry has narrowed; Q2 volumes may be weak due to monsoon and dealer destocking.
Commodity volatility: sulphur, caustic and cotton input costs, Middle East and Gulf conflict affecting shipping and feedstock; chemicals faces Q2 margin pressure from expensive Q1 inventory.
Caustic soda price correction risk from new Indian capacity, despite management's view that import parity will hold.
Renewables (AB Renewables) capital needs and debt levels; a separate analyst session has been promised with the company team.
Birla Pivot EBITDA break-even timing, which has already slipped slightly versus earlier guidance.
Royalty payable to Birla Holdings starting June 2026 adds a cost line for standalone.

Birla Pivot remains on track to achieve EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27.

rows.label: Birla Pivot EBITDA break-even by FY27 exit
rows.why: Pivot revenue is INR2,548 crore (+75% YoY) with annualised run rate above INR10,000 crore, but break-even timing has slipped slightly from earlier guidance.

500300|2026-09.headline: Grasim Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue hit record ₹50,105 crore (+26% YoY); adjusted consolidated PAT fell 10% after ₹767 crore Nackawic exceptional charge.
500300|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue rose 33% YoY to an all-time high of ₹12,747 crore, with standalone EBITDA at ₹4,615 crore boosted by ₹4,000 crore-odd UltraTech dividend. Reported consolidated PAT was hit by an exceptional ₹767 crore charge (₹825 crore standalone) for idling the AV Group NB pulp mill at Nackawic, Canada; excluding it, consolidated PAT was ₹536 crore and standalone PAT ₹3,132 crore. Birla Opus paints grew 35% YoY in Q2 but revenue fell sequentially on flat realisations and seasonal softness, while management guides to 50% full-year growth on October strength. Chemicals and VSF were up YoY, but caustic prices are at five-year lows and epoxy margins are compressed.

financial_highlights.change: 2.6x YoY, led by UltraTech dividend income
Adjusted PAT down 10% YoY; consolidated PBT up 34% YoY

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹1,337 crore, +35% YoY with volume +20%; H1 volume +33%. Sequentially revenue fell on seasonality and flat realisation; institutional sales fell QoQ but grew 59% YoY. Combined Opus and White Putty revenue share in early teens; target is double-digit share for Opus alone in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹2,785 crore, +66% YoY; retail segment already EBITDA-positive. Q2 EBITDA hit by one-time employee costs (~₹10 crore ESOP impact cited); break-even targeted in H2 FY27 and FY27 revenue above ₹12,000 crore.

segments.name: Cellulosic fibres (VSF/CSF)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹5,344 crore, +29% YoY on volume, mix and stable domestic realisation. Management said Q2 VSF margin was about ₹22/kg and guided Q3 as range-bound; sequential profitability fell on sulfur and pulp cost increases.

segments.name: Chemicals (caustic, chlorine derivatives, specialty)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2,759 crore, +15% YoY. Caustic CFR SE Asia at five-year low of USD390/t; domestic chlorine prices improved. CPVC (50,000 t, Aug 2026) and epichlorohydrin (50,000 t, Oct 2026) commissioned at Vilayat; chlorine integration to reach 67%. Epoxy margins compressed by BPA/ECH price increases and sluggish demand.

segments.name: Other businesses (textiles, insulators, renewables)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue +16% YoY, EBITDA +14% YoY. Renewable capacity 2.2 GWp after adding 269 MW YoY; CCI approval received for Sprng acquisition, closing expected in calendar 2026, which would take capacity to about 10 GW.

guidance_outlook: Birla Opus: full-year FY27 revenue growth of about 50% YoY maintained; H2 expected to be significantly better than H1 with 57-58% of revenue historically in H2.
Birla Opus: target double-digit revenue market share in H2 FY27 for Birla Opus alone; ambition of ₹10,000 crore brand and India's second-largest decorative paints company by exit FY28.
Industry growth expected at 15-20% in H2 FY27 after 16-17% in H1; listed price increases of 14-15%, retained increases of 9-10%.
Birla Pivot: break-even in H2 FY27 and revenue above ₹12,000 crore for FY27.
Standalone FY27 capex of ₹3,157 crore earmarked, of which ₹1,022 crore spent in H1; management maintained the guidance and expects H2 spend to be heavier.
Paints capex overall stays at about ₹10,000 crore (±1%), with the H1 shortfall of ₹300-400 crore mainly franchise and tinting machines.
UltraTech on track for 242.9 MTPA capacity by exit March 2028; Cellulosic Phase I (55,000 t) nearly complete on procurement; Phase II (110,000 t) environmental clearance at advanced stage.
capex_capacity: Standalone FY27 capex earmarked at ₹3,157 crore; ₹1,022 crore spent in H1 FY27; management said H2 will be heavier.
Cellulosic fibres expansion planned at 165,000 tpa in two phases: Phase I 55,000 tpa with procurement nearly complete; Phase II 110,000 tpa with environmental clearance application at advanced stage.
Chemicals: CPVC 50,000 t commissioned Aug 2026 and epichlorohydrin 50,000 t commissioned Oct 2026 at Vilayat; total chlor-alkali capacity about 2.6 Mtpa (1.5 Mt caustic, 1.1 Mt chlorine derivatives).

Birla Opus network: 1,760+ exclusive franchise stores (about 300 added in Q2), about 150 depots, 61,000+ billed dealers in 12,600+ towns.
demand_pricing: Global CSF prices rose for four consecutive quarters; Q2 FY27 average USD1.85/kg, +23% YoY. China CSF operating rates 93%, inventory six days.
Caustic soda under pressure: CFR SE Asia at five-year low of USD390/t; domestic prices firmed on stable demand and rupee depreciation. Chlorine prices improved, particularly in Gujarat.
Epoxy value chain margin-compressed as BPA/ECH costs rose and demand was sluggish; management is trading volume for margin.

Paints: Q2 net realisation flat QoQ despite dealer price list increases; trade discounts and schemes were higher in Q2 across the industry. Opus October volume growth well above H1 average; secondary sales via contractor scans grew 34% YoY vs primary +20%.
Birla Opus price gap to market leader narrowed to about 2-4% by September, excluding a 10% impact on pricing, from a much wider gap at the start of the year.

qa_highlights.question: Does H2 paints revenue growth need to exceed the 50% achieved in H1 to hit the double-digit share target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 should be significantly better than H1 and reiterated 50% YoY growth guidance for the full year, but did not split H2 growth further.

qa_highlights.question: Is there slippage in paints capex versus the ₹10,000 crore plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the overall paints capex remains about ₹10,000 crore (±1%), with ₹300-400 crore less spent so far, mainly on franchise and tinting machines.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for VSF profitability in Q3 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 prices were held stable and Q3 is expected to be range-bound, with sulfur easing from October; sulfur inventory is under two weeks and should be restocked from December.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Nackawic pulp mill get a ₹625 crore funding infusion, and what is the benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said Grasim holds 45% of the entity and will contribute its share of closure and liability costs; the mill was loss-making with reliability and cost issues, and idling from October 2026 lowers operating and fixed costs. Grasim sourced about 20% of its pulp from the mill and has covered supply from other sources; payback is expected within four years.

qa_highlights.question: Did Birla Opus gain revenue market share in Q2, and were discounts higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Opus did not gain revenue share in Q2 as larger competitors' primary sales were higher than expected. Industry trade discounts were higher in Q2 from wholesale schemes, while Opus discounts were lower; the gap to the leader was cut to 2-4%.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the H2 paints growth, and what is the industry growth view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects industry growth of 15-20% in H2 and Opus growth of about 50%, citing reach expansion, contractor advocacy and regional festival campaigns. Industry H1 growth was 16-17%, with 8-9% from price and 7-8% from volume.

risks_watch: Birla Opus H2 target: management guides to about 50% FY27 paints growth and double-digit market share in H2 FY27, but Q2 gained no revenue share and H1 growth was driven by primary sales; October volume strength is the only evidence so far.

Paints profitability: management said crude-linked raw material costs moved from pre-war 65-70% to 90-110% and suppliers have not cut prices; Opus is buying at higher costs while cutting its price gap to the leader to 2-4%.
VSF margins: Q2 margin about ₹22/kg; management guided Q3 range-bound but gave no Q4 guidance; sulfur inventory under two weeks, restocking from December, pulp prices not moderating.

Chemicals: caustic CFR SE Asia at USD390/t, a five-year low; epoxy margins compressed by BPA/ECH costs with volume traded for margin; management said Q4 may be a bit better but cautioned heavily on forecasts.

Nackawic/AV Group NB: ₹825 crore standalone and ₹767 crore consolidated exceptional charge; a ₹625 crore funding contribution at 45% stake with a stated four-year payback; further closure liabilities are not quantified.
Birla Pivot: break-even targeted in H2 FY27 and FY27 revenue above ₹12,000 crore; one-time employee costs (~₹10 crore ESOP) hit Q2 EBITDA, and the B2B segment's profitability path is still unproven.
Sprng acquisition: CCI approval received and closing targeted in calendar 2026; the 10 GW pro forma capacity depends on closure, and the 20 GW ambition is unquantified.
key_quotes: We maintain that guidance, and you can do the maths based on that.
No, we did not gain revenue market share, which is one of the reasons is that the primaries of certain companies were higher than we anticipated.
Q4, I don't want to give any guidance or any promises because I'm not very sure how the situation changes.
So we are busy trading off volume margin at this stage.

Noticeably cautious and evasive on Q2 market share, discounting, and chemicals outlook. They declined to give quantified Q3/Q4 VSF or epoxy guidance and repeatedly stressed that the reported revenue market share is only a derived estimate.

rows.why: Price gap to market leader cut to 2-4% by September from a much wider gap at the start of the year, though the 10% pricing impact and higher raw material costs limit the room to hold it.

500304|2026-03.headline: NIIT Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR997 mn, but EBITDA was near breakeven at negative INR0.2 mn as investment continued.

Order intake rose 17% to INR4,209 mn for the year and 18% YoY in Q4 to INR869 mn, giving a positive book-to-bill entering FY27. Ex-iamneo, Q4 revenue was INR875 mn, only a marginal YoY increase, so growth was largely acquisition-driven. Management guided Q1 FY27 to double-digit revenue growth and breakeven to low-single-digit negative EBITDA, but said full-year visibility depends on quarterly macro conditions.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR630 mn, +13% YoY; enterprise tech INR489 mn, +20% YoY (+9% organic ex-iamneo). BFSI-led spend under pressure at large private banks.

segments.name: Consumer GTM
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR367 mn, +21% YoY; consumer tech INR210 mn, +28% YoY. Mix shifted to 63:37 enterprise:consumer from 65:35.

segments.name: Technology programs
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR699 mn, +22% YoY; 70% of revenue versus 67% last year. Management cited AI adoption and higher-level skills as drivers.

segments.name: BFSI and other programs
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR298 mn, +4% YoY; management cited BFSI and others down about 12% for the year, with early signs of banking onboarding demand returning in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-iamneo the organic business looked slightly down; what gives confidence on growth this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited BFSI and others down about 12% and technology up about 20% for the year; BFSI green shoots in Q4 and the opening order book should support growth. Management said headcount additions at iamneo were targeted investments, while organic headcount fell by 30.

qa_highlights.question: Does 'stronger revenue' for FY27 mean growth above FY26's 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Only if the environment stays stable; management said it cannot commit to beating FY26 and expects to revisit guidance every quarter. Q1 FY27 is expected to show double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company shift investment from consumer to enterprise given the job market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the direction and said the focus is shifting to working professionals, undergraduates and early-career learners, not only enterprise. Consumer working-professional programs launched in Q3 are showing traction.

qa_highlights.question: Why no acquisitions in the last year, and is the inorganic strategy changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still looking and has an active pipeline, reviewed two or three targets closely, but found none that met its criteria. iamneo was described as a well-timed addition.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins improve in Q2 and Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said platform investment is behind it but content and AI curriculum spend continues; some improvement is expected toward the tail end of the year, not necessarily in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI reskilling market getting crowded, and can NIIT stand out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said many players offer AI skills, but NIIT differentiates on AI fluency and outcome-based, personalised training, which is reflected in contracts won where it must demonstrate value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable market and where can NIIT be in a few years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to size the TAM, pointing to third-party reports, and said AI adoption has moved from pilot to production with more appetite expected in FY27.

500304|2026-06.headline: NIIT Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR957 million and EBITDA loss narrowed to INR14 million from INR63 million.

Operating expenses grew 7%, narrowing EBITDA loss to INR14 million from INR63 million a year earlier. PAT rose 85% YoY to INR81 million, helped by INR180 million net other income, mostly treasury income. Management guided to double-digit YoY revenue growth and near-breakeven EBITDA in Q2 FY27, with positive margins in H2.

Consumer businesses (Jio and Retail) drove growth, with Jio Platforms FY26 EBITDA of Rs 76,255 Crores (around 19% YoY) and Retail record quarterly revenue of Rs 98,000 Crores. Quarterly PAT was pressured by higher depreciation and interest from 5G asset capitalisation. 500325|2026-09.headline: Reliance Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA hit a record Rs 62,409 crore (+24% YoY) and PAT crossed Rs 50,000 crore on a half-year basis, led by O2C.

Digital services EBITDA rose 18% to about Rs 22,200 crore, while Retail EBITDA fell about 10-11% to Rs 6,228 crore as it invests in online commerce.
