500331|2026-09.headline: Pidilite Q2 FY27 standalone revenue grew 21.7% on 10.7% UVG, but EBITDA margin fell 430 bps to 20.4% as VAM input costs spiked.
500331|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue was just under INR4,000 crore in Q2 FY27, up 21.7% in nominal terms, with underlying volume growth (UVG) of 10.7% that management called broad-based. Gross margin fell 720 bps YoY and sequentially as VAM consumption rate hit $1,630/t versus $1,370 in Q1, and EBITDA margin came in at the low end of the range at 20.4%. H1 standalone revenue grew 22% with UVG of 11% and H1 EBITDA margin of 23.5%. Management priced up 12-15% in Q1, cut back on pricing in Q2 as VAM cooled, then took another round from October 1 and flagged a possible further 3-5% round.

financial_highlights.change: Down 430 bps YoY; lower end of 20-24% corridor
EBITDA up 53%; Dubai, Bangladesh, Kenya, Thailand each grew >20%
Consumer & Bazaar +22%, B2B +22%; Nina the only headwind (waterproofing workfront shortage)
Benefited from low-cost inventory from Q4 FY26

segments.name: Consumer & Bazaar (standalone)
segments.commentary: UVG of 11.1% in Q2 and 11.6% in H1; Roff, Dr. Fixit and new campaigns in Q3; Stainoff getting strong quick-commerce response.

segments.name: B2B (standalone)
segments.commentary: UVG of 9.2% in Q2 and 8.3% in H1; projects business reorganised into segment-based approach (builders, hotels/hospitals/education, EPC) with momentum expected into Q3.

segments.name: International subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue +21.8% and EBITDA +53% in Q2; four markets each grew above 20%.

segments.name: Domestic subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue +22.2% in Q2, led by ICA (wood finish) and construction chemical JVs; Nina down on monsoon-period workfront constraints.

guidance_outlook: H2 EBITDA margin expected within the 20-24% corridor, ideally the upper end, based on VAM around $1,200/t and the October pricing.
Management aims to keep UVG in double digits and ultimately move to early teens over time; not chasing volume for its own sake.
Further price increase of 3-5% in areas of heightened inflation may follow towards end of Q3 or early Q4, depending on the environment.
Margin base view remains 20-24%, with a bias to the higher end and gradual inching up.
capex_capacity: Exterior render (Grupopuma JV) production currently at Rajasthan facility; management evaluating additional plants given momentum.

Management says entire absolute cost increase has been passed on, but percentage margin recovery lags; calibrated pricing going forward.
VAM was $800-900/t through FY26, spiked to about $2,000 after West Asia conflict, cooled to around $900-1,000 in Q2, and was about $1,200 at the time of the call.
Urban growth picked up and urban slightly ahead of rural in Q2 for the first time in a long time; rural growth stable.
Competitive intensity described as reasonable and unchanged; local competitors in Fevicol and Dr. Fixit are a mix of very local and large players.
Exports into West Asia still underperforming due to shipping disruption.
Fevicol delivered 50-100 bps better growth than in the past.

qa_highlights.question: Was pricing delayed in expectation of geopolitical resolution, and what is current VAM and crude pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cut back pricing in Q2 as VAM cooled to around $900-1,000, then took a round on October 1 as VAM rose again; current VAM about $1,200 and crude about $115. Q3 and H2 margins expected in the 20-24% corridor, ideally the upper end.

qa_highlights.question: Are local players exiting as in detergents, and what share of raw materials is crude-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: No fundamental shift in competitive intensity; competitors in Dr. Fixit and tile adhesives are large companies. Sandeep said bulk of raw and packaging materials are crude-linked, but pass-through lags due to demand-supply dynamics.

qa_highlights.question: Are Araldite Wud and Araldite White new products and how are they priced?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, they are new to the portfolio and aimed at the premium wood and stone segments; management also cited Wonderproof, M-Seal Advance and Fevicol Multi Lock/X-Per as fundamental innovations.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken and how sustainable is volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Round one was 12-15% in high-inflation areas; a further 3-5% round is planned in some areas. Management said demand has been robust, targets double-digit UVG with a GDP-linked assumption of 6.5-7% real growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company seeing productivity gains from AI and operating leverage on A&P and staff costs?
qa_highlights.answer: AI is being used for marketing content, influencer work, analytics and supply chain/manufacturing variance reduction; productivity gains are a later phase and headcount reduction is not the aim during growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk from a competitor's new VAM plant, and is backward integration planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no cost advantage in domestic VAM given scale economics and India's lack of ethylene/acetic acid advantage, and prefers procurement plus cycle management.

qa_highlights.question: Has demand held up despite macro headwinds and job-loss concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says demand in India has held up and the team is not assuming macro improvement for the rest of the year; exports to West Asia remain weak.

risks_watch: Volatility in VAM and crude: VAM at about $1,200/t versus $1,370 in Q1 and $1,630 in Q2; further spikes would pressure H2 margins.

West Asia conflict, shipping disruption and El Nino effects not fully baked into the outlook; exports to West Asia underperforming.
Nina waterproofing headwind in monsoon period; Q3 retail and projects momentum to be verified.

500335|2026-03.headline: Birla Corp FY26 volume grew about 4% to a record with EBITDA near INR800 crore for the year and about INR1,000 crore in Q4, with FY27 volume guided only as mid-single-digit growth.
500335|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year with some plant operating setbacks that were overcome, delivering around 4% volume growth and a record volume from existing capacity. Q4 EBITDA was close to INR1,000 crore, with blended cement share rising from 82% to 88% and trade share from 70% to 77% over the year. Management is now building capacity from 21.5 to 27.5 million tonnes by FY29 at a capex of about INR4,753 crore including GST, and is guiding FY27 capex of INR900 crore. Management flagged that FY27 cost per tonne will rise by INR150-175 from Q1 on packaging and fuel, and declined to give EBITDA or volume guidance beyond broad directional statements.

segments.name: Cement (blended and premium)
segments.commentary: Blended cement at 88% and trade share at 77% of volumes in FY26; premium share about 63% per analyst read-back, with management aiming to move progressively towards near 100% blended. Perfect Plus is the flagship premium brand, now present across North and Central India.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete (RMC)
segments.commentary: Progress described as slow but steady; a fifth RMC plant in Uttar Pradesh is due soon, marketed under Perfect Plus. Management does not want to scale aggressively given receivable and recovery risks.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and wall putty
segments.commentary: Chemicals seen as a brand extension with a supply chain model being revamped and scale-up planned for the coming year; wall putty not being pursued aggressively as it is highly price-driven. Management said chemicals will never be a huge number and capex is light.

segments.name: Jute
segments.commentary: Management said the jute business had a turnaround-year setback due to abnormal raw jute prices and import disruptions from Bangladesh, with several mills shut or on reduced days. Management ruled out a strategic investor and is hoping for policy support after the change of government in West Bengal.

FY27 cost per tonne to rise by INR150-175 from Q1, mainly packaging and fuel cost.

Kundanganj 1.4 million tonne unit started, along with a third line; Prayagraj and Gaya Phase 1 each 1.4 million tonnes, expected in Q3-Q4 FY28.

Brahampuri coal block not being pursued actively as bid capacity is much lower than stated; Marki Barka expected to start by FY29 subject to regulatory issues.

demand_pricing: Management sees rising non-trade and OPC demand in many markets but says it is not chasing OPC; focus remains blended and premium cement.
Premium share and blended share expected to rise, but management would not commit to reaching 100% blended or to a timeline; slippage possible quarter to quarter.

Management says competitors who added capacity in UP are grinding OPC, which it will not do even with incentives; it views its high utilisation as a reason it is not under pressure to add volume.
Domestic fuel prices rising as cement players switch from imported fuel; imported fuel share about 30% of mix.

qa_highlights.question: Growth plans, capacity expansion and premium positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capacity expansion beyond Maihar Line-II and linked grinding units; target 27.5 million tonnes by FY29, with focus on blended and premium cement and no acquisitions currently.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and cost levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of about INR4,000-4,500 crore underway, with most internal accruals going to capex, so debt will rise; debt to EBITDA to stay below 2.5x. Bikram coal is the main cost lever from next year.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume, price hike, cost increase and capex reconfirmation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the analyst: it said mid-single-digit volume growth, not a specific 20 million tonnes; cost per tonne to rise INR150-175 from Q1; FY27 capex INR900 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital tighten and what is net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel inventory was built deliberately at year-end due to coal price and geopolitical concerns; net debt about INR2,100 crore, peak net debt expected around INR4,000 crore in this capex cycle; interest cost hard to estimate as term loans are linked to floating benchmarks.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra incentive of about INR500 crore receivable not yet realised, plus higher working capital from fuel inventory; realisation expected from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: RMC and construction chemicals plans and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: RMC is a brand extension, with a fifth UP plant soon; chemicals to scale up with revamped supply chain but remain small; capex light.

qa_highlights.question: Incentives in FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 incentive income about INR140 crore total, of which about INR90 crore for earlier years and about INR48-50 crore for the current year; FY27 expected around INR130 crore.

500335|2026-06.headline: Birla Corp Q1 FY27: realisations hit by soft Central India trade prices and lower incentives; Q2 cost up INR70-80/t sequentially, FY27 EBITDA guidance not reiterated.
500335|2026-06.overview: Management said the quarter was hurt by being at high utilisation in trade and blended cement, where prices did not rise, while gains came from non-trade, industrial and OPC segments where the company has little exposure. Central India prices stayed soft, and the company's dependence on that region rose with Kundanganj Line 3. Reported realisation fell about INR40/t sequentially, which management attributed mainly to lower incentives (INR33 crore vs INR60 crore in Q4) and year-end discounts; excluding these, it said realisation rose INR80/t. Costs rose on fuel and geopolitical factors, with a further INR70-80/t increase expected in Q2. Management kept earlier FY27 capex (INR900 crore), net debt and growth guidance, but declined to comment on full-year EBITDA.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not shifting away from trade or blended cement; if other players do not raise prices in the trade segment it will decide its own marketing strategy and ways to protect margins, which may not involve price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the other expenses increase (INR511 crore to INR551 crore consolidated) and Kundanganj incentive accrual.

rows.why: Volume growth guidance of 6-7% was maintained but not quantified on the call; Mukutban ran at 7.5 lakh t and utilisation is above 90%, with demand buoyant from mid-May and June but delayed monsoon a risk.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: FY28 (significant step-up); next phase order placement start
rows.why: Utilisation is about 90% with the 27.6 MTPA expansion approved but spend almost nil, and management said FY28 capex will step up significantly, so a fresh capex step is likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to comment on full-year EBITDA and only maintained existing guidance, with price recovery in Central India still hoped for rather than visible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 cost up INR70-80/t and no price movement in July, with trade prices soft for about a year in Central India; full-year EBITDA guidance was not reiterated.

rows.label: Central India trade price recovery
rows.why: Trade prices flat to rolled back in June and Central India soft for about a year; management said it may revisit its marketing strategy if larger players do not raise trade prices, but sees no price war.

rows.label: Q2 cost step-up from fuel and geopolitics
rows.why: Costs guided up INR70-80/t sequentially in Q2 after INR150/t geopolitical impact on bags and fuel in Q1; packaging at INR269/t vs INR191/t year-ago.

rows.label: Bikram coal captive supply ramp
rows.why: Bikram coal use rises to 1.2 lakh t in FY27 and 3.5 lakh t in FY28 versus fuel cost of INR1.64/KCal against Bikram cost of about INR1.05/KCal cited by analyst, with about one-third of CPP coal needs met.

tone.note: Management was confident in keeping capex (INR900 crore), net debt and growth guidance and that competition will stay rational, but cautious on full-year EBITDA, Q2 costs and Central India prices; analysts pressed on EBITDA per ton, the realisation decline and the trade/non-trade mix.

500335|2026-09.headline: Birla Corp Q2 FY27 margins squeezed: EBITDA/tonne of INR482 under pressure as fuel costs rise and trade cement prices stay soft.
500335|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as modest, with cost pressure from pet coke and domestic coal and weak trade pricing in the central region. Capacity utilisation was about 85% in the quarter. Power and fuel costs rose sharply, and purchased clinker (due to a shutdown carried over from the prior quarter) weighed on standalone margins. Management expects fuel costs to rise further sequentially in Q3, with fuel alone adding about INR100/tonne, and sees little certainty on price recovery. Net borrowings rose to INR2,432 crore from INR2,200 crore in June, driven by working capital.

financial_highlights.value: INR482/tonne (as referenced by analyst for Q2)

financial_highlights.metric: Power and fuel cost per tonne (Q2)
financial_highlights.value: INR1.81 million kcal-type unit as stated; Q3 guided at INR1.00-1.05 (transcript wording 'cost per million type' unclear; management later said 2 to 2.05)

financial_highlights.change: up from INR2,200 crore as of June

financial_highlights.value: INR30 crore accrued in Q2; INR63 crore in H1; closing balance about INR545 crore; no receipts in Q2

financial_highlights.change: Mukutban was about 400 km last quarter

financial_highlights.value: about 13%; imported fuel about one-third; domestic purchased coal about half; AFR about 4%

segments.name: Trade / non-trade cement
segments.commentary: Company is heavily skewed to trade and blended sales, where trade prices stayed flat despite healthy demand. Non-trade prices in Central India corrected in late Q2 and saw a modest uptick in October, which management does not view as solid.

segments.name: Jute
segments.commentary: Management said jute is a minor contributor and not material to BCL's top or bottom line. Q1 benefited from a price revision, and high raw jute costs hit the middle line.

guidance_outlook: Fuel cost per tonne expected to rise by about INR100/tonne sequentially in Q3; management expects coal prices to rise from Q2 levels in Q3.
Domestic coal prices may ease after winter if power demand falls and Coal India subsidiaries' supply improves; pet coke prices expected to stay at or above current levels into Q4.
Management aims to pass cost increases to customers, with an expected recovery of about INR5-10 per bag, but cannot be an outlier versus the market.
Capacity expansion of 6.2-6.5 million tonnes slated for FY28-FY29; company is maintaining the earlier timeline.
Captive coal expected to meet about 15% of fuel requirement this year; captive coal currently 20-25% cheaper than market.
Capex guidance for FY27-FY29 not given; management expects to provide it towards year-end.
capex_capacity: Expansion of about 6.2-6.5 million tonnes expected to come in FY28-FY29; timeline maintained.
Second captive coal mine (Bikram) is on stream; output is being ramped up, with low-grade coal used in power plant so far and better-grade coal being sought for the kiln.
Renewable power share targeted to rise from 32-plus% to 45% within about a year.
Capex for FY27-FY29 not disclosed; management to guide towards year-end.
Mukutban and Kundanganj incentive plants: INR545 crore incentive balance outstanding; West Bengal incentive matter sub judice.
demand_pricing: Trade prices in the central region stayed soft despite healthy demand in some months; consolidation has not produced the price discipline expected by the industry.
Non-trade prices corrected in late Q2, with some uptick in October; management does not see these gains as firm.
Drought in parts of Maharashtra and Rajasthan and floods earlier in North Bihar and eastern UP are risks to demand.
Upcoming UP elections may soften non-trade demand once model code of conduct applies; Gujarat and Rajasthan infrastructure demand is supportive.
Peers with capacity additions and sub-70% utilisation are seen as likely to push volume, which keeps prices soft.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 EBITDA per tonne stay at INR482 or lower, given cost increases and limited price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a specific EBITDA figure. Fuel alone is expected to add about INR100/tonne sequentially in Q3, with the recovery of about INR5-10 per bag uncertain and dependent on peer behaviour.

qa_highlights.question: What are the October price hikes versus the Q2 average?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exit rate in October is around INR5-7/bag, but the average may not reach that level.

qa_highlights.question: How much fuel comes from captive coal and what is the cost gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive coal is expected to cover about 15% of fuel this year, and is currently 20-25% cheaper than market fuel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fuel mix and what are lead distance, Mukutban volume and packaging cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel mix: about one-third imported, about half domestic purchased, about 13% captive, about 4% AFR. Lead distance 336 km overall (Mukutban 411 km); Mukutban volume 6.5 lakh tonnes; packaging INR248/tonne.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt has fallen, but costs are rising. How did borrowings fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said net borrowings rose to INR2,432 crore from INR2,200 crore as of June, mainly due to working capital needs from pet coke purchases at higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why does standalone look weaker than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to fuel mix: RCCPL plants have captive Sial Ghoghri coal and transferable linkage coal in Maharashtra, while BCL plants bought pet coke and domestic coal at higher prices.

risks_watch: Fuel cost escalation (pet coke, domestic coal) with Q3 costs expected up sequentially and about INR100/tonne from fuel alone.
Pricing discipline in Central India trade segment; whether peers' capacity expansion keeps prices soft.
Weather: drought in Maharashtra and Rajasthan, and elections in UP that may soften non-trade demand.
Recovery of the INR545 crore incentive balance; West Bengal matter remains sub judice.
Delivery of the 6.2-6.5 million tonne capacity expansion in FY28-FY29, and capex guidance expected at year-end.
Purchased clinker cost in the quarter was linked to a delayed shutdown; the effect should taper in Q3 as the shutdown is completed.
500335|2026-09.management_tone: Cautious and candid on costs and pricing: management repeatedly called the quarter modest and said it cannot predict pricing or demand reliably. It was more confident on operational levers (captive coal, AFR, renewables) and on the expansion timeline.
key_quotes: We know it is modest and subdued, largely due to factors which everybody knows, especially on the cost side.
So on fuel accounts only we expect a cost increase of about INR100 a ton.
As of date, it is 20% to 25%.
We are maintaining our earlier guidance in terms of this time line.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Fuel alone adds about INR100/tonne sequentially in Q3 on pet coke and coal, against EBITDA of INR482/tonne, with the INR5-10/bag price recovery uncertain and trade prices soft.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 6.2-6.5 Mt expansion has its timeline maintained, but it falls outside the 2-4 quarter window except for its late tail, and utilisation is 85% with management saying it can go to 90-95%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation is 85% and management says it can run to 90-95%, but no volume growth guidance was given and peers with sub-70% utilisation are likely to push volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 85%, which is high, but capex for FY27-FY29 is not guided and management will only give it towards year-end.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give EBITDA figures, called the quarter modest and said it cannot predict pricing or demand reliably.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel costs are guided up about INR100/tonne sequentially in Q3, price recovery is uncertain, and net borrowings rose to INR2,432 crore from INR2,200 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or grades were discussed.

rows.label: INR5-10/bag price pass-through
rows.why: Management targets INR5-10/bag recovery and cites an October exit rate of INR5-7/bag, but says the average may not reach it and it cannot be an outlier to the market.

rows.label: Captive coal cost advantage
rows.why: Captive coal is expected to meet about 15% of fuel this year and is 20-25% cheaper than market fuel, with the Bikram mine now on stream.

rows.label: West Bengal incentive recovery
rows.why: The INR545 crore incentive balance has no Q2 receipts (INR30 crore accrued in Q2) and the West Bengal matter is sub judice.

tone.note: Management was cautious on fuel costs, pricing and demand, saying the quarter was modest and it cannot predict prices, and was more confident on captive coal, AFR, renewables and the FY28-FY29 expansion timeline; analysts pressed on Q3 EBITDA per tonne, price recovery and net debt.

500336|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue ₹2,163 crore (+1% YoY) and EBITDA ₹170 crore, down from ₹211 crore; management guides FY27 EBITDA ₹680–700 crore.
500336|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was flat YoY at ₹2,163 crore, while EBITDA fell to ₹170 crore (7.9% margin) from ₹211 crore and PAT to ₹98 crore from ₹130 crore. Steel Pipe and Strip volume hit a record 2.6 lakh tons, but EBITDA per ton fell to ₹5,121 from ₹6,708 as exports went to nearly nil after the Middle East crisis. Lighting revenue grew 9% YoY to ₹501 crore but EBITDA dipped to ₹44 crore. Management guided FY27 volume of 11 lakh tons and combined EBITDA of ₹680–700 crore, which analysts questioned against the implied per-ton economics; the company remains debt-free with ₹337 crore net cash.

financial_highlights.metric: Lighting & CD revenue Q4 FY26 / FY26
Steel Pipe & Strip revenue Q4 FY26 / FY26
financial_highlights.change: Q4 vs ₹1,688 crore; FY26 vs ₹5,749 crore
Q4 vs ₹164 crore (₹6,708/ton); FY26 vs ₹446 crore (₹5,392/ton)

segments.name: Steel Pipe & Strip
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹1,662 crore and EBITDA ₹126 crore on record 2.6 lakh tons; FY26 volume 9.04 lakh tons, 43% value-added, utilisation 78–80%. Exports were 1.36 lakh tons in FY26 and dropped to nearly nil in Q4 due to the Middle East crisis.

segments.name: Lighting & Consumer Durables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹501 crore (+9% YoY) with PBT ₹33 crore vs ₹37 crore; March 2026 was the highest monthly sales month in every category. Professional Lighting FY26 revenue ₹473 crore (26% share) with order book ₹160 crore; Wire & Cable FY26 revenue ₹38 crore, FY27 target ₹260 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 combined EBITDA guided at ₹680–700 crore (Steel ₹470–480 crore, Lighting ~₹200 crore); management said it could reach ₹750 crore before a ~₹40–50 crore labour-code impact.
FY27 steel volume target 11 lakh tons (+21–22%); Q1 FY27 volume guided at ~2.65 lakh tons with Steel EBITDA of ₹120–125 crore.
FY27 steel revenue ~₹7,200 crore and group revenue ₹9,400–9,500 crore (+24–25%) per management.
Exports targeted above 2.5 lakh tons in FY27 (vs 1.36 lakh tons), with US order book ~65,000 tons and ~10,000 tons/month added from June; export EBITDA cited at ₹9,000–10,000 per ton.
Steel EBITDA per ton assumed at ~₹4,700 for FY27; Lighting value growth target 22–25% annually over the medium term.
Wire & Cable FY27 revenue target ₹260 crore, on track for ₹500–600 crore in three years.
capex_capacity: Capacity rose ~2 lakh tons over the last 1.5 years; capacity is about 1.4 million tons now and expected to reach ~1.6 million tons in FY27.
A further ~3 lakh tons is planned, taking capacity to ~1.9 million tons in FY28–FY29 (per management).
Seamless-to-ERW/ONGC-linked capex needs 9–10 months; volume impact expected in FY28 and excluded from the 11 lakh ton target.
Capex policy stated as one-third of profit to capex, one-third to working capital and growth, one-third to shareholders.
demand_pricing: Steel order book about ₹1,000 crore-plus, led by exports, spiral and some domestic API orders; H1 FY27 expected to be the highest-ever half for value-added sales.
North America export order book ~65,000 tons; management expects ~1.2 lakh tons of US exports in FY27.
Government/API/tender business is about 15–16% of volume; water pipes plus spiral take it to about 28–30%.
API and spiral EBITDA per ton fell from about ₹12,000 (FY23) to ₹5,600 (FY26) per an analyst's figures, which management acknowledged; tendering competition has risen.
Imported raw material is about 30–35% of input cost; higher input and fuel costs and the labour code (₹30–50 crore impact) pressure FY27 margins.
Steel HR coil availability was tight for 3–4 months due to gas shortages linked to the Middle East crisis; management says it is now largely resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 miss expectations when competitors grew strongly, and will the 12,000 tons of missed exports be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the Middle East crisis, which cut exports to near nil and left about 12,000 tons of ready material unshipped, plus a domestic steel shortage. It said Q1 FY27 volume will be a record ~2.65 lakh tons.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA of ₹680–700 crore credible given the implied ₹4,700 per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance already includes risks such as input cost inflation, fuel and power costs, and labour-code costs of ₹30–40 crore; it could reach ₹750 crore. It cited export EBITDA of ₹9,000–10,000 per ton offsetting pressure in oil and gas and domestic businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Why is volume growth only ~70,000–80,000 tons domestically if exports add 1.1–1.25 lakh tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government spending on oil and gas and water schemes is assumed to stay low, so it kept targets conservative; it said 11 lakh tons is a minimum and could be exceeded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Lighting demerger and buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the demerger will be discussed with the board once the crisis ends, possibly by the next board meeting. It said a buyback is being reconsidered now that the regulations have been reintroduced, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has steel growth lagged the industry over 4–5 years and why has API/spiral EBITDA per ton fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed slow growth to no major capex during COVID and two years after, and a focus on higher-margin products. It said API/spiral per-ton EBITDA halved as tendering is uncontrolled and competition has increased.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of steel availability constraints for Q1–Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the HR coil shortage lasted 3–4 months due to a demand surge and gas shortages, is now largely sorted, and that domestic HR coil supply is growing each year.

risks_watch: Execution on the 2.65 lakh ton Q1 FY27 volume and recovery of the ~12,000 tons of missed exports.
Whether steel EBITDA per ton recovers from ₹5,121 (Q4) toward the ~₹4,700 FY27 assumption and the export mix ramps (US ~1.2 lakh tons).
Middle East crisis effects on exports, gas availability and HR coil supply.
Input cost pressure (imported raw material 30–35% of cost), labour-code costs and government spending delays on water and oil & gas projects.
Credibility of guidance: management has missed volume targets in consecutive quarters, as an analyst pointed out.
Lighting demerger timing and the buyback decision, both not yet confirmed.
500336|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 and the US export opportunity, but defensive when questioned on repeated missed targets and falling per-ton margins. Management attributed the shortfall to external shocks and repeatedly reassured investors with few hard assumptions.
key_quotes: I can assure you that for FY27, whatever the situation with the Middle East crisis, considering all that, it will be the best year in history for Surya Roshni.
Our Q1 will have the highest-ever volume, around 2.65 lakh tons in Q1 itself and we will grow by about 27% to 28%.
I often say our relationship with the bank has ended; now our relationship is only with the shareholders.
Look, two things. One, as far as risk is concerned, the numbers we have just told you are telling these numbers after considering all these risk factors.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 78–80% with ~1.4 mt capacity; the ~3 lakh ton expansion to ~1.9 mt is already planned, so further announcements are likely as the FY28–FY29 build is formalised, though the stated policy directs one-third of profit to capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says ₹680–700 crore EBITDA could reach ₹750 crore and 11 lakh tons is a minimum, but the guide already absorbs ₹30–50 crore labour-code costs and domestic government spending is assumed low.

rows.why: Q4 EBITDA fell 19% YoY to ₹170 crore, FY26 EBITDA guided to ₹680–700 crore implies a ~25–30% jump from ₹541 crore, and exports were nearly nil in Q4 with ~12,000 tons unshipped; input cost, gas and HR coil risks remain.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wire & Cable revenue was ₹38 crore in FY26 with a FY27 target of ₹260 crore, and the company targets 22–25% annual Lighting value growth over the medium term.

rows.why: Exports were 1.36 lakh tons in FY26 but nearly nil in Q4; management expects ~1.2 lakh tons of US exports in FY27 against a ~65,000-ton order book, with export EBITDA cited at ₹9,000–10,000 per ton.

500336|2026-06.headline: Surya Roshni Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR2,046 crore and PAT 77% to INR60 crore, but steel EBITDA/ton of INR4,006 sits well below the FY27 INR4,600-4,700 guidance.
500336|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR2,046 crore (up 28% YoY), EBITDA of INR120 crore (up 46%) and PAT of INR60 crore (up 77%) were driven mainly by Steel Pipes & Strips, where volume hit a record Q1 of 2.28 lakh tons. Management attributed the EBITDA/ton shortfall to ocean freight (about INR800/ton on total volume) and coating, gas and ORM cost increases (about INR200/ton), and expects recovery as new orders are booked at higher freight rates. Lighting & Consumer Durables grew 15% to INR456 crore with margin up to 7.9%. The company remains debt-free with net cash of about INR155 crore; buyback and demerger decisions were deferred with no firm timeline.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +17% YoY (from INR31 crore); PBT +12% YoY (from INR21 crore)

financial_highlights.value: About INR155 crore (B.B. Singal cited INR154 crore) as of 30 June 2026

segments.name: Steel Pipes & Strips
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,590 crore (+32% YoY) on record Q1 volume of 2.28 lakh tons (+21% YoY); section, ERW API, spiral, cold rolling and GP pipes led, galvanized soft on delayed government fund releases. Capacity utilisation about 82%, value-added products 47% of volume, exports 20% of segment volume.

segments.name: Lighting & Consumer Durables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR456 crore (+15% YoY), best-ever Q1, led by LED bulbs, battens and downlighters; EBITDA INR36 crore with margin 7.9%, passing through about 7% input cost increase. Professional lighting order book about INR150 crore.

segments.name: Wire & Cables
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 sales nearly matched FY26 full-year volume; FY26 revenue target INR250 crore, against a 3-year INR500 crore goal. Electrician loyalty program enrolments reached 36,000.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steel volume about 11 lakh tons (+20-22% volume growth); quarterly path of about 2.6-2.65 lakh tons in Q2, 2.8-2.9 lakh in Q3 and about 3.2 lakh in Q4.
FY27 steel EBITDA/ton guidance of INR4,600-4,700 reiterated; management expects about INR4,400-4,500 in Q2 and INR4,600-4,700 full year, implying above INR5,000 in H2 per Q1 analyst math.
Company FY27 EBITDA guided at INR670-680 crore on revenue of INR9,400-9,500 crore; Q2 EBITDA about INR150 crore and H2 about INR400 crore.
Lighting FY27: revenue about INR2,200 crore (vs INR1,809 crore FY26), value growth 19-22%, volume growth about 25%, EBITDA about INR200 crore.

Steel value growth 30%+ expected for FY27; US market contribution 10-11% of volume (about 1.2-1.25 lakh tons in FY27), total exports about 3 lakh tons; export share of steel to rise from about 20% to 25%.
Ocean freight: new orders booked at higher rates, with July impact described as very low and no freight impact expected in the next two months; break-bulk shipping arranged for US volumes.
Full-year API/spiral EBITDA/ton expected to recover from Q1 INR3,420 to about INR5,000 (vs INR5,500-5,700 in FY26).
Per-ton cost reduction target of about INR1,100 and manpower cost reduction of about 20% over the next year; 15-18% CAGR targeted for the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capacity 14 lakh tons currently; target 16 lakh tons by end-FY27 with three DFT mills commissioning between August and December 2026 at Gujarat, Malanpur and Bahadurgarh; about 2 million tons by FY28-29.
Adding 2-3 lakh tons of capacity every year; capex about INR100 crore for the 14-to-16 lakh ton expansion, funded from internal accruals.

Hindupur (South) greenfield-style expansion on 10 additional acres: first mill about January 2027, total 4-mill plant adding about 15,000 tons initially, about INR60 crore investment, roughly 3 lakh tons overall.
Greenfield projects under evaluation with clarity promised by next board meeting; expansions focus on DFT and section pipes.
demand_pricing: Steel order book INR800 crore (export API orders include 78,000 tons for the US) vs INR1,000 crore at end-March; management said about 75-80% of business is distribution-type and fixed.
Ocean freight rose sharply; Q1 exports carried about INR3,800/ton higher freight, costing about INR800/ton of blended EBITDA. Management says new orders are priced at the higher freight.

US market opened for ERW API pipes, with realisation EBITDA/ton of about INR7,200 in Q1; Middle East orders fell (roughly one-third of usual 15,000-20,000 tons per quarter now able to ship), and API orders down about 50%.
Steel prices rose INR3,000-4,000/ton in April, then fell in May-June, leaving the quarter roughly neutral on inventory; steel now seen stable within INR1,000/ton.
Q1 API/spiral EBITDA/ton of INR3,420 cited with coating material as a significant drag; water pipe faces higher competition.
Lighting: about 80% of production in-house, about 20% outsourced, with the outsourced share largely made exclusively for Surya.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta (Enigma): how will steel EBITDA/ton reach INR4,700-4,800 when Q1 was about INR4,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 volume was about 2.30 lakh tons vs 2.65 lakh planned (port delays, Middle East orders down 8,000-10,000 tons, API/spiral shortfall of 8,000-10,000 tons). Margin gap of about INR700/ton was attributed to ocean freight (about INR800/ton on total volume) and coating, gas and ORM costs (about INR200/ton). New orders are priced at higher freight, and Q2 is guided at INR4,400-4,500/ton with full year INR4,600-4,700.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta: how much inventory loss occurred in Q1 given steel price swings?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose INR3,000-4,000/ton in April and fell in May-June, so the quarter was roughly neutral with no inventory impact. Steel is now seen stable within INR1,000/ton. About 25,000 tons of imported material already at port should support Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Kiran (TableTree): why did the steel order book fall from INR1,000 crore to INR800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier book was cleared and fresh orders carry higher freight; Middle East shipments are about one-third of the usual 15,000-20,000 tons per quarter, and API orders are down about 50%. About 75-80% of business is distribution-type and fixed, so the drop has limited volume impact.

qa_highlights.question: Kiran: is the US export product GI or API/spiral, and what is the FY27 and FY28 export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The US product is ERW API pipe, with Q1 realisation around INR7,200/ton, helped by freight; break-bulk tie-ups should lower freight exposure. US share of steel is seen at 8-10% (later 10-11%, about 1.2-1.25 lakh tons in FY27); export share rises from about 20% to about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Love Gupta (Counter Cyclical): any update on buyback and demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback work is ongoing and a decision is expected 'very soon', with no material to disclose yet; working capital rose during steel price swings. Demerger is a matter of board consensus, with the MD saying the timing is right once macro improves.

qa_highlights.question: Pranav (Rare Enterprises): why delay demerger or buyback, and will pricing offset the freight-driven EBITDA erosion?

500350|2026-03.headline: RSWM FY26 PAT turned positive at ₹52 crore (1.1% margin) from a ₹41 crore loss, while revenue fell 5.6% to ₹4,554 crore.

Q4 EBITDA was ₹85 crore at a 7.4% margin, up 115 bps YoY. For FY26, EBITDA rose 40.5% to ₹327 crore (7.1% margin, up 231 bps), helped by a ₹22.66 crore deferred tax liability write-back under the new tax regime. Management attributed the turnaround mainly to product-mix optimisation, exit from Chhata spinning (~₹250 crore revenue), working capital control and lower finance cost, and said it is not cyclical. 500350|2026-06.headline: RSWM Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.7% QoQ to ₹1,161 crore and EBITDA to ₹94 crore (8.0% margin), led by a 39.8% gross margin.
500350|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹1,161 crore, up 1.7% QoQ, with domestic sales up to ₹825 crore and exports down to ₹336 crore. Gross margin expanded to 39.8% from 37.4%, lifting EBITDA to ₹94 crore (+10.1% QoQ, +16.1% YoY) and margin to 8.0%. PAT was ₹17 crore against ₹7 crore a year ago, but lower than Q4 FY26, which included a one-time tax benefit. Management gave no full-year guidance; fabric profitability weakened sharply while yarn held up, and new projects (PET food-grade chips, denim garmenting JV, knitting expansion) were outlined.

financial_highlights.change: +1.7% QoQ vs ₹1,142 crore in Q4 FY26
vs 7.4% in Q4 FY26 and 6.9% in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Yarn (synthetic, cotton, mélange)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 96% for synthetic, 98% for cotton and 92-93% for mélange. Management said yarn demand held up and cotton/mélange spreads were good in Q1; Q2 is running similarly so far.

segments.name: Denim fabric
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was about 90%. Management said the segment faced the same cost and demand pressure as knit, with exports and domestic roughly balanced.

segments.name: Knit fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation was in the mid-80s%. Fabric EBIT was close to nil in Q1 and was negative (about ₹2 crore) in Q4 FY26, versus about ₹35-36 crore last year, as export garmenters' demand was subdued.

guidance_outlook: No full-year growth or EBITDA margin guidance given; management said all quarters should be similar to or better than Q1.

Power cost savings of about ₹40 crore for FY27 at constant utilisation (from renewables and efficiency), with a stated target of around ₹100 crore; renewable share of power rose from mid-20s% to mid-40s%, and about 60% in the current quarter.
Management expects per-unit power cost to fall by more than ₹1 year-on-year on average.
Knitting expansion expected to add benefits from Q3 FY27, with capacity going from 650 tons to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing.

Food-grade PET chip plant: completion in Q4 FY27, trials and commercial production in Q1 FY28; 50,000 tpa capacity, ₹500 crore revenue expected, about 15% EBITDA (industry norm per management). Utilisation ramp of 75%, 85%, then 90-91% over three years.
Graphene-based fibre (with Birla Cellulose): management expects commercial traction within FY27.
risks_watch: Crude and polyester price volatility, and a possible reversal of Q1 stocking gains.
Export demand recovery, especially knit fabric and Middle East markets; the company said recent inquiries are improving.
Fabric margins near nil; monitor whether fabric EBIT recovers in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
PET plant execution: food-grade certification and trials, no customer tie-ups yet, and a 15% EBITDA assumption that is management's industry norm.
Garmenting JV: stake and capex undisclosed, new skills needed, and a labour-intensive business that is new to RSWM.
Finance costs rising with working capital needs (₹31 crore).
Management gave no full-year guidance; the company's disclosure is limited on volumes and capex amounts.
Investor-presentation timing: it was uploaded about 15 minutes before the call, which an analyst objected to.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on the graphene-based fibre initiative with Birla Cellulose, when will it generate revenue, and what is the addressable market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project is ongoing with positive trial judgements and a first product round received from Grasim/Birla Cellulose; it expects it to start rolling within FY27. No market-size estimate yet; it will first master the product and then assess applications.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give yarn and fabric volumes and price movements for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose tonnage or metres. It gave utilisation: synthetic yarn ~96%, cotton ~98%, mélange 92-93%, denim ~90%, knit mid-80s%, and said polyester prices rose up to 30% in March, with stabilisation since.

qa_highlights.question: What is the stake, capacity and timing for the denim garmenting JV, and will it use internal fabric?
qa_highlights.answer: Stake still under discussion, with RSWM as major majority holder; phase 1 up to 5 lakh pieces per month, with two further phases. It is not a captive line; internal and external fabric will compete on price and quality. Knit garmenting may come in phase 2 or 3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any tie-up with customers for the food-grade PET chip plant, and what are its revenue and margin assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no customer tie-ups yet. Capacity is 50,000 tpa, expected revenue ₹500 crore, and industry EBITDA of about 15%. Completion is planned in Q4 FY27 with commercial production in Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is there full-year growth or margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said Q1 performance was positive, with cash profit up about 12% QoQ and EBITDA of ₹94 crore (about 8%), and expects all quarters to be similar to or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fabric EBIT close to nil versus ₹35-36 crore last year, and is there a transfer-pricing change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to subdued knit demand, cost pressure, and export garmenter weakness, not transfer pricing. Denim is balanced across export and domestic, while knit is mostly export-dependent. Inquiries have improved for the last two months. Yarn did better because yarn demand held up.

qa_highlights.question: How much power cost reduction is expected, and by how much per unit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renewables and efficiency gave a visible ~10% cut in power and fuel QoQ (₹123 crore to ₹112 crore). It targets about ₹40 crore in FY27 savings at constant utilisation, with a total target of around ₹100 crore. Per-unit power cost is expected to fall by more than ₹1 YoY on average.

qa_highlights.question: What PET plant utilisation ramp is planned, and what is the knit expansion benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: PET utilisation: 75% in year 1, 85% in year 2, and 90-91% by year 3. Knit capacity rises from 650 to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing, with benefits expected from Q3 FY27.

capex_capacity: Knitting expansion: capacity going from about 650 tons to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing capacity that does not exist today; benefits expected from Q3 FY27 via trials then scale-up.

Food-grade PET chip (B2B) plant: civil construction under way and orders placed for critical machines; completion in Q4 FY27, trials and commercial production in Q1 FY28; capacity 50,000 metric tons per year; expected revenue ₹500 crore; industry EBITDA norm about 15%.
PET plant utilisation ramp: 75% in year 1, then 85%, then 90-91% by year 3; certifications and trials required as food-grade product.

Denim garmenting JV: board gave principal approval on the day of discussion; stake percentage still under discussion but RSWM to be major majority shareholder; phase 1 up to 5 lakh pieces per month, with two further phases planned; denim first, knit possibly in phase 2 or 3.

Power cost: about ₹40 crore savings for FY27 at constant utilisation; company targeting around ₹100 crore total; renewable share of power up from mid-20s% to mid-40s%, about 60% in current quarter; power and fuel ₹112 crore vs ₹123 crore in Q4 FY26.
Graphene-based fibre with Birla Cellulose: first product round from Grasim/Birla Cellulose received; management expects it to start rolling within FY27; no capex or market-size figure disclosed.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 was volatile: crude-linked polyester fibre prices rose up to about 30% in March, hurting volumes in April-June; customers bought only as needed (lowest stocking), so business was mainly fresh lifting.
Prices have stabilised somewhat by the call date but crude volatility persists; domestic demand was less volatile than international demand.
Synthetic yarn: reasonably good sales in Q1, and Q2 running similarly so far. Cotton and mélange yarn: Q1 was good due to yarn-cotton spread and stocking gains; Q2 reasonably good so far.

Fabric: knit demand subdued as export garmenters (most knit customers) operated at low production; cost pressure from fibre, gas, freight and chemical prices. Denim is roughly balanced between export and domestic. Management said the last two months saw positive demand and a lot of inquiries.

Export revenue fell QoQ to ₹336 crore; management confirmed export weakness drove the lack of top-line growth, citing West Asia conflict, long transit times and high freight. Middle East demand subdued in the quarter.
Management said it could not give volumes in tonnes or metres; utilisation given instead: synthetic yarn ~96%, cotton ~98%, mélange ~92-93%, denim ~90%, knit mid-80s%.
key_quotes: So, thereby, in synthetic yarn business, RSWM could do reasonably good sales in this quarter, and the current quarter is also going in more or less the same way.
We have not done any tie-up at this point of time.
So, 75, 85 and then probably up to 90, 91%.
I expect it will be anything more than ₹1 per unit on an average year-over-year basis because of the impact of all these renewable sources we are using.

500350|2026-09.headline: RSWM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to ₹1,322 crore and PAT more than tripled to ₹24.5 crore, while fabric segments stayed near breakeven on raw-material cost pressure.
500350|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached ₹1,322 crore in Q2 FY27, up 13.9% QoQ and 15% YoY, with EBITDA of ₹116 crore (8.7% margin) up 47.1% YoY. PAT rose to ₹25 crore from ₹6 crore a year earlier, though this was after a one-time ₹11.5 crore exceptional provision on electricity duty for captive solar. Management said fabric (denim and knit) profitability was squeezed by cotton and polyester price spikes that could not be passed on quickly, with the fabric PBIT reported as negative ₹6 crore in the quarter. Management guided to better Q3 and Q4 on price pass-through and the ₹92 crore knitting expansion, and said H2 should beat H1.

financial_highlights.change: +23.2% QoQ; +47.1% YoY; margin +66 bps QoQ, +191 bps YoY
from ₹17 crore in Q1 FY27 and ₹6 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Yarn (synthetic, cotton, blended, melange)

Overall EBITDA margin should be around or better than 8.7% in the coming quarter; fabric division EBITDA should target double digits.

Full impact of the ₹92 crore knitting expansion (including 250 metric tonnes of additional knitted production and printing) expected in Q4 FY27, fully visible in Q1 FY28; project on track for December completion.
Revenue mix expected to shift toward roughly two-thirds yarn and one-third fabric from the current three-fourths/one-fourth split in Q1 FY28.
Standalone ROCE to improve from the current 6-6.5% level, 'this or slightly better', without a numerical target.
Standalone debt of ₹1,480 crore with ₹95 crore due in H1 FY27; annual repayment around ₹180 crore in FY28.
LNJ GreenPET (100% subsidiary, bottle-to-bottle recycling) expected to start commercial production in Q1 FY28 with about ₹200 crore revenue expected.
capex_capacity: Knitting expansion of ₹92 crore: printing and 250 metric tonnes of additional knitted production expected in Q4 FY27; project in line with timelines and cost.

LNJ GreenPET bottle-to-bottle project: commercial production expected Q1 FY28; about ₹62 crore RSWM equity, of which ₹29 crore already invested; ₹27 crore of a ₹36 crore preferential share issue from LNJ Textiles Advisory to go into bottle-to-bottle recycling.

LNJ NDS9 Global Private Limited (RSWM 74%, NDS9 26%): premium denim and knit garment manufacturing for international clients; Phase-1 investment ₹208 crore, RSWM equity about ₹46 crore; more than 12 months to complete, likely Q4 FY28 or Q1 FY29.
Management is focused on utilisation, especially in knitting and melange, and on automation and digitalisation.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices rose about ₹16,000 per candy (about ₹60/kg on cotton yarn); polyester rose from ₹96 to ₹146 over six months; gas, dyes, chemicals and freight also rose.
Order booking runs 30-40 days in knit and denim, so price increases lag cost increases; management said sale prices rose but not in line with costs.
Denim market described as good with fairly high utilisation; knit utilisation improved QoQ.
Export order flow was disrupted by West Asia tensions; apparel export demand slowed, while India's H1 textile exports grew moderately.
Management said price increases for next season are being negotiated with brands and domestic customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the fabric division (denim and knit) earning no meaningful profit for three quarters, with negative PBIT of ₹6 crore, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to cost push from cotton, polyester, gas and chemicals, with price pass-through lagging by 30-40 days of order booking. It said the issue is temporary, Q4 should be better, and Q1 FY28 looks brighter. It also noted that PBIT losses partly reflect interest and depreciation from new capex still ramping up.

qa_highlights.question: How much surplus cash is available and where will it be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow after interest will first repay current loans, then fund normal capex, and then equity in the two new projects: LNJ NDS9 and LNJ GreenPET.

qa_highlights.question: What is the equity outlay in LNJ NDS9 Phase-1 and LNJ GreenPET?
qa_highlights.answer: RSWM's share is about ₹46 crore in LNJ NDS9 (of ₹208 crore Phase-1) and about ₹62 crore in LNJ GreenPET, of which ₹29 crore is already invested.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental depreciation and interest came from new capex this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only interest has started; depreciation has not begun because the knitting project is not yet commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 profit came from one-off inventory or trading gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cotton trading gains from short-term price spikes are part of operations. Cotton yarn is less than one-fifth of turnover, and the company does not do speculative stocking.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric contribution and EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric was about 26% of Q2 revenue. Management targets double-digit EBITDA margins in fabric and said the group margin should be around or above 8.7% in the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt repayment schedule and the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone debt is ₹1,480 crore, with ₹95 crore due in H1 FY27 and around ₹180 crore in FY28. Management did not give a peak debt figure.

risks_watch: Fabric margins: cost pass-through lag in denim and knit; watch whether Q3 and Q4 price increases stick and whether fabric turns positive PBIT.
Execution of the ₹92 crore knitting expansion (December completion, Q4 output) and LNJ GreenPET start in Q1 FY28.
Input-cost volatility in cotton, polyester, gas and freight, plus West Asia disruption to export orders.
Exceptional item: ₹11.5 crore electricity duty provision on captive solar; ₹7.42 crore deposited under protest; SLP pending before the Supreme Court.
Quality of earnings: H1 PAT and other equity were helped by ₹181 crore fair-value gain in OCI on HEG-related equity, not operating income.
Capital allocation: equity commitments to LNJ NDS9 and LNJ GreenPET, plus ₹180 crore FY28 debt repayment, against ₹400-450 crore run-rate EBITDA as cited by an analyst.

500355|2026-03.headline: Rallis Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% to ₹456 cr and EBITDA moved to ₹-1 cr from ₹-19 cr; management expects 15-25% input cost inflation to be passed on.
500355|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹456 cr (up ~6% YoY), with volume growth of ~5% and pricing up ~1%. EBITDA improved to ₹-1 cr from ₹-19 cr and PAT to ₹-15 cr from ₹-32 cr, helped by better B2B exports, CSM and seeds margins. Management described a choppy year (early monsoon, post-September rain gap, short Rabi) and a shift in the industry toward a seller's market after the Middle East conflict. Management is passing through cost increases, calling 15-25% input cost inflation a reality for Kharif, and is guiding to seeds growth in the mid-teens.

financial_highlights.change: improved 96% vs ₹-19 cr in Q4 FY25
vs ₹-32 cr in Q4 FY25 (management cites 52% improvement)

financial_highlights.value: ₹3 cr profit on sale of Aurangabad land

segments.name: Domestic B2C
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹255 cr, up 15% from ₹222 cr on 14% volume growth, led by insecticides. FY26 B2C revenue ₹1,657 cr (+5%, 9% volume growth). Management cites FY26 herbicide +15%, fungicide +5%, insecticide -3%.

segments.name: Soil & Plant Health (within B2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹47 cr, up 27% from ₹37 cr on 29% volume growth, driven by micronutrients and biofertilisers. Management says SPH is roughly 20% of B2C sales.

segments.name: Seeds
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹31 cr, up 23% from ₹25 cr (8% volume, 15% price), led by cotton and millets. FY26 seeds revenue ₹481 cr (+15%).

segments.name: Exports (B2B)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹77 cr, down 33% from ₹114 cr on lower Metribuzin and Pendimethalin volumes. Management says Acephate supply is constrained because raw material suppliers compete in US markets.

segments.name: CSM (contract manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹66 cr, up 59% from ₹41 cr on both volume and price. Margin was helped by a contract clause that pays benefit if volumes fall below thresholds.

segments.name: B2B total
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹170 cr, down 7%; FY26 B2B revenue ₹759 cr (+14%) on volume, price and customer base growth.

guidance_outlook: Seeds: management expects high double-digit growth in FY27 on a combination of price and volume, clarified as mid-teens; cotton expected to grow fastest, then maize, rice and millet.
Crop protection: price increases of roughly 5-10% expected; revenue growth could be double-digit; margins described as stable to soft depending on competitor response.
Input costs have risen 15-25%; management says this is a reality for Kharif and will take 3-4 months to unwind even if the war ends.
Management is not building inventory beyond Kharif and will buy only what it can sell; Kharif raw material is largely secured.
Monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA; management says a total failure is unlikely and planting will happen regardless.
capex_capacity: Record production levels achieved through better manufacturing efficiency; FY26 annual capacity utilisation improved vs FY25.
Five ingredients produced in-house for crop protection; other inputs sourced from suppliers, with Kharif supply secured.
Seeds focus narrowed to five strategic crops: cotton, maize, millet, mustard and rice.
Inventory slightly elevated YoY at quarter end; Rallis built some low-cost raw material inventory ahead of the war.
Aquafeed is at an experimental stage with no investment size set; management wants one more year before deciding. Micronutrient business has reached ₹50 cr+ scale.
demand_pricing: Industry is moving from a buyers' market to a seller's market after the Iran war, with panic buying and hoarding reported. Glyphosate is up ~25%, and Glufosinate, Mancozeb, Metribuzin and other generic AIs have also risen.
Rabi was hit by unseasonal rain and hail on 2.49 lakh ha. Summer sowing is down 4.7% YoY as of end-March.
Management expects the sector to grow 3-4% in FY27 (this figure was later clarified to be GDP growth), with volumes possibly shrinking on lower acreage and margins stable to soft.

Price increases announced early; management sees a price increase on crop protection of 5-10%, with seed pricing rising for rice, maize and millet but flat for cotton (government did not raise cotton prices).
Competitive intensity: Clasto and Benzilla inventory was liquidated in Q4, compressing B2C gross margin on a standalone basis.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement in Q4 when the commentary was pessimistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSM margins were higher due to a volume-threshold clause and SPH, exports and seeds were better, while standalone crop protection margin fell because of Clasto and Benzilla inventory liquidation in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 B2C volume growth came from pre-placement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said placement was limited to normal levels; some low-cost inventory was held back for Q1 sales at higher prices. For FY26, herbicide was up 15%, fungicide 5% and insecticide down 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth and margin outlook for seeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects high double-digit growth, clarified as mid-teens, from price and volume. Dryer capacity constraints and paddy open-field drying raised costs, so margin outcome is still uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost increases and how much can be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs have risen 15-25%. Management has announced price increases, expects them to hold through Kharif, and says a 3-4 month unwind is needed even if the war ends.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the B2C growth came from SPH and what is core crop protection growth?
qa_highlights.answer: SPH grew 27%; excluding SPH, B2C crop protection growth is marginal, low single digit, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory risk if crude prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not hold excess inventory and is building only Kharif stock, with calibrated purchases to match expected sales.

risks_watch: Monsoon risk: IMD forecasts 92% of LPA with El Niño; management cites 5-10% demand cut risk for herbicides and insecticides under erratic rain.
Input cost inflation of 15-25% may compress downstream margins if prices cannot be passed on fully, and competitors' price responses are unknown.
Acephate export supply constrained by raw material suppliers who compete in US markets; exports fell 33% in Q4.
Seed margin uncertainty from dryer capacity constraints, incremental drying costs and possible lower recovery.
Kharif inventory costing and the state of the Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz remain open items.

500365|2026-09.headline: Welspun Specialty Q2 FY27 total income INR242 crores and EBITDA about INR4 crores; Tube volumes hit by weak export demand and EU duties.
500365|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was about INR242 crores on sales volume of about 8,800 metric tons, with reported EBITDA of about INR4 crores and cash PAT of about INR1 crores. H1 FY27 total income was about INR440 crores on about 15,000 tons, with EBITDA of about INR19 crores and cash PAT of about INR10 crores. Bar volumes grew about 20% YoY, while Tube volumes fell on weak European sentiment, delivery delays and higher energy and freight costs that only partly passed through to prices. Management says the Tube order book is about four months and the bid book about 10 months, with the company guiding to a delay of a couple of quarters on its 20-30% volume growth target.

segments.name: Bars
segments.commentary: Bar sales volume in Q2 grew about 20% YoY, driven mainly by higher market penetration. Management cited this as the reflection of its strategy.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Tube volumes were weak in Q2 due to sentiment, delayed contracts and delivery schedules. Closing order book is about four months of volume, mostly due for delivery in Q3 and Q4 FY27, with a large share of heat exchanger tubes; bid book is about 10 months or more.

segments.name: Piping
segments.commentary: Piping volumes declined sharply in Q2 YoY. Management attributed this to weak order booking and demand, not a deliberate choice to avoid low-margin volume. Analyst cited a 1.3 KMD-type historical benchmark; management said it was confident of a recovery in Q3 and Q4.

guidance_outlook: Management is still working toward the earlier 20-30% volume growth target, but said it may be delayed by a couple of quarters.
Near term expected to stay challenging due to high energy and freight costs, trade barriers and cautious customer sentiment.
Priorities: convert bid pipeline into firm orders, raise volumes and capacity utilisation, cost optimisation and working capital discipline.
No significant capex planned in FY27 or FY28 beyond minor maintenance capex, unless a specific opportunity arises.
Renewable energy expected to be about 67% of total energy use in FY27, up from 58% in FY26.
capex_capacity: No significant capex planned for FY27 and FY28 beyond minor maintenance; new investment only for a specific project opportunity.
Tube bid book about 10 months or more of volume, with most projects expected to be finalised in Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Long-length tubes up to 24 metres, moderator heat exchanger tubes for nuclear power and duplex finned tubes won in the period.
Received NPCIL approval for Moderator heat exchanger tubes after audit; new products include vacuum degassed stainless steel forging ingots and heavy-wall P91 tubes.
demand_pricing: EU safeguard and duty increases pushed average duty on stainless steel bars to Europe above 20%, from under 10% earlier; management said duty incidence now runs about 20-30%, making Indian exports uncompetitive versus EU mill prices.
Freight and energy costs rose sharply, raising raw material and scrap prices; selling prices passed through only partially, pressuring margins.
Domestic market described as growing with short-term demand gaps; management noted some oversupply and desperate selling in pockets.
Order book has more than 60-70% of volume from Middle East oil and gas fabricators; ADNOC approved the Pipes product, with Tubes approval expected soon.
24 new customers added in H1 FY27. Global stainless steel pipe and tube market about 0.5 million tons, growing 4-5% annually (excluding the last 1-2 disruptive years).

qa_highlights.question: How soon will ADNOC approval for Tubes follow the Pipes approval?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said applications were evaluated in parallel and expects Tube approval soon after the Pipe release, without visibility into ADNOC's internal timelines.

qa_highlights.question: What capital allocation is planned for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capex planned apart from minor maintenance, unless a specific project opportunity arises.

qa_highlights.question: How is domestic pricing competition and cannibalisation developing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed pressure to demand-supply mismatch, with dry spells creating some oversupply and desperate selling in pockets; expects this to ease with market improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to EU tariffs and any mitigation?
qa_highlights.answer: Company had already shifted to non-EU markets over three to four quarters; products differentiated from commodities retain some edge, but price pressure persists given weak demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Piping volumes decline so sharply in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said weak order booking and a scattered delivery schedule were the cause, not a choice to avoid low-margin business; expects improvement in Q3 and Q4, and confirmed confidence in a return to prior levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India competitive landscape in thermal power given piercing-route competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Some thermal OEM specifications require extrusion, and different owners set their own specs, so extrusion players retain a significant opportunity. Government revised its thermal plan from 90 GW to 150 GW by 2035.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TAM per gigawatt of thermal capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3,500-4,000 tons per GW, including about 3,000 tons of boiler tubes and about 500 tons of non-boiler seamless tubes.

risks_watch: Tube order book conversion and whether Q3-Q4 deliveries of heat exchanger tubes are met on time.
Further EU safeguard or duty changes, and whether the stated 20-30% duty incidence persists.
Continued margin pressure from energy and freight costs that are only partly passed through.
Timing of ADNOC Tube approval and SIRIM audit in November for Malaysia.
Domestic pricing pressure and oversupply in pockets; Middle East order conversion pace.
500365|2026-09.management_tone: Cautious on the near term: management repeatedly cited weak demand, duties, freight costs and a Tube setback, but stayed confident on the Indian market, the bid book and approvals. Answers on the 20-30% growth target and Tube timelines were hedged with phrases like "maybe that gets delayed by a couple of quarters."
key_quotes: Our Tube bid book is healthy at about 10 months of volume or more, and most of these projects are due to be finalized this quarter or the next.
The first half of financial year '27 has tested us and the wider industry.
So whatever quantity was going out of the market into the EU is also going to now choke, you can say, our market.

rows.why: ADNOC approved the Pipes product and Tube approval is expected soon after, but there is no visibility into ADNOC's internal timelines; Middle East fabricators are over 60-70% of the order book.

rows.why: Management noted oversupply and desperate selling in pockets and expects easing with market improvement, so pricing pressure may persist in the near term.

tone.note: Management was cautious on the near term, citing EU duties of 20-30%, freight and energy costs, and the Tube setback, but confident in the Indian market, the bid book and approvals; analysts pushed on the Piping volume decline and the 20-30% growth target timing.

500368|2026-03.headline: Patanjali Foods Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR11,156 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.48% and FY27 guidance points to 12-15% blended EBITDA growth.
500368|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue from operations at INR11,155.60 crore, with EBITDA excluding exceptional items of INR501.96 crore (4.48% margin) and PBT of INR235.69 crore (2.10% margin). FY26, the first full year after the HPC business integration, delivered revenue of INR40,169.58 crore, crossing the INR40,000 crore mark, with EBITDA of INR1,931.52 crore (4.79%). Edible oil and FMCG grew double digits, while staples (rice) and ghee softened sequentially in Q4. Management flagged a sharp crude-linked edible oil price spike from March 2026 and a further rise in April, which it expects to be beneficial to large players in the near term.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR8,324 crore (+23.28% YoY), EBITDA margin 2.58%; branded oil about 75% of edible oil sales. Edible oil volume 20.3 lakh tonnes vs 18.84 lakh tonnes last year; aggregate segment volume 25.1 lakh tonnes vs 23.64 lakh tonnes.

segments.name: FMCG (Foods + HPC)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR2,890 crore (25.76% of revenue) with 57.62% of EBITDA; FY26 revenue INR11,188 crore (+19.95%), EBITDA margin 10.81%.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR477.89 crore (+13.97% YoY), slightly down QoQ from INR490 crore in Q3; FY26 INR1,907.81 crore (+15.9%), highest ever. Doodh biscuits FY26 turnover over INR1,300 crore vs INR1,000 crore in FY25. Q4 EBITDA INR65 crore.

segments.name: Staples and ghee
segments.commentary: Staples Q4 revenue INR848.83 crore, FY26 INR3,658 crore; sequential drop of about INR407 crore driven mainly by rice. Ghee Q4 INR338.91 crore, FY26 INR1,423.86 crore; ghee sales fell about INR129 crore on early-summer and Middle East disruption. Staples Q4 EBITDA INR5.46 crore.

segments.name: Ethnic foods (Foods business)
segments.commentary: Foods business Q4 EBITDA INR72 crore combined, of which ethnic foods INR66 crore and staples INR5.46 crore. Mid-teens YoY decline was flagged by an analyst; management did not dispute the figure.

segments.name: Nutrela (soya/textured)
segments.commentary: Nutrela Q4 revenue INR106 crore, FY26 INR527 crore; Q4 EBITDA INR16.85 crore. Textured soya FY26 revenue INR526.78 crore.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR17.94 crore, FY26 INR58 crore after portfolio rationalisation; Q4 EBITDA INR2 crore.

segments.name: Home and Personal Care (HPC)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR840.50 crore (+35.42% YoY), EBITDA INR136 crore. Dental INR425.97 crore in Q4 and INR1,412.80 crore in FY26; skin care INR239.75 crore in Q4 (+57.66% YoY), FY26 INR680 crore; home care INR97.82 crore in Q4, FY26 INR331.88 crore.

segments.name: Oil palm plantation
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,793 crore and EBITDA INR357 crore vs INR203 crore prior year, helped by maturing plantations and higher palm oil prices. Cultivated area 1,10,722 hectares as of 31 March 2026, +23.65% YoY; about 38% in the 7-25 year prime yielding phase.

guidance_outlook: Edible oil volume growth of about 3-5% in FY27, in line with expected national consumption growth; management said it is slightly below 4%.
Foods portfolio revenue growth of 8-10% on a blended basis in FY27, with Foods margins expected to recover to about 10% after FY26 softness.
HPC revenue growth target of about 15% in FY27, with EBITDA margin near or above 18%, about 200 bps better than under the parent.
Blended EBITDA growth of 12-15% expected in FY27.
Edible oil EBITDA maintained in a 2-4% range despite near-term price volatility.
Q1 and Q2 FY27 expected to be very positive for edible oil and oilseed crushing, given Indonesian export-centralisation disruption.
Biscuit target of high double-digit growth, with Q1 FY27 expected to show a substantial uptick from INR478 crore in Q4 FY26.
capex_capacity: Oil palm cultivated area 1,10,722 hectares at 31 March 2026, +23.65% YoY and +2,558 hectares QoQ; total allocated area 6.63 lakh hectares.
Oil palm production fell in Q4 FY26 due to seasonality, while maturing plantations are expected to drive volume growth.
No new capex or commissioning timelines were given in the call.
demand_pricing: Palm, soyabean and sunflower oil prices rose about 20%, 23% and 22% respectively between January and March 2026 (RBD palm, refined soy and sunflower, per prepared remarks); April 2026 YoY increases were palm 15%, soybean 17%, sunflower 22%.
Consumer shift toward mustard oil observed as palm-linked prices rose; mustard, groundnut and cottonseed are domestic oils.
Edible oil price hikes were passed through almost daily; management said prices rose 10-15% (about 14% overall) and that its prices moved in line with the market.
Staples and ghee price hikes of 2-5% taken; ethnic foods other than ghee largely not repriced. Pulses and rice also repriced.
Cost of goods sold rose 98 bps QoQ and 294 bps YoY in Q4 FY26, with pressure from packaging, freight and insurance after mid-March.
Receivable days rose; INR700-800 crore of extra credit extended to customers. Advances paid to vendors for raw material security raised borrowings.
Rice category demand declined substantially through FY26; drought/El Nino and government policy risks flagged for staples.
Retail inflation 3.4% in March 2026 vs 3.21% in February 2026.

Low tax charge: tax netted against refunds of INR788 crore in FY26, including INR330 crore in Q4

qa_highlights.question: Biscuit category growth in Q4 FY26, whether it met expectations, and how the category is shaping up in April-May.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said biscuit growth was roughly 13% YoY (initially said over 15%, later corrected) and a marginal sequential dip from INR490 crore in Q3 to INR478 crore in Q4, attributed to seasonality and consumption disruption. Target remains high double-digit growth; Q1 FY27 expected to show a substantial uptick from INR478 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Foods revenue fall mid-teens YoY in Q4, and was there a one-off in the low tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Rice demand fell substantially through FY26, and ghee sales dropped about INR129 crore on early summer onset and Middle East disruption. Q4 tax was low because the company netted earlier-year refunds of INR788 crore in FY26, including INR330 crore in Q4, against current tax demand following post-CIRP assessment.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA for the quarter (Foods, biscuits, nutraceuticals, Nutrela, HPC).
qa_highlights.answer: Foods combined EBITDA INR72 crore (ethnic foods INR66 crore, staples INR5.46 crore); biscuits INR65 crore; nutraceuticals INR2 crore; Nutrela INR16.85 crore; HPC INR136 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Edible oil volumes for Q4 and FY26, and price hikes taken.
qa_highlights.answer: Edible oil volume 20.3 lakh tonnes vs 18.84 lakh tonnes; aggregate segment volume 25.1 lakh vs 23.64 lakh tonnes. Edible oil volume rose about 80,000 tonnes Q3 to Q4 and 1.5 lakh tonnes over FY25 to FY26. Oil price increases of 10-15% (about 14%) were passed through almost daily; staples up 2-5%, ghee repriced, other ethnic foods largely not repriced.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and higher borrowings: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra customer credit of about INR700-800 crore was extended amid market conditions, and advances were paid to vendors to secure raw materials, raising borrowings. Management aims to collect receivables within one to two quarters and return to cash procurement if geopolitics permit.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 guidance for edible oil volume, Foods and HPC revenue and margins, and blended EBITDA.
qa_highlights.answer: Edible oil volume growth 3-5%, slightly below 4%. Foods revenue growth 8-10% blended, with Foods margin recovering to about 10%. HPC revenue growth about 15% with EBITDA margin 18%-plus, about 200 bps better than under the parent. Blended EBITDA growth 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Near-term impact of Indonesian palm oil export centralisation on edible oil revenue and margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the disruption to private trade creates short-term volatility but benefits large players holding inventory; Q1 and Q2 FY27 expected to be very positive for edible oil and oilseed crushing. Volume growth still tracks national consumption of about 3-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Palm oil plantation EBITDA for Q4 and FY26.
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 plantation revenue INR1,793 crore and EBITDA INR357 crore, vs INR203 crore prior year (a prior-year figure of INR1,262 crore was also cited, apparently a revenue number). Drivers: maturing plantations and higher palm oil prices.

risks_watch: Crude-linked edible oil price volatility and Indonesian export centralisation; management expects Q1-Q2 FY27 to benefit but the pass-through pattern and margin outcome are unproven.
Edible oil EBITDA margin of 2.58% in Q4 and FY26 against a 2-4% target range; consumer shift toward mustard oil could affect branded mix.
Foods weakness: rice demand decline, drought/El Nino and government policy risk for staples; ghee softness linked to Middle East disruption.
Working capital stress: receivable days up with INR700-800 crore extra credit to customers and higher borrowings from vendor advances; collection timeline is one to two quarters.
Biscuit growth slowed to about 13% YoY from over 15% in Q3 (per management correction); watch whether Q1 FY27 shows the promised uptick.
Low Q4 tax charge due to refunds of INR788 crore; PBT margin of 2.10% in Q4 means reported profit quality depends on one-time refund adjustments.

I think we should see a good growth of anywhere between 12% to 15% growth for the next year.
But overall, the target that we continue to place for ourselves is upwards in high double digits.
Crude-linked volatility remains elevated, which would make the operating environment increasingly challenging for smaller and unorganized players.
