rows.why: INR700-800 crore of extra customer credit and vendor advances raised borrowings; management aims to collect within one to two quarters and return to cash procurement.

500368|2026-06.headline: Patanjali Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to INR11,337 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR543 crore (4.80% margin).
500368|2026-06.overview: Management reported the fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue, led by edible oils (INR8,505 crore, record) and oil palm (INR740 crore, up 25% YoY). FMCG revenue was INR2,938 crore at a 6.45% EBITDA margin, with biscuits and HPC growing strongly while staples were loss-making at INR-59 crore EBITDA. Input inflation from delayed monsoon and West Asia conflict was a net positive for edible oils (long positions) but a headwind for FMCG. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, while flagging caution on staples demand and margins.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8,505 crore, record, led by mustard oil; EBITDA margin 5.22%. Veg oil inflation helped as the company is long edible oils.

segments.name: Oil palm plantation
segments.commentary: Revenue INR740 crore, up 25% YoY. Cultivated area 1,15,861 ha as of 30 June 2026 against 6.63 lakh ha allocated; about 37% in the 7-25 year prime yielding phase.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Revenue INR560 crore, up 27% YoY, EBITDA margin 15.35% vs 9.35%. Doodh Biscuit (INR5 and INR10 packs) is cited at about INR1,300 crore annual business.

segments.name: Textured soya (Nutrela)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR160 crore, up 14% YoY and 50% QoQ, EBITDA margin above 18%. Management cites about 40% market share.

segments.name: Ghee
segments.commentary: Revenue INR219 crore, softer on seasonal demand and lower Middle East off-take amid geopolitical disruption.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Revenue INR38 crore, helped by extended summer and launches of mango chutney, mango panna juice and orange juice.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR18 crore; management says the segment has turned EBITDA-positive from earlier marginal losses, with sports nutrition gaining momentum.

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Revenue INR629 crore: dental INR325 crore, skin care INR165 crore, home care INR83 crore, hair care and others INR56 crore. Skin care was the main growth driver.

segments.name: Staples and ethnic foods
segments.commentary: Staples revenue above INR1,000 crore with EBITDA of INR-59 crore; ethnic foods (honey, dry fruits, spices, herbal etc.) revenue INR203 crore with EBITDA INR9 crore.

guidance_outlook: Full-year edible oil volume growth of 3% to 5%, with edible oil margin construct of 3% to 5% (also cited as 2% to 4% later in the call).
Food and FMCG growth of 8% to 10%; beauty and personal care growing around 15%.
FMCG vertical EBITDA growth of 12% to 15% for the year; later described as 10% to 12% EBITDA growth overall.
Textured soya margin guided at 16% to 18%, with management expecting to stay above 18%.
FMCG revenue expected to reach about INR12,500 crore this year from about INR11,000 crore+ last year (CEO estimate).
Oil palm business expected to grow more than 15% this year.
Management aims for EBITDA of about INR2,500 crore over the next 18 months on an annualised basis (CEO view, not formal guidance).
E-commerce and quick commerce plus modern trade targeted to rise from about 15% to 20% of revenue within 18 months.
capex_capacity: Oil palm cultivated area 1,15,861 ha as of 30 June 2026 out of 6.63 lakh ha allocated under the National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm.
No capex or new capacity figures were discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Foods volume grew about 5% YoY and pricing about 12% (management corrected an earlier approximation of 7-8% volume growth).
Calibrated price increases taken in edible oils; targeted discounts in FMCG; smaller pack sizes introduced. Pricing measures continue in Q2.
Palm oil prices firmed from March 2026, eased late in the quarter, then recovered to a two-week high in mid-August; rupee depreciated about 2.5%.
Soya oil futures rose about 40% by end-March, then stabilised; FOB prices corrected 6%.
Milk and sugar prices firmed; wheat stable. Packaging, freight and logistics costs rose in the quarter.
Management cautious on staples: El Nino food inflation uncertainty and rural demand stress; staples expected to see the most rural pressure in Q2.
Dishwash: management says no plans to exit or slow down, with variant launches continuing as the MNC exits.

financial_highlights.change: About 26% of revenue and about 30% of EBITDA excl. unallocable income

financial_highlights.value: INR629 crore revenue; EBITDA INR122 crore

qa_highlights.question: Given a large MNC temporarily exiting dishwash and Godrej Consumer reportedly exiting liquid dishwash, is there a big opportunity for Patanjali in the segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no intention to exit or slow down dishwash, variants will keep launching, and the market is expanding. It did not have the dishwash-specific number to hand and offered to share it after the call.

qa_highlights.question: With competitors' odd-price biscuits (INR4.5, INR9) now largely gone, how does this affect growth for the market leader and Patanjali?
qa_highlights.answer: Doodh Biscuit (INR5 and INR10 packs) is cited at almost INR1,300 crore annual business. Biscuit EBITDA margin was nearly 15% in the quarter, with management committed to INR5 and INR10 price points and adding premium variants such as Almond and Chyawanprash cookies.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management more cautious on staples than peers, and what price hikes were taken by category?
qa_highlights.answer: Caution rests on El Nino food inflation uncertainty and rural income and demand stress, plus pending policy on commodity control orders. Management stayed positive on top-line growth and reaffirmed staples/food growth of 8% to 10%; it did not give category-wise price hike details in this answer.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the foods recovery across ethnic foods and staples?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to inflation-driven buoyancy, sequential staples revenue growth of about INR260 crore (about 30%), and focus on niche items like Kesar and rice, plus new lentil and besan variants. Ethnic foods had seen some contraction, and margins are lower in this business.

qa_highlights.question: What were the volume and pricing split for foods, and the EBITDA for ethnic foods, HPC and staples?
qa_highlights.answer: Foods volume grew about 5% YoY and pricing about 12%, correcting an earlier 7-8% volume estimate. EBITDA was INR9 crore for ethnic foods, INR122 crore for HPC, and negative INR59 crore for staples.

qa_highlights.question: Is TSP (Nutrela) margin resilient when soya and food inflation rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged TSP typically does less well in high commodity inflation because pass-through is limited, and the space is hyper-competitive. It still reaffirmed a 16% to 18% margin for the year, with Q1 above 18% on INR160 crore revenue and about 40% market share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the structural drivers beyond FY27, and what is the target EBITDA path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited oil palm growth of more than 15% this year, margin expansion in HPC, Nutrela and biscuits, and edible oil margins moving from 2-4% toward 5%-plus. It cited a CEO view of moving toward about INR2,500 crore EBITDA over the next 18 months on an annualised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Did the acquisition of the HPC business from Patanjali Ayurved (INR1,100 crore) get overpaid, and what is the valuation basis?

The CFO said the details were disclosed to the exchanges and approved by shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 profit growth (84% YoY, as cited by the analyst) be sustained for Q2 to Q4?

500368|2026-09.headline: Patanjali Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR11,323 crores, but operating EBITDA margin fell to 3.76% on edible oil pressure.
500368|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue from operations reached a record INR11,323 crores in Q2 FY27, up 16% YoY, with operating EBITDA of INR426 crores (3.76%) and PBT of INR409 crores (3.59%). H1 revenue was INR22,660 crores (up 22%), with EBITDA of INR969 crores (4.28%). Edible oil drove growth, with revenue up 22% to a record INR8,532 crores but margin at 3%, while the food staples and ethnic foods businesses were weak and management chose to de-grow staples. Management flagged softer rural demand, rising inflation (CPI 6.09% in October) and a later festive calendar, and said the festive season has since gained momentum.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR8,532 crores (record, up 22% YoY) at 3% EBITDA margin; H1 revenue INR17,037 crores (up 25%) at 4.11% margin. Volume growth about 3.9% in Q2 per management correction; H1 volume 11.07 lakh tons (corrected), up about 10.5%.

segments.name: Oil palm plantation
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR742 crores. Cultivated area 1,27,265 ha out of 6.63 lakh ha allocated; about 34% of area in prime yielding phase, about 8% young, about 57% immature.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR638 crores (up 28% YoY), EBITDA margin 11.91%; H1 revenue INR1,198 crores (up 28%), margin 13.52%. Volume about 56,122 tons vs 49,874 tons in Q1 (up 12.53% per correction); growth mainly volume-led, Doodh biscuits about 85% of portfolio.

segments.name: Staples (food)
segments.commentary: Revenue cut to INR838 crores from INR1,110 crores in Q1 as a deliberate de-growth; EBITDA INR15.61 crores (1.86%) vs negative INR59 crores in Q1.

segments.name: Ethnic foods (Nutrela)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR525 crores (up about 14% QoQ from INR460 crores); EBITDA INR16.78 crores (3.19%) vs 1.89% in Q1, still below management's 8-10% food margin target.

segments.name: Skincare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR187 crores in Q2 (corrected from INR188 crores), up about 25.6% YoY and 13.8% QoQ, almost entirely volume-led.

segments.name: Dental care (Dant Kanti)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR378 crores, up about 16% QoQ from INR325 crores in Q1 and about 4.5% YoY (corrected); H1 dental INR704 crores, up 9%.

segments.name: Textured soya
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR186 crores, volume growth 16% YoY; H1 INR345 crores (up 15%).

segments.name: Ghee
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR306 crores; H1 INR525 crores. Management expects demand to strengthen through winter and wedding season.

Inorganic opportunities are being evaluated selectively; nothing currently in pipeline for near-term investment.

qa_highlights.question: Has competitive intensity in toothpaste and biscuits changed over the last few quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Dental competition has intensified on launches, pricing and variants. Dant Kanti grew to INR378 crores in Q2 from INR325 crores in Q1 (about 16%), and management said the brand is competitive due to new toothbrush and variant extensions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering inorganic acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating selectively for distribution or portfolio gaps, but seller price expectations have been too high; nothing is on the cards for near-term investment.

qa_highlights.question: Volume versus price split for biscuits, skincare and edible oil?
qa_highlights.answer: Biscuits are largely volume-led with no price increase, about 80-85% Doodh biscuits. Edible oil volume grew about 3.9% with the rest from price; skincare is mostly volume-led, up 25.6% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why are staples and ethnic foods declining?
qa_highlights.answer: Management chose to de-grow staples to protect margin (revenue INR838 crores, EBITDA 1.86%). Ethnic foods grew to INR525 crores with margin 3.19%, and management expects margins to improve from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Any inventory loss from the edible oil duty cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact was marginal and fully booked in the quarter, as material was in bonded warehouses or afloat; the EBITDA drop from 5.22% to 3% reflected the duty change.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the lease transfer from Patanjali Ayurved for the Indore land at INR185 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: The Indore plant is being relocated because the land is now residential. The lease premium is paid to the parent, which paid MPSIDC earlier, and rental is minimal; treasury income impact is expected to be small.

Intensifying dental competition, with the leader and others raising launches and pricing.
Edible oil pack-size standardisation (three-month transition) could affect demand; management says no financial impact.
Corrections to several figures in the call (Q2 edible oil volume, Q1 volume, biscuit growth) suggest disclosure accuracy to verify against the filed data.

500378|2026-03.headline: Jindal Saw Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA fell to INR413 crore and PAT to INR114 crore, with export shipments suspended since March 2026 due to MENA conflict.
500378|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 weakened versus Q3 on both standalone and consolidated bases, missing management's prior guidance that Q4 would beat Q3. Standalone EBITDA was INR413 crore (Q3: INR527 crore) and PAT was INR114 crore (Q3: INR227 crore), while FY26 standalone EBITDA fell 47% and PAT fell 58% year on year. Management attributed the drop to weak ductile iron pipe demand from slow Jal Jeevan Mission execution, suspended exports from March 1, 2026 after MENA force majeure, a INR48 crore forex loss, and an API monogram suspension on seamless pipes. Net debt declined, with standalone net debt at INR2,453 crore. Management guided that Q1 FY27 will also be affected.

Capex guidance: INR500-600 crore in FY27 across Indian sites, then INR400-500 crore in FY28, mainly debottlenecking and replacement, with no major new Indian greenfield or brownfield plant.
Management expects the Jal Jeevan Mission momentum to pick up, with execution possibly starting post-monsoon; the timing was described as uncertain.
Management declined to say whether margins have bottomed, citing freight, crude and inflation uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Abu Dhabi seamless carbon pipe plant (subsidiary, 100% owned): land with fuel infrastructure secured, equipment ordering and LCs under way, long-term land lease signed with AD Ports; debt-equity and project cost still being revised.

Management says Abu Dhabi and Saudi projects will be fast-tracked; Saudi's net balance-sheet impact is lower given the 51% stake.
Capex spent in FY25-26 was about INR800 crore; roughly 10 Indian locations, with recent spending mostly on debottlenecking, efficiency and staff infrastructure.
Management says India's DI capacity is in oversupply and it will work with existing capacity, with options such as product mix shifts and export and domestic shifts for ductile lines.
demand_pricing: Water (DI) demand deferred, not lost, per management. Work is now mostly state-funded orders via EPCs, which are priced differently from older Jal Jeevan orders.

Management expects new pipeline demand from MENA energy-security shifts, India's gas pipeline fast-track order (March 2026), and ONGC deepwater projects of about $20 billion. Domestic seamless demand is about 1.5 million tonnes per management.
Steel is bought only against firm orders, so raw-material swings fall on the manufacturer; most international sales are on a delivered basis, so freight and diesel costs hit margins.
Ductile pricing has a pig-iron-linked escalation clause, covering roughly 30-35% of contracts and mainly the domestic market; some states also have escalation clauses.

Competition is rising in Saudi, with local factories being set up by rivals. Management expects imports to continue to serve most Saudi demand for about a year, and says its own plants are fully booked for a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there DI overcapacity, and will utilisation and margins recover quickly?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Goyal said DI pipes have oversupply, while longitudinal, helical and seamless capacity is adequate for demand. DI utilisation will stay low until Jal Jeevan Mission gets going.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost to the Middle East disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a deferment, not a loss. About 30,000-40,000 tonnes were ready for shipment; the value is above INR30-40 crore, according to management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the seamless and stainless steel margin going to improve, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects seamless margins to improve as demand stays robust, and stainless steel to benefit from upper-end approvals, with impact in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new order intake strategy in helical SAW, and does the industry have capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is fully booked for a couple of quarters and will not take immediate low-margin domestic orders. It says the export order book will return once shipping normalises.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone long-term debt is about INR525 crore and consolidated about INR650 crore, and the balance sheet can take more debt. It said debt/EBITDA including working capital could reach 2-2.5x if EBITDA returns to about INR3,500 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the escalation pass-through is mainly pig-iron linked and domestic, with coal stocks held and shipped quarterly. DI execution is shifting to state-backed orders, and Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 execution is expected to take a month or two to start.

500378|2026-09.headline: Jindal Saw Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT fell to INR35 crores (from INR91 crores in Q1) as EBITDA dropped to INR312 crores on MENA disruption and water-segment softness.
500378|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 0.8% QoQ to INR4,523 crores and 6% YoY, but EBITDA fell to INR312 crores from INR420 crores in Q1, and PAT fell to INR35 crores including a INR27 crore tax credit. Management attributed the weakness to delayed Saudi job-work shipments, logistics cost inflation, coking coal costs in DI pipes, low utilisation in water pipes, Abu Dhabi DI plant underutilisation, and pellet margin pressure. Standalone net debt declined to INR2,245 crores from INR2,346 crores. Management guided H2 to be better than H1, with margins expected to move toward double digits from Q3/Q4 as oil and gas orders ramp.

500387|2026-03.headline: Shree Cement Q4 FY26 domestic volume rose 11% YoY to 10.56 Mt; EBITDA/ton up to INR1,125 with utilisation at 66%.

500387|2026-06.headline: Shree Cement Q1 FY27 consol operational EBITDA fell to INR1,272 crore (1,111/t vs 1,339/t) on volume of 114.5 lakh t, as fuel switch and lower clinker factor hit costs.
500387|2026-06.overview: Management asked analysts to shift to consolidated reporting (India plus UAE and other subsidiaries), citing ~10% of turnover from overseas and non-standalone businesses. Q1 was hit by the Middle East war: petcoke share fell from 54% to 9% and coal rose to 81% from 32%, while Omani gypsum did not arrive, raising fuel cost to about INR1.95/kcal and lowering the clinker conversion factor to 1.50 from 1.58. Trade mix fell to 62% from 71% and blended to 60% from 70%, which management attributes to a weaker conversion factor pushing more OPC into non-trade. Management says fuel cost has peaked and guides to better Q2 onwards, with FY27 volume target of 40 million tonnes reiterated.

segments.name: India grey cement (standalone)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation 62% overall (North 66%, East 60%, South 57%), flat YoY on a larger base. South sales rose from 11 lakh t to ~16.9 lakh t, North grew ~20%, East was flat; Q1 India volume about 10.4-10.5 million t.

segments.name: UAE (Ras Al Khaimah)
segments.commentary: No meaningful sales in April and May due to the war, which dragged consolidated volume. Capacity doubling is underway to about 7 million t by Q3 FY27, funded from UAE cash; management declined to disclose UAE EBITDA or revenue.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: 26 operational plants versus 19 at start of year, with 8 added in Q1 and 10 more planned next quarter. Management says RMC is EBITDA-neutral at present, targeting about 5% margin over time.

segments.name: Northeast (Assam/Meghalaya) greenfield
segments.commentary: Plant planned for Q4 FY28 with 1 million t first phase and infrastructure for 4-5 million t; management says all approvals are in place.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target maintained at 40 million t (India); H1 FY27 expected at about 19.5-20 million t (Q1 about 10.4-10.5 million t, Q2 guided at 9-9.5 million t).

Trade/non-trade mix expected to normalise gradually; long-term aim is 70% trade, 30% non-trade, with conversion factor recovery as the lever.

Standalone share of consolidated revenue expected to fall from 88-89% to 75-80% over about five years.
capex_capacity: India capex of INR456 crore in Q1 FY27 against full-year guidance of about INR1,500 crore.

Northeast greenfield plant to commission in Q4 FY28: 1 million t initial phase, site built for 4-5 million t; limestone available in region.

Sales push into Maharashtra and Gujarat, served by the South plant.

qa_highlights.question: What were blended fuel cost, trade mix, clinker factor and realisation in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel cost INR1.95/kcal; trade mix 62% (vs 71%), blended 60% (vs 70%); clinker factor 1.50 (vs 1.58); realisation INR4,919/t vs INR4,854/t a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 fuel cost rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects fuel cost to be broadly flat at INR1.95/kcal, with at most a INR0.02-0.03 increase, provided Middle East stays calm.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the mix shift to non-trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower-quality coal raised clinker ash absorption and cut the conversion factor, leaving more OPC, which sells mainly into non-trade. Management expects normalisation over time, not a permanent change.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR200 crore non-standalone EBITDA comes from UAE, and what are UAE EBITDA/revenue per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split EBITDA or revenue for UAE or other subsidiaries and asked analysts to model consolidated figures only.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Northeast plant economics given capex per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR1,800 crore figure relates to 1 million t of a 4-5 million t site, not a standalone 1 million t project, and that it will proceed in learning steps.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inorganic growth plan given net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it is not pursuing acquisitions and will not buy capacity at about $110/t capex for $5 EBITDA/t assets.

500387|2026-09.headline: Shree Cement Q2 FY27 India volumes rose 18% YoY to 9.31 mt, but consol EBITDA/ton fell to INR966 on higher fuel cost.
500387|2026-09.overview: India sales volume grew about 18% YoY to 9.31 million tonnes, with realisation up 1% to INR4,870 per tonne. Consolidated EBITDA rose about 4% YoY to INR1,016 crore, but EBITDA per tonne fell to INR966 from INR1,055, mainly due to higher fuel cost (landed cost INR2.09 per kcal vs INR1.66 a year ago). Sequentially, volumes fell 11% in India and consolidated EBITDA dropped from INR1,272 crore on seasonality, West Asia conflict and weak monsoon. Management reiterated 40-41 million tonne India volume guidance for FY27 and an 80 million tonne capacity target.

500400|2026-03.headline: Tata Power Q4 FY26 PAT rose 8% to INR1,416 crores and FY26 PAT topped INR5,000 crores, with FY27 capex guided at about INR25,000 crores.
500400|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 EBITDA up about 10% to INR4,216 crores and PAT up 8% to INR1,416 crores, with full-year EBITDA up about 11% to INR16,090 crores and PAT above INR5,000 crores for the first time. Mundra was offline for nine months, and its SPPA with Gujarat is now signed, with four other states expected to follow in 4 to 6 weeks. FY26 capex came in well below the earlier guidance as transmission and right-of-way delays pushed projects out of the quarter. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR25,000 crores and about 2.5 GW of renewable commissioning, with roughly half of the 5 GW under-implementation pipeline due in FY27 and the rest by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the regulatory asset wind-down in Delhi is progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator has committed in an affidavit to amortise the regulatory assets over six years up to 2032, which is under monitoring by the Supreme Court and APTEL.

qa_highlights.question: Will Tata Power sacrifice coal profitability under the Gujarat SPPA, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said details will be shared once all five procurers sign, with no quantification given at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 5 GW renewable pipeline represent installed or contracted capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is on installed capacity; contracted capacity is lower (about 1,200 MW for FDRE and hybrid wind per the slide cited by the analyst).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR250 crore deferred tax asset and the Q4 PAT lifts at IEL and Mumbai Transmission?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the deferred tax was recognised in Q4 based on better profit visibility and carry-forward losses. IEL uplift was from a plant commissioning; Mumbai Transmission's recurring uplift is from about INR1,000 crores of annual capex.

risks_watch: FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crores is nearly double FY26 actual; slippage risk from transmission and right-of-way delays has already caused one shortfall.
Regulatory prior-period gains (INR783 crores in FY26) are lumpy and hard to forecast, so FY27 reported Delhi distribution profit could fall.
Four remaining Mundra SPPAs (states other than Gujarat) are not yet signed; billing is under Section 11 pending approvals.
Curtailment on solar projects and temporary GNA issues could hold back commissioning and PLF.
Coal monetisation remains open; management said a sale depends on valuation and signing all SPPAs.
Net debt to underlying EBITDA of 3.3x with a large capex programme; management says leverage discipline will be maintained.
Possible Indonesian coal export duty or royalty changes; coal cost is a pass-through under the SPPA.

key_quotes: We have now concluded the SPPA with Gujarat, and we are in the process of finalizing it with all the other 4 states, which we expect in next 4 to 6 weeks, we will complete.

500400|2026-06.headline: Tata Power Q1 FY27 PAT rose 11% to INR 1,401 crore and EBITDA 8% to INR 4,249 crore, the 27th straight quarter of growth.
500400|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 1,401 crore (+11%) and EBITDA of INR 4,249 crore (+8%), with revenue also up. Q1 capex was INR 5,300 crore, a first, against a FY27 plan of INR 25,000 crore. Odisha DISCOM collections were delayed by government payment timing and a heatwave-related disconnection pause, which management says is timing-related. Renewable capacity additions were 226 MW in Q1, with about 500 MW near commissioning and a FY27 target of 2,500-2,700 MW, taking installed capacity past 9 GW.

financial_highlights.change: first time quarterly spend at this level

financial_highlights.metric: Rooftop revenue (Q1, per analyst calculation from slides)
financial_highlights.change: revenue roughly doubled YoY per management

segments.name: Renewables (generation)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 6.7 GW, with 2.5 GW to be added in FY27 and capacity expected to cross 9 GW by year-end. Q1 commissioning was 226 MW; 500 MW is described as ready within weeks, with Q2 commissioning of 800-900 MW targeted.

segments.name: Rooftop solar
segments.commentary: Management guides to 60-70% growth this year. Q1 revenue was about INR 1,350 crore on 371 MW installed, and Mundra-style battery storage is being added. Management says cumulative rooftop revenue could reach INR 30,000 crore by 2029.

segments.name: Transmission (Mumbai and TBCB)
segments.commentary: Mumbai transmission has about INR 10,000 crore of regulated investment over five years. Two TBCB projects are near commissioning (Jalpura-Khurja now, Bikaner-Neemrana by October); TBCB revenue so far is construction-revenue booking, not line-by-line EBITDA.

segments.name: Distribution (Odisha and Delhi)
segments.commentary: Odisha PAT grew about 6% and units sold rose 10.4%, but collections were delayed by government payments, the heatwave disconnection pause and billing lag. Management says the DISCOM should be judged on a 12-month basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing (TP Solar)
segments.commentary: Module output crossed 1,000 MW in Q1 for the first time, while cell output fell after a line change. Margins are around 25-26%, and management expects yield and efficiency to peak in Q2.

segments.name: Tata Projects / solar EPC
segments.commentary: Third-party solar EPC has been discontinued and no new orders are being booked; remaining legacy projects are in final stages, and losses were booked in Q1. Management expects one more quarter of impact.

segments.name: Mundra (coal and power)
segments.commentary: Mundra's PAT rose on a higher share of coal profits, while EBITDA fell. The plant runs under a supplementary PPA on cost-reflective terms with no equity return. The state cabinet approvals are expected in August-September.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Odisha DISCOM growth muted, and why did Tata Projects losses widen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited delayed government payments for drinking water and street lighting, a heatwave-driven pause in disconnections until 15 June, and billing lag. It expects a recovery in Q2. Tata Projects is closing legacy loss-making projects, with about 10% in the final stage and one more quarter of impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Can curtailment losses be quantified, and when will transmission bottlenecks ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment across the industry was about 5% in Q1, which management says should settle over the next few quarters as evacuation lines are completed. Q2 commissioning should ramp up with about 500 MW near ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for renewable auction volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Central-agency auctions have slowed as states move to direct bids and customised FDRE/RTC tenders. Pumped storage and large C&I deals are the growth areas.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the TBCB EBITDA margin so low?
qa_highlights.answer: TBCB projects are still under construction, so revenue is recognised under lease accounting. Line-by-line EBITDA starts from Q2 as the two projects commission, with Q3 and Q4 to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TP Solar margins rise, and will third-party cell sales continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party cell sales were small. Some sales may continue for a few quarters for ALMM-exempt or open-access projects, but management does not expect large sales ahead. Margins reflect higher-efficiency products.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mundra PAT rise while EBITDA fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the PAT increase came from a higher share of coal profits. Under the supplementary PPA, the plant recovers coal costs and fixed costs on a normative basis but earns no equity return, so under-recovery is possible in some quarters.

Rooftop growth (60-70% target) and falling module realisations as capacity rises across the industry; watch margins at TP Solar.

Tata Projects losses are expected for one more quarter; the Mundra supplementary PPA leaves the plant without an equity return; the nuclear plan awaits government rules.

500400|2026-09.headline: Tata Power reported record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR1,652 crores, up 33% YoY, with revenue up about 26% to INR19,886 crores.
500400|2026-09.overview: Tata Power posted its highest-ever quarterly PAT of INR1,652 crores (up 33% YoY from INR1,245 crores), with consolidated EBITDA up 5% YoY and revenue up about 26% to INR19,886 crores. H1 FY27 PAT rose 22% to INR3,053 crores and EBITDA rose 7% to INR8,494 crores. Management attributed the strength to weak-monsoon power demand, and approved a 1,800 MW Shirwata pumped storage project at INR11,871 crores. Key overhangs remain the Kleros enforcement action tied to the Singapore arbitration and high renewable curtailment of 11% in Q2.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO Sanjeev Churiwala said there was no exceptional income in the associate profit line.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Mundra long-term PPA and whether revenue is booked under Section 11 or the new SPPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the SPPA is signed with Gujarat and filed at CERC, billing to all five DISCOMs is under the SPPA, and its impact is already in the quarterly accounts. Two more states are in advanced talks.

qa_highlights.question: Will Mundra run after Section 11 expires on 31 December if not extended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to conclude the SPPA with a majority of states by 31 December, after which it applies to all states as a common PPA, with CERC approval also expected by then.

qa_highlights.question: Why did distribution regulatory assets rise about 28% YoY to INR83.1 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Delhi lacked a full commission quorum, so true-ups and tariff revisions are delayed; Odisha has a similar issue. Management expects amortisation to pick up in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did traditional generation EBITDA jump about 37% YoY, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects efficiency gains plus DSM gains, with DSM not material but higher in summer; sustainability depends on efficiency improvements.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Shirwata capex to INR11,871 crores versus earlier estimates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR8,000 crore figure was never the estimate; INR11,871 crores is the gross capex figure, quoted without probable incentives.

qa_highlights.question: Is Tata Power bidding for the South Kalamb HVDC project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it did not bid; OEM technology availability and back-to-back arrangements are the constraints under review.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash balance split between renewables and the rest?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash of about INR1,400 crores is attributed to renewables as of September; the rest is spread across other businesses. H1 capex was about INR10,000 crores, of which about INR6,000 crores went to renewables.

500402|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 53% YoY to INR293.9 crores with PAT up 140% to INR28 crores, but FY26 revenue of INR868 crores missed the INR900-1,000 crore guidance.
500402|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR293.9 crores, up 53% YoY and 27% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR25 crores at an 8.4% margin and PAT of INR28 crores. Management attributed the margin dip to one-time legal and arbitration costs, a non-cash expected credit loss provision and bank limit mobilisation costs. FY26 revenue of INR868 crores (up 13%), EBITDA of INR86 crores (9.7% margin) and PAT of INR76 crores (up 55%) fell short of the INR900-1,000 crore revenue guidance, which management blamed on fund-availability-linked execution pacing in March. Management guided to at least 25% growth in revenue and profit in FY27, and the company is building BESS manufacturing capacity alongside its water EPC business.

segments.name: Power and BESS
segments.commentary: Power is a very small share of revenue. A 2.5 GWh BESS assembly line at Supa MIDC Pune is due to start by end-June 2026, expanding to 5 GW and 600 containerised units per year by end-2026. The NTPC BESS order is INR1,128 crores, of which INR96 crores is O&M; capex for BESS up to 5 GW plus containers is about INR200 crores plus INR35 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27: at least 25% growth in both top line and bottom line, with growth expected in every quarter; management said it will give annual numeric guidance at the annual call.
Shortfall in FY26 revenue (about INR50-100 crores of spillover) expected to be executed in Q1 and Q2 FY27; management said EPC orders execute over about 3 years.
EBITDA margin target of around 10%; new orders carry a minimum 10% margin, and management said the Q4 margin would have been about 10% without one-time costs.

NARCL: about INR45 crores minimum payment planned in FY27; surplus cash to be used for growth rather than NARCL repayment; arbitration awards in hand (about INR627-630 crores) expected to cover the balance.
Tax: accumulated losses and the new tax regime (no MAT) expected to keep tax payments low for a few years; management cited a tax shield of more than INR500 crores.
capex_capacity: 2.5 GWh BESS assembly line at Supa MIDC Pune to commence by end-June 2026, with expansion to 5 GW planned.
Container manufacturing of 600 units per year targeted by end-2026, for about INR35 crores.
Total BESS capex (up to 5 GW) about INR200 crores including about INR25 crores R&D; INR175 crores quoted for the 2.5 GW and 5 GW phases with INR125 crores for the first 2.5 GW.
Battery packs are about 35-40% of BESS EPC cost and containers about 8-10%, with battery packs and containers being manufactured in-house.
Peak revenue potential quoted as INR2,500 crores per 2.5 GW phase, about INR5,000 crores for both phases.
demand_pricing: Management cited government BESS targets of about 236 GW by 2031-32 and a 10% BESS mandate for renewables; it said 92 GW of BESS projects are in the pipeline.
All new contracts carry price variation clauses; management said it takes no order without PV and without clarity on funding.
Margin discipline: new orders are being taken at minimum 10% margin; OEM battery-pack orders also at minimum 10%.
Payment terms: NTPC and Power Grid BESS orders expected at 15-20 days; World Bank or bank-funded water projects 15-30 days.
Competition in BESS is rising; management pointed to its Energy Vault tie-up and power EPC experience as advantages.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue below the INR900-1,000 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution is linked to customer fund availability; March saw customer fund shortfalls on tenders such as RITES, so about INR50-100 crores of spillover moves into FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins dip in Q4 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited one-time legal and arbitration costs, an Ind AS expected credit loss provision and bank limit mobilisation costs, together adding about INR10 crores to other expenses; margin is expected to rise as new orders grow in the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net water order book and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is INR5,000 crores total order intake per year including JVs, with net share of INR2,500-3,000 crores; the analyst's net order book estimate was about INR3,300 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Are Jal Jeevan Mission payment delays a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JJM payments were stopped for verification and are resuming, with the scheme extended to 2028; it has not taken new JJM projects recently and is focused on AMRUT and bank-funded projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will the NARCL dues be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR630 crores of awards are in hand, with about 75% payable to NARCL; the balance is expected to be funded from awards rather than operating cash flow, with about INR380 crores to be paid in total.

risks_watch: FY26 revenue missed the INR900-1,000 crore guidance; the spillover of INR50-100 crores into FY27 must show up in Q1 and Q2 results.
Dependence on customer fund flows and government payments; JJM payment delays were acknowledged, and the company said it is avoiding orders without funding clarity.
NARCL repayment depends on arbitration awards, with about INR4,526 crores of claims pending and historical conversion of about 40%.
Net debt to EBITDA of 4.41x, debt-to-equity of 0.4x, receivables of INR417.5 crores and surety bond exposure of INR305 crores.
Q4 PAT includes a tax reversal from recognised accumulated losses; sustainability of earnings depends on this and on the 10% margin target.
BESS commissioning by end-June 2026 and 5 GW expansion by year-end; watch for timing slippage and the margin on OEM and EPC orders.
500402|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and FY27 growth (at least 25%), but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss, which management attributed to fund timing. Answers on the NARCL repayment and arbitration award conversion were detailed but internally inconsistent on figures, and several answers on the order book and BESS capacity were vague.
key_quotes: The company has decided to remain focused on execution rather than building the order book and will remain very selective in choosing orders given the enormous opportunity currently available across all sectors the company deals with.
So unless there is a PV, we don't take the order.
The management remains focused and committed to deliver on its guidance, and we are optimistic about what lies ahead for the SPML Infra.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets around 10% EBITDA margin, says Q4 would have been about 10% without about INR10 crores of one-time legal, ECL and bank costs, and new orders carry a minimum 10% margin versus FY26 EBITDA margin of 9.7% and Q4 at 8.4%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: A 2.5 GWh BESS assembly line at Supa MIDC Pune is under construction with INR125 crores capex and is due to commence by end-June 2026, then expand to 5 GW and 600 containers per year by end-2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q1 and Q2 FY27, then FY27
rows.why: Management guides at least 25% revenue growth in FY27 with growth in every quarter, backed by an INR5,369 crore order book entering Q4 and about INR50-100 crores of FY26 spillover expected to execute in Q1 and Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already announced; 5 GW phase by end-2026
rows.why: Total BESS capex of about INR200 crores (INR175 crores for 2.5 GW and 5 GW phases) is already committed, and the company is raising capex and working capital for BESS up to 5 GW plus 600 containers per year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management has not given annual numeric guidance for FY27 until the annual call, and FY26 revenue of INR868 crores missed the INR900-1,000 crore guidance because of customer fund shortfalls.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue missed the INR900-1,000 crore guidance by INR32-132 crores, and the spillover of INR50-100 crores into FY27 must show up in Q1 and Q2 results; JJM payments were stopped for verification and receivables rose to INR417.5 crores.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BESS assembly line starts by end-June 2026 and container manufacturing of 600 units per year is targeted by end-2026, with battery packs and containers made in-house.

rows.label: Water order book and NTPC BESS order
rows.why: Order book of INR5,369 crores entering Q4 (about INR4,000 crores new) includes the INR1,128 crores NTPC BESS order, and the company targets INR2,500-3,000 crores net water share of INR5,000 crores total order intake a year.

rows.label: NARCL settlement and debt reduction
rows.why: About INR45 crores minimum NARCL payment is planned in FY27 out of INR380 crores outstanding against INR700 crores agreed, with awards of about INR627-630 crores expected to cover the balance, while net debt to EBITDA is 4.41x.

rows.label: Jal Jeevan Mission payment resumption
rows.why: JJM payments were stopped for verification and are resuming with the scheme extended to 2028, but the company has not taken new JJM projects recently and is focused on AMRUT and bank-funded projects.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 growth of at least 25%, the 10% margin target and the BESS line by end-June 2026, but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss and vague on order book and NARCL figures; analysts pushed on the revenue miss, the Q4 margin dip and receivables.

500402|2026-06.headline: SPML Infra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 74% YoY to Rs 286 crore and PAT 87% to Rs 22.7 crore; order book about Rs 5,100 crore.
500402|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 74% YoY to Rs 286 crore, EBITDA rose 81% to Rs 28 crore and PAT rose 87% to Rs 22.7 crore, with EBITDA margin at 10% versus 9% a year earlier. Sequentially revenue was roughly flat, while EBITDA improved about 17% over Q4, which carried a one-time tax reversal that depressed the comparison. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of more than 25% growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with new-order impact expected mainly from Q4 FY27. Progress continued on the battery energy storage system (BESS) plant in Pune, where phase one of a 2.5 GW assembly line is ready and the NTPC container supply is targeted for Q4 subject to approvals. The call was largely Q&A-driven and several answers were imprecise, so the figures below are as stated by management.

financial_highlights.change: +87% YoY; QoQ down about 20% due to one-time tax reversal in Q4

financial_highlights.value: approx. Rs 150 crore as on 30 June

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Water book quality improved; only about Rs 1,251 crore of the order book relates to legacy projects, with the rest carrying operating margins of 10% or higher. Pipeline of about 134 projects worth roughly Rs 98,725 crore across 11 states, over 80% irrigation and water supply.

segments.name: Power substation / transmission
segments.commentary: Named as the third growth pillar alongside water and BESS; management said substation modernisation tenders are rising. No specific Q1 order value was given for this segment.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: 2.5 GW first-phase assembly line ready in Supa MIDC Pune; expansion to 5 GW and 600 container units per year targeted for H1 FY28. NTPC order: design approvals targeted by Dec 2026, container supply from Q4 FY27 with Rs 200-300 crore revenue targeted in FY27. Technology partner is Energy Vault (US).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue, EBITDA and PAT growth guided at more than 25% YoY, reiterated; management said it would update quarterly as orders convert.
FY27 order intake target above Rs 5,000 crore; Rs 1,293 crore already won in Q1 (one answer cited about Rs 1,200 crore), and management said it is hopeful of surpassing the target.
New orders are expected to contribute mainly from Q4 FY27 because design and drawing approvals take 3 to 9 months.
Management said it does not take orders below 10% EBITDA margin; recent wins Konar, KKRI and Indore were stated to be above 10%.
NTPC BESS revenue of Rs 200-300 crore targeted in FY27, subject to design and container approvals.
BESS revenue ballpark given as Rs 2,000-2,500 crore at 2.5 GW and Rs 4,500-5,000 crore at 5 GW; no timeline or margin given.
Legacy NARCL liability: about Rs 320 crore paid so far (including Rs 45 crore prepayment); about Rs 300 crore expected to remain after FY27 following arbitration recoveries.
capex_capacity: BESS phase one: 2.5 GW battery pack assembly line fully ready in Supa MIDC Pune; certifications from IEC and UL in progress for NTPC supply.
Capacity to scale to 5 GW with 600 container units per year; completion targeted in H1 FY28 (one answer said Q1 of next year).
Total BESS capex about Rs 236 crore, stated as already funded through equity raised and sanctioned bank limits; container term loan of about Rs 10 crore sanctioned.
About 25 acres of land acquired for BESS and container expansion.
Management said no board-level discussion yet on capacity beyond 5 GW.
demand_pricing: Water tender pipeline about Rs 98,725 crore across 11 states; large projects include Vanganga-Nalganga river link (about Rs 1 lakh crore), Marathwada Water Grid (Rs 37,600 crore), Ken-Betwa MP component (Rs 24,300 crore) and Papi Basin recharge (Rs 90,200 crore).
Management said it bids on more than Rs 10,000 crore of tenders each month; Gujarat named as preferred state.
BESS market potential cited at 208 GW by 2030; management said it expects tender flow to be continuous.
Pass-through (PV) clauses are kept in all contracts for steel, dollar and lithium cost swings; management said it avoids contracts without price variation.
Management said it is bidding on Amrut projects, which it described as fully funded.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 3,843 crore new order figure net of JV partner share, and will margins rise toward 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Figure is SPML's share only, with JV stakes of 26%, 49% and 51% excluded. Management said it targets above 10% margin on all new orders and expects legacy orders to be executed over FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much NTPC/BESS revenue will come in FY27 and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 200-300 crore of BESS execution is possible in FY27 if NTPC design and container approvals arrive by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is any additional capex needed for the order book and BESS expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 236 crore BESS requirement is already funded through equity and sanctioned bank limits, so no further funding is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no separate margin number; it said revenue, EBITDA and PAT are all targeted to grow more than 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the NARCL liability be repaid, and how?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 700 crore total including interest; Rs 320 crore paid, Rs 375 crore linked to arbitration awards of about Rs 678 crore, and about Rs 300 crore remaining after FY27 as recoveries come in.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Energy Vault tie-up help with NTPC approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Energy Vault's technology has passed NTPC's proven-technology test, which eases design and drawing approvals.

risks_watch: NTPC design and container sample approval by December 2026; any slip pushes the Rs 200-300 crore BESS revenue into FY28.
Order intake must reach above Rs 5,000 crore; only about Rs 1,293 crore was won in Q1.
Quarterly revenue has been flat sequentially, and the call gave no quarterly phasing for the 25% growth guidance.
Rupee depreciation and battery import costs, which management said are covered by PV clauses.
Competition in BESS EPC and OEM supply from other entrants.
Arbitration recoveries are needed to clear the NARCL balance; about Rs 4,526 crore of claims with about 40% expected to convert into awards.
500402|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on guidance and order quality, but vague on specifics: many answers were repeated, and the 25% growth target was restated without quarterly or margin detail. Caution shows on NTPC timing, which depends on approvals not yet received.
key_quotes: The company is maintaining the turnover of the preceding quarter as the turnover is mainly related to orders which was taken in the last two years for which all the design and drawing approval have already been obtained which shows consistency in the project execution.
As we explained into our previous con call that as a strategy, at this moment we don't take any order less than 10%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 10% vs 9% a year ago and management says it bids only above 10% EBITDA margin, but no FY27 margin target was given and legacy Rs 1,251 crore book is still being executed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 2.5 GW phase one is fully ready in Pune, and the scale-up to 5 GW and 600 containers per year is targeted for H1 FY28, which falls just outside the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 74% YoY to Rs 286 crore and the company reiterated more than 25% FY27 growth, backed by a Rs 5,100 crore order book; Q1 revenue was flat QoQ and no quarterly phasing was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: BESS capex of about Rs 236 crore is already funded through equity and sanctioned bank limits, 25 acres are acquired, and management said no board-level discussion exists beyond 5 GW.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is hopeful of beating the Rs 5,000 crore order intake target after Rs 1,293 crore in Q1, but new orders only contribute from Q4 FY27 after 3-9 month approvals.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: NTPC BESS revenue of Rs 200-300 crore depends on design approvals by Dec 2026, and flat sequential revenue with no quarterly phasing leaves the 25% growth target exposed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: NTPC BESS container supply is targeted from Q4 FY27 with Rs 200-300 crore revenue in FY27, using Energy Vault technology, though it is subject to IEC/UL certification and approvals.

rows.why: Order book of about Rs 5,100 crore, roughly 1x FY27 revenue run-rate of Rs 286 crore per quarter, with 134 water pipeline projects worth Rs 98,725 crore and bids above Rs 10,000 crore per month.

rows.label: NARCL liability clearance via arbitration
rows.why: About Rs 320 crore paid and about Rs 300 crore expected to remain after FY27, dependent on recoveries from about Rs 678 crore of arbitration awards.

rows.label: Debt to equity up to 2.4x from 1.1x
rows.why: Debt-to-equity rose to 2.4x from 1.1x, though net worth grew to over Rs 1,000 crore from about Rs 500 crore, and the BESS build is already funded.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 25% growth guidance, order quality above 10% margin and funded BESS capex, but cautious on NTPC approval timing and vague on quarterly phasing; analysts pushed on margins toward 12%, NARCL repayment and BESS timing.

500402|2026-09.headline: SPML Infra Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 20% YoY to INR238.7 crores, with H1 operating cash flow of INR82.4 crores versus a INR44.1 crore outflow.
500402|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue was INR238.7 crores (up 20% YoY), EBITDA INR26.3 crores (up 33%, margin 11% vs 10%) and PAT INR22.2 crores (up 46%, PAT margin 9.3%). H1 revenue was INR505 crores (up 45%), H1 EBITDA INR55 crores (up 33%) and H1 PAT INR45 crores (up 64%). Cash generation was the main highlight, with H1 operating cash flow of INR82.4 crores and cash and equivalents up 88% to INR119 crores. Order inflow commentary was softer: management said Q2 was affected by water tender slowness and monsoon months, and the order book stood at about INR5,056 crores as of 26 September 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs outflow of INR44.1 crores in H1 FY26
up 88% from INR63 crores at March 2026
increased on profit accretion and warrant conversion of legacy obligation of about INR700 crores

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Water remains the largest segment, about 65-70% of the order book per management's split. Tendering was uneven in H1; large schemes such as PKC link, Ken-Betwa, Wainganga-Nalganga and NVDA projects are expected to tender by March 2027. Management said JJM dues are being cleared and JJM 2.0 orders are coming with fund clarity; SPML said it has no direct JJM exposure.

segments.name: Power T&D and substation
segments.commentary: Management said power (including the BESS NTPC order) is about 30-35% of the order book. Recent win: INR186 crores from Power Grid for Bhadla-III and Ramgarh substation extension, the company's entry into 765 kV EHV work. Management expects similar orders this fiscal year.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: NTPC Barauni BESS order of INR1,128 crores has design and drawing approvals; management expects about INR300 crores of revenue in FY27, starting H2. Pune plant is at Phase 1 with 2.5 GWh capacity, targeting 5 GWh by H1 FY28; a 600-container facility is also being built. Proprietary 104.4 kWh battery pack has international certification; OEM battery-pack business is being developed alongside EPC.

guidance_outlook: Revenue and PAT growth guidance of at least 25% for FY27 unchanged; management said FY27 will exceed guidance, with H2 revenue and profitability expected above H1.
FY27 order inflow guidance of about INR5,000 crores retained; management said securing this will not be a challenge.
Management expects new orders won in FY27 to generate revenue only from FY28, since design and drawing approvals take 6-9 months.
Growth of about 25% per year on top line and bottom line expected for the next few years, to be updated annually based on order book and pipeline.
Pune BESS capacity to reach 5 GWh by H1 FY28; longer-term expansion to 5-10 GWh possible, with Pune land (about 25 acres) sized for up to 10-20 GWh.
capex_capacity: BESS manufacturing at Pune: Phase 1 operational at 2.5 GWh; target 5 GWh by H1 FY28, per management's comments.
BESS container manufacturing facility (600 containers) started; expected completion in H1 FY28. NTPC order containers to be partly sourced from own plant; future BESS containers to be fully in-house.
Pune site has about 25 acres of land, which management said can be expanded to 10-15-20 GWh.
Order book about INR5,056 crores as of 26 Sep 2026; only about INR1,161 crores is legacy, and the rest is largely projects with expected operating margins of 10% or higher.
Management said the INR5,000 crore FY27 inflow target includes JV share.
demand_pricing: Management said it bids only on contracts with price variation clauses and avoids fixed-price tenders. Management said it does not bid below 10% expected margin, and that commodity and FX moves have not materially hit BESS margins.
BESS tenders are strong across PSUs and non-PSUs; management said over INR8,000 crores of tenders have been bid, with one more EPC conversion targeted in FY27 (order size INR500-1,000 crores).
Management said the government is reviewing the pricing mechanism for fixed-price BESS contracts, which have come under cost pressure across the industry.
Legacy orders are mostly subcontracted back-to-back, carrying lower margins and minimal working capital; management said there is no residual BG, LD or performance exposure.
O&M: management said EPC to O&M split is about 95:5 by value, and that O&M margins are higher than EPC margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why no new BESS orders since the NTPC order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is bidding actively on PSU and non-PSU tenders, expects one more EPC conversion in FY27, and is also pursuing OEM battery-pack orders with shorter turnaround.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its 25% growth guidance after strong H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the at-least-25% guidance unchanged for now, citing H2 being stronger than H1 due to monsoon-constrained H1 activity, and said it expects to exceed guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is operating cash flow sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow is healthy when projects are fully funded with design approvals in place, and expects positive operating cash flow to continue as the order book shifts to such projects.

qa_highlights.question: How are commodity price increases affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids projects without price variation clauses, so margins are protected; BESS contract has a price variation provision and the recent price moves were not material.

qa_highlights.question: What is the arbitration award position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR100 crores of awards across two matters are at a very advanced stage, with settlement expected soon; this would reduce debt. Management also cites total arbitration claims of about INR3,827 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 order inflow reach INR5,000 crores, and what is the water/power split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR5,000 crore target is on track, the order book is about 65-70% water and 30-35% power including the NTPC BESS order, and JV share is included.

risks_watch: Order inflow pace: Q2 inflow was soft, and water tendering has been uneven; FY27 target of INR5,000 crores depends on water schemes tendering by March 2027 and on BESS conversions.
Execution timing: NTPC BESS revenue of about INR300 crores in FY27 depends on the Pune plant and containers, which are still ramping, and new orders take 6-9 months to start revenue.
Government fund flow: management acknowledged possible near-term liquidity pressure on government schemes, including JJM underspend of about INR20,000 crores to date.
Legacy order book of INR1,161 crores is expected to complete in FY27-FY28, at lower margins, and management gave no quantified execution schedule.
Arbitration monetisation: about INR370 crores of legacy obligation is backed by an arbitration award of about INR655 crores with interest; settlement timing for the INR100 crore awards is not fixed.
500402|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand, cash flow and margin protection, but cautious on order inflow and timing. Management repeatedly gave no firm dates for tender conversion or arbitration settlement, and deflected on some questions (for example, C&I BESS participation and the water/power split was given only in approximate ranges).
key_quotes: Our guidance of at least 25% growth remain unchanged for now, and we will keep you updated in our quarterly calls.
We prioritized fully funded project in cash-rich states, and that is now showing up clearly in our cash flows.
We do not bid for projects without a price variation clause as we have strategically decided not to take risk on factors outside our control, such as commodity price and foreign exchange.

rows.why: Management expects one more EPC conversion in FY27 (INR500-1,000 crores) from over INR8,000 crores of tenders bid, and the NTPC BESS order of INR1,128 crores is expected to deliver about INR300 crores of revenue in FY27.

500403|2026-03.headline: Sundram Fasteners FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR 5,612 crore and PAT hit a record INR 580 crore, helped by Q4 EBITDA margin of 17%.
500403|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR 5,612 crore (up from INR 5,231 crore) and profit before exceptional items of INR 750 crore (up 12% from INR 668 crore). Exceptional items included a full reversal of a prior impairment provision, partly offset by an INR 11 crore gratuity provision under the new Labour Code. Q4 saw exports return to growth in both USD and INR terms, and EBITDA margin widened to 17% from 15.6% a year earlier. Management said April started well and that it targets double-digit growth over the next two years.

financial_highlights.change: Highest in company history; INR 577 crore after MTM vs INR 517 crore
Stated for the quarter/year as per call; treat with caution
Crossed INR 1,500 crore for first time; includes exchange gains
YoY, on stable RM and absence of one-time Q4 FY25 costs
Q4 grew in USD and INR terms; rupee weakened about 4%

segments.name: OE (original equipment)
segments.commentary: Management cited OE as very strong, with growth of about 13% expected in FY27 for the segment. Growth in FY26 was driven by OE and retail.

segments.name: Retail / aftermarket
segments.commentary: Retail grew close to 20% YoY in Q4. Management projects about 15% retail growth in FY27.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports fell about 8%, attributed to tariffs and geopolitics. Q4 turned positive. Management guides 15-20% export growth in FY27, backed by North American Class 8 recovery and Cummins demand.

segments.name: Non-auto (about 35% of mix)
segments.commentary: Includes wind energy, aerospace (GE, HAL, Skyroads), railways and defence. Management said non-auto margins run 100-200 bps above automotive, with shorter working capital cycles.

segments.name: Product mix FY26
segments.commentary: Fasteners 40-42% of revenue; pumps and assemblies, cast and machine assemblies 25-27%; cold extruded and sinter metal about 15%; hot forged and machine components 12%; balance other including radiator caps.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for double-digit revenue growth over the next two years; FY27 segment guidance is OE about 13%, retail about 15%, exports 15-20%, implying about 15% overall growth.

Commercial vehicle market growth seen at 4-6% and passenger vehicles at 4-6% in FY27 by analysts; management expects to outperform by 2-3 percentage points, with CV about 8%, PV about 10%, tractors 6-7%.
Class 8 trucks in North America expected to grow at least 10-15% in CY2026 after EPA 2027 norms take effect 1 January 2027; Q1 preliminary Class 8 orders were almost double year-ago.
Management expects UK interest rate cuts in 2026 to help the UK commercial vehicle market.
Railways: current run rate INR 2-3 crore per month, targeting about INR 100 crore per annum, with ramp-up expected by Q3-Q4 FY27; hit rate about 20%.
Wind energy fasteners: next expansion phase to take monthly output from INR 30-35 crore to INR 50 crore.
Raw materials expected to remain stable in the next quarter; nickel, aluminium and copper increases are indexed and passed through to customers.
capex_capacity: Capex of not less than INR 300 crore each year; 25-30% for replacement and about 70% for customer-driven revenue growth.
Wind energy fastener capacity expansion in the next phase, from INR 30-35 crore to INR 50 crore per month.
Aerospace fasteners expansion undertaken to grow alongside customers including GE, HAL and Skyroads.
Power costs reduced through RE power investments and power exchange purchases at lower clearing prices.
demand_pricing: Order books described as full, with new orders coming in; management says it is the first choice for customers in many product developments.

Raw material inflation in nickel and aluminium since the West Asia conflict; management says RM costs have been broadly stable, with pass-through contracts in OE and export pricing set by market conditions in aftermarket.
EV programmes downsized: GM cut EV projections by 50% and Stellantis postponed programmes. Management says ICE and PHEV orders are recovering; full ramp-up expected by 2027.
Company holds about INR 4,000 crore of EV orders (per analyst question; management did not dispute the figure).
Management reports gaining small car share as small players struggle with supply; small car segment recovered after GST rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioning for EV and supply chain risks, and what differentiates it?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharathan said the company leads in ICE and has EV orders with major Indian OEMs, and that electrification is not an immediate threat in high-horsepower, power generation and marine segments. Differentiators cited were quality, brand and first-choice status in developments.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocation prioritised and how are margins protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Kumar said dividends are 30% of PAT and capex is at least INR 300 crore a year, with 70% for growth. Raw material changes are passed through contractually in OE and by credit notes; export contracts have no pass-through obligation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-auto roadmap, and how does its cash flow and profitability differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh said non-auto includes wind, aerospace, railways and defence, with railways at INR 2-3 crore per month targeting INR 100 crore per annum. Non-auto margins are 100-200 bps higher, with shorter working capital cycles. Non-auto is about 35% of mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is the export share target of 50% still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh said 50% is an aspiration; visibility points to a return to 30-35% export share from new customers and programmes.

qa_highlights.question: What are the segment and industry growth expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharathan gave OE 13%, retail 15% and exports 20%, about 15% overall. Company expects to outperform industry by 2-3 percentage points in every segment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin dip QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Kumar said the dip reflected RM and direct material inflation after the West Asia conflict, with no other specific cause; full-year margins were described as okay.

qa_highlights.question: How do three-year growth and returns compare with management expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Kumar said the target is nominal GDP plus 2% (about 12-13%) for business planning. Exports and some investments did not perform to plan, but cycles were expected to turn after GST 2.0.

risks_watch: EV programme downsizing at GM and Stellantis, and postponed programmes, could weigh on export volumes.
Raw material inflation in nickel and aluminium since the West Asia conflict; pass-through is contractual in OE but not in exports.
Export share fell about 8% in FY26; Q4 recovery and Class 8 pre-buy need to be sustained, and EPA 2027 warranty issues remain open.
Railway hit rate (about 20%) and qualification timelines for direct participation.
Exceptional items: impairment reversal, MTM on investments and Labour Code gratuity provision of INR 11 crore affect reported PAT comparability.
Exchange gains from rupee weakness contributed to Q4 other income; quality of earnings should be checked.

500403|2026-06.headline: Sundram Fasteners Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose 20% to INR1,618 crores from INR1,367 crores; standalone profit up ~10% to INR150 crores.
500403|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a very good start, with consolidated turnover up 20% YoY to INR1,618 crores and growth across OE, aftermarket and exports. Standalone profit rose from INR138 crores to INR150 crores, which management attributed to tighter control of fixed costs. Input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict was a pressure, with direct materials passed through to domestic OEMs and indirect/energy costs under negotiation. Management guided to margin expansion in Q2 once indirect cost recoveries are accounted for, and said the 20% run rate should hold through the festive period.

qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 13% in tonnage; raw material inflation contributed roughly INR20-25 crores to the top line.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing domestic market share given industry growth of 20%+ vs SFL's 16% domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth matched industry in M&HCV (~20%), PV (~23%) and tractors (~14-15%); the gap is mainly 2W/3W, which is only 5-6% of revenue and where SFL is not present.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GM and Stellantis EV revenue expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: GM EV revenue was under INR50 crores in FY26 and is planned at INR200-250 crores this year, including Stellantis; management will take it one year at a time, with INR750 crores cited as a past peak projection.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the cash conversion cycle stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it should stay around current levels, around 140-150 days, as higher export share lengthens the operating cycle; DSO has come down and the spike is mainly inventory timing.

500403|2026-09.headline: Sundram Fasteners Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 30% YoY, driven by OE and exports; EBITDA margin fell to 15.7% on raw material inflation.
500403|2026-09.overview: Management reported about 30% revenue growth in Q2 FY27, led by OE, with exports up 57% YoY (about 10 points from currency and about 47% from volume and dollar terms). Steel and aluminium inflation in Q1 and Q2 compressed contribution margin by roughly 2.5-3%, which took Q2 EBITDA margin to 15.7% and H1 to 15.9%. Management said the brunt of the RM hit is already in the P&L and expects H2 margins to expand as export mix rises. Operating cash flow looked weak, which management attributed to working capital build from longer export cycles, GST input credit and inflated RM inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow weak?

500405|2026-03.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q4 FY26 standalone revenue INR 1,587 crore (+3% YoY), operating EBITDA INR 253 crore at 15.9% margin; ABS running at ~65% of design capacity.
500405|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 3% YoY to INR 1,587 crore on higher volumes (100,664 t, +5.4% YoY) and better spreads, with operating EBITDA up 75% YoY to INR 253 crore (15.9% margin) and PAT of INR 168 crore. FY26 revenue fell 11% to INR 5,338 crore on a ~17% lower average styrene monomer price, while volumes grew ~2% to 363,203 t. Styrene spiked in March 2026 on the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, creating inventory-gain/loss uncertainty management could not quantify. The mass ABS plant restarted at ~65% of design capacity after an equipment failure, and EPS Phase-II (Amdoshi) lifted capacity to 115,000 tpa in April 2026. The company remains debt-free with INR 700 crore investable surplus.

segments.name: ABS
segments.commentary: Mass ABS plant restarted at ~65% of design capacity after an equipment failure; effective capacity cut to ~45,000 t from 70,000 t for now. Phase-II targeted by FY28 but not confirmed.

segments.name: SPC / Xmold compounding
segments.commentary: Management targets ~50,000 t compounding volume by FY28 (if not FY27) and expects Xmold utilisation of ~65-70% in FY27 vs ~45-50% in FY26. Two AC manufacturers onboarded in Sri City.

500405|2026-06.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 1,693 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.53%, while volumes fell 24.5%.
500405|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR 1,693 crore, up 22% YoY, despite lower volumes, driven by higher raw material prices from the West Asia conflict. Operating EBITDA rose 88% YoY to INR 331 crore (19.53% margin) and PAT was INR 236 crore (13.96% margin), helped by wide global deltas between styrene monomer and downstream products. Manufactured volumes fell 24.5% YoY to 70,842 MT, with exports nearly absent and non-OEM demand down roughly 50%. Management declined to guide on volumes or margins, calling the situation fluid, and announced polystyrene and compounding expansions plus a new 80,000 TPA PS line totaling about INR 450 crore, funded from internal accruals.

segments.commentary: Phase 2 EPS capacity completed, taking capacity to about 1,43,000 TPA; management said no near-term EPS expansion planned and exports have stalled.

qa_highlights.answer: Non-OEM demand fell close to 50%; OEM demand was stable to slightly better. Exports were about 10% of normal. Import data is no longer published; unofficial estimate about 20,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 80,000 TPA compounding expansion be absorbed, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the expanded compounding capacity to be used over 2-3 years after June 2027, with ABS compounds the main growth driver.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the profit improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain came from wider global deltas, not volume; management called the level an aberration that will normalise over time and gave no guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Total capex about INR 900 crore, funded internally, and includes the 150,000 cubic metre wide-width board line.

qa_highlights.answer: India CFR styrene about USD 1,300 currently, versus USD 1,350-1,400 Q1 average. Current GPPS delta about USD 250-275 and HIPS about USD 350.

qa_highlights.question: Are alternate styrene sources structurally more expensive?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; freight rates are higher because Gulf voyages took 4-7 days, while alternate sources involve longer voyages and shipping constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Did the industry de-grow in line with the company?
qa_highlights.answer: In polystyrene, management said the industry de-grew at the same rate; in EPS, the company de-grew less than the fragmented industry.

500405|2026-09.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose to Rs 1,957 crore (vs Rs 1,100 crore) with EBITDA Rs 160 crore and PAT near Rs 95 crore, mostly price-driven.
500405|2026-09.overview: Standalone operating income for Q2 FY27 was Rs 1,957 crore against Rs 1,100 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of Rs 160 crore (8.12% margin) and PAT of about Rs 95 crore, nearly double. Management attributed the revenue jump partly to volumes and mostly to higher selling prices following raw material inflation. H1 FY27 operating income was Rs 3,649 crore, EBITDA Rs 508 crore and PAT Rs 331 crore (9.08% PAT margin), while H1 sales volume fell 3% YoY to 166,085 MT on weaker exports. The company remains debt-free with an investable surplus of Rs 886 crore and approved an interim dividend of Rs 2.5 per share (125%).

segments.name: Compounding (PS and ABS)
segments.commentary: Compounding drove the H1 volume growth; internal transfers of PS and ABS to the XPS insulation board division were about 11,700 MT in H1 FY27 vs 4,300 MT a year earlier. Compounding capacity expands from 50,000 to 80,000 TPA, with the step-up targeted around Q3 FY28.

segments.commentary: Sales are seasonally low in monsoon months. A new wide-width line of 150,000 cubic metres is expected to start commercial production in Q1 FY28, with full absorption over 24 to 30 months.

segments.commentary: Running at about 85% of the truncated 65% rated capacity because of an equipment failure not yet fully repaired. A second ABS line is targeted for Q3 FY29 and is the most capital-intensive project.

segments.commentary: EPS capacity is 145,000 TPA across two locations; India EPS demand is seen at 165,000-170,000 tons this year, with market share below 70%. Specialty share of mix is about 40%. Company market share in polystyrene is about 60%.

segments.commentary: Trading sales were about 22% of Q2 sales.

qa_highlights.answer: Landed styrene monomer crossed $1,600/t; the company expects non-OEM pressure if they cannot pass costs on. Domestic raw material requirements are fully met, and improvement is expected from December if geopolitical issues settle.

qa_highlights.question: Is there inventory loss from falling styrene prices in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate inventory loss is booked; SAP uses moving-average valuation, and the market-versus-import price gap is treated as part of normal volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PE and ABS internal transfers to the XPS division rise so sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from compounding of PS and ABS. Internal transfers of about 11,700 MT in H1 FY27 versus 4,300 MT last year lifted utilisation, and total volumes exceeded last year, though net market sales fell 2.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise about 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly raw material, including in-transit and high-seas stock on CIF terms, as raw material prices nearly doubled YoY; this stock is expected to be consumed in the following month.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GPPS and HIPS spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads were about $200-250/t for GPPS and about $300-350/t for HIPS after freight and other costs; the spread has narrowed as freight rates rose.

qa_highlights.answer: India PS demand is about 375,000 tons for FY27-28 per the analyst; the company holds about 60% market share. EPS demand is 165,000-170,000 tons this year, with share below 70%.
