500408|2026-03.headline: Tata Elxsi Q4 FY26 revenue INR993.8 crore, up 0.9% QoQ in constant currency; EBITDA margin 24.6%, up 130 bps QoQ; FY27 growth guided to higher single digit.
500408|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR993.8 crore, up 0.9% QoQ in constant currency, with transportation flat (+0.2% QoQ CC) and Media & Communications up 5.6% QoQ CC. Healthcare & Life Sciences fell 13.1% QoQ CC as expected deal awards slipped into Q1 FY27. EBITDA margin rose 130 bps QoQ to 24.6%, driven mainly by currency tailwinds (about 155 bps) partly offset by a salary increase (about 90 bps), with operating efficiencies adding about 65 bps. Management cut FY27 growth aspiration from double-digit to higher single-digit, with transportation expected to lead.

segments.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences

500408|2026-09.headline: Tata Elxsi Q2 FY27 operating revenue INR 1,055.7 crore, up 2.3% in constant currency; EBITDA margin 21.9%, up 70 bps QoQ.
500408|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 1,055.7 crore, growing 2.3% in constant currency, with all three verticals up sequentially (transportation +2% QoQ, media and communication +3.4%, healthcare and life sciences +3.5%). EBITDA was INR 231.4 crore, up 7.1% QoQ and 19.7% YoY, with margin at 21.9%. Management attributed about 60-70 bps of the margin gain to currency and 10-20 bps to operating leverage and fading one-offs, which absorbed an annual wage revision. Europe automotive remained soft and the transportation outlook depends on it; management expects H2 to exceed H1 across businesses except the Europe-dependent part of transportation.

Up from previous quarter; peak pre-COVID ~81-82%

segments.name: Media and Communication
segments.commentary: Grew 3.4% QoQ in constant currency on ramp-ups of closed deals and AI-led wins, including a GenAI virtual assistant engagement with a global technology leader.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 3.5% QoQ in constant currency after bottoming last quarter; win with a global renal care leader for next-gen home dialysis systems.

500410|2026-03.headline: Ambuja Cements guided FY27 volumes to ~80 Mt (~8% growth) and cut capex to INR6,000-6,500 crore, with cost peaking at INR4,500/t and a INR250/t reduction targeted.
500410|2026-03.overview: Ambuja (consolidated, including ACC and Orient references) reported FY26 record volumes of 73.7 Mt (+16% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (+31%, INR887/t, +12%), with PAT of INR2,647 crore (+17%). Q4 was weak operationally: volumes were muted, cost per tonne rose to about INR4,500 in the quarter against an earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, and acquired assets (Sanghi at 57%, Penna at 46% utilization) lagged. Management reset its growth timeline, pushed capex out, and set a INR250/t cost reduction target for FY27. Pricing was flat-to-slightly-up at about INR254/bag, with industry realisations pressured by soft demand.

500410|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA INR1,589 crore (16.7% margin, +331 bps), net cost INR4,241/t (down INR206/t QoQ), trade volumes down 2% YoY.
500410|2026-06.overview: Ambuja reported revenue of about INR9,500 crore, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crore and PAT of INR660 crore for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA per ton at INR931. Management prioritised value over volume: total volumes fell about 7% YoY, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21%, and about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume in South was cut. Net operating cost fell INR206/t QoQ to INR4,241/t, which management says already absorbs about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost pressure. Management guides to 8% full-year volume growth (July trade volumes up 8% YoY) and FY27 cost of INR4,250/t, and expects some sequential cost pressure in Q2 that it says it can offset.

financial_highlights.value: ~70 million tonnes (implied from cost arithmetic on analyst question)

financial_highlights.change: margin ~7% vs 14-15% in prior four quarters per analyst

financial_highlights.value: ~INR24 crore (VRS at a South India plant)

segments.name: Trade / non-trade
segments.commentary: Trade volumes fell 2% YoY and non-trade fell 21% YoY; trade share rose to 78% from 74% QoQ. Management says trade will be upwards of 75% of sales going forward.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Trade volumes grew 2% YoY, and management called North the highest-EBITDA cluster. North, West, Central and East together are about 80% of volume, with South about 10%.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Grew both trade and non-trade, per management, with Mumbai and Gujarat margin-accretive. West is about 30% of volume.

segments.name: South

segments.name: Central
segments.commentary: Volumes declined as the company shifted to blended cement offerings to improve margins.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth guidance of 8%; management says July trade volumes were up 8% YoY, implying a steep ramp needed for the rest of the year.
FY27 net operating cost target of INR4,250/t, with Q1 at INR4,241/t; a further INR250/t reduction targeted in FY28 to about INR4,000/t.
Identified savings of INR130-150/t from lead distance (INR35/t), fly ash and BCFC logistics (INR30/t), green power and heat rate (~INR50/t), and other items (INR10-15/t).
Q2 expected to see geopolitical-driven cost pressure of about INR100/t if conditions persist, which management says is mitigated by inventory (about 1 month clinker, about 3 months coal).
Capex of about INR6,500 crore in FY27 (about 25%, or INR1,500-1,600 crore, spent in Q1); FY28 capex run-rate of INR6,000-7,000 crore; capacity additions of 8-10 mtpa per year.

Capacity to reach 119 mtpa by end FY27 (Dahej, Salai Banwa, Bhatinda, Jodhpur already commissioned or in trials; Kalamboli and Warisaliganj expected Q2; Maratha clinker in Q1 FY28; Mundra in about 2029).
Green power target of 60% share by FY28 (48% on a revenue-plus-consumption basis versus 34% consumption-based today); RE capacity 973 MW, target 1,122 MW.
Targeted utilisation of 70-75% on a value-focused basis.
AFR (alternative fuel) share targeted at 12-15% in FY27 (currently about 7%) and 25% in the longer term.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity of 109 mtpa today, targeted at 119 mtpa by end FY27 after adding about 10.2 mt.
RE capacity 973 MW (up about 500 MW over the year), with about 75 MW more commissioning; WHRS capacity 228 MW rising to about 376 MW by FY28.
Around 3.5 mtpa of old ACC plants temporarily suspended for about six months (Chaibasa, Marwar, Wadi, Lakheri cited by analysts); management says not permanent closures and no impairment expected.
Sanghi jetty expansion of about INR600 crore for clinker utilisation; Penna AFR and WHRS investments of INR100-150 crore.
Three coal blocks in pipeline, the first to be operational in about 30 months; investment payback 5-6 years.
demand_pricing: Management said cement demand was stable in Q1, with infrastructure and housing support, but input cost and monsoon risks in the near term.

Net sales realisation (NSP) is down YoY and rose only about 1% QoQ per analysts; management attributed the gap to accounting netting of expenses and Ex-works Incoterm shifts, and said NSP is market-driven.
Management cited Q1 disruptions from diesel shortages, packing material availability and geopolitical tensions as reasons for the YoY volume decline.
Brand pull and channel momentum in North, West, Central and East; South channel needs investment.
Capacity utilisation about 65% overall; management says value-focused utilisation target is 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company deliberately sacrificing volume for value, and will FY27 volume growth be muted or recouped in the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8% FY27 volume guidance holds, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY; it said market share was sustained or improved in trade while non-trade share was deliberately reduced.

qa_highlights.question: Where is green power heading, given 973 MW is already commissioned against a 1,122 MW target, and what is the economic benefit of captive use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 45 crore units were sold in Q1 and about 50% (~20 crore units) is expected to be consumed in Q2. The 34% share is consumption-based; on a revenue-plus-consumption basis it is about 48%, with a path to 60% by FY28. Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus green power cost in the range of INR3.3/unit per an analyst's arithmetic.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 cost outlook given geopolitical pressure, and is the FY27 INR4,250/t guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR100/t of potential cost rise in Q2 if geopolitical conditions persist, offset by INR130-150/t of identified savings and inventory of about 1 month clinker and 3 months coal. Net Q2 cost is expected slightly better than Q1 at INR4,241/t; FY27 INR4,250/t guidance maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NSP lag peers and rise only about 1% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to accounting netting of certain expenses against NSP, Ex-works Incoterm shifts, and channel investment. It said NSP is market-driven and cost is the controllable lever.

qa_highlights.question: Which plants were temporarily suspended and is there any impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3.5 mtpa of capacity is temporarily suspended for roughly six months, a mix of old ACC plants and one acquired-company plant across Central, East, North and South. Management said these are not permanent closures and no impairment is expected; the INR24 crore exceptional item relates to a VRS at a South India plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why did South and the acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi) see non-trade push and volume cuts, and how will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume in South was curtailed, with channel build-out needed for one to two quarters more. Orient runs at about 87% utilisation; Penna needs channel and trade investment; Sanghi is investing about INR600 crore in jetty expansion.

Green power grid connectivity for captive use (about 2-3 quarters) and the shift from sales to in-house consumption; the RMC EBITDA margin drop to about 7% from 14-15% needs explanation.
Status of the about 3.5 mtpa suspended capacity and the six-month restart, plus the Maratha clinker timeline slipping to FY28.

500410|2026-09.headline: Ambuja Cements Q2 FY27: consol EBITDA INR1,271 crore (~14% margin, INR770/t) on 16.5 MT volume; 14-project, ~30 MTPA expansion announced.
500410|2026-09.overview: Ambuja Cements (consolidated, including ACC) reported Q2 FY27 cement volume of 16.5 MT, revenue of INR9,197 crore, EBITDA of INR1,271 crore and PAT of INR236 crore, with the company stating it remains debt-free. Trade volumes grew 8.6% YoY and trade share rose to 74%, while B2B volumes were still negative, leaving overall volume roughly flat. Management announced 14 expansion projects adding ~30 MTPA cement and 10.3 MTPA clinker, costing about INR14,500 crore, and guided H2 volume growth above industry at a higher single digit. Cost per tonne was INR4,410 (INR4,182 normalised), with an FY27 target of INR4,250/t. The proposed merger of ACC and Orient Cement into Ambuja is now going to NCLT, with completion targeted within FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to justify the new capex now, given weak H1 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decision is not driven by the quarter; the first capex wave is nearly complete and the new plan is a defined path to 149 MT by FY29 and 155 MT by FY30, with ~INR14,500 crore required for 30 MT.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and how will leverage evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the programme as largely self-sustaining from cash flows over three years, with the balance sheet able to handle any interim funding need.

qa_highlights.question: Expected fuel cost trajectory and spot coal prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended fuel cost was INR1.87/kcal in Q2; imported spot now about INR2.80-2.85/kcal versus roughly INR2.2 at Q2 time. Imported fuel is under 40% of mix, with pet coke ~10-12%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lessons from the first phase, including contractor issues, and a tighter scheduling plan with 14-18 month execution timelines and equipment already ordered.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate low in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to tax shield from Penna and Sanghi, which comes through the merger and is one component of EPS accretion.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~INR40/t extra from the trade shift now, rising to ~INR150/t by June as trade value gains build.

500411|2026-06.headline: Thermax Q1 FY27 hit by a INR 91 crore cost-to-completion charge on a legacy government EPC project, with revenue growth only about 7%.
500411|2026-06.overview: Management called Q1 FY27 the toughest quarter relative to expectations in several years. The biggest drag was a INR 91 crore cost-to-completion hit on a legacy government EPC project (original order about INR 1,200 crore, taken in FY22), triggered by late engineering changes from the engineering partner in June. About INR 300 crore of finished Industrial Products goods could not be shipped in the quarter, partly due to high Gulf-war shipping rates, and commodity cost pressure added about INR 10 crore. Green Solutions lost about INR 20 crore at FEPL and about INR 8 crore in Bio-CNG. Revenue grew only about 7%, and management said the backlog (about INR 14,000 crore) and a strong H2 are the basis for remaining bullish.

qa_highlights.answer: Original order was about INR 1,200 crore, taken in FY22, with a total loss close to INR 150 crore. About 74% is invoiced and 26% is balance. The engineering partner has confirmed engineering is 100% complete, and the last four quarters are construction-heavy.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is government/PSU, and will Thermax bid on such projects again?
qa_highlights.answer: Government/PSU orders are about INR 300-400 crore, under 5% of the roughly INR 14,000 crore book. Management will not rule out future bids but will price them for risk and only where capability is unique.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 300 crore shipment slippage a recoverable profit, and what is the Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slipped volume was partly shipped and carried better-than-average margin, but gross margins are not 45-50%; project gross margins are about 15%. Q2 will also carry a larger scheduled shipment, and the US data-centre shipment is expected to be recognised in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the issue not flagged earlier, and what will be done about it?
qa_highlights.answer: The engineering change arrived in June, and the Board and auditors took several weeks to review the impact. Management did not commit to pre-announcing profit warnings but said it will consider sharing surprises earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is talent the root cause of execution slippage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the top five people on the project had over 20 years of Thermax experience and that the error was a project-model mistake, not a talent gap. Several restructurings were announced, and TOESL and FEPL have external leadership.

qa_highlights.question: What policy changes drive the Bio-CNG and green methanol pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bio-CNG prices to rise 20-30% around August, with announcements possible at an August 10 conference. Green methanol tenders by SECI are a second lever; thermal demand is also growing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin once legacy projects are done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees line of sight to 10%+ profitability for Industrial Infra. Chemicals already reached double-digit EBITDA in Q1.

risks_watch: Further cost-to-completion or LD exposure on the remaining legacy government EPC project over the next four quarters.
Bio-CNG PGTR outcomes for the last two projects in August-September, with Q3 closure expected.
Commodity (steel plates up about 18%) and tariff pressure on Industrial Products and Chemicals margins in Q2.
Pipeline conversion: handshakes not booked pending advances; US data-centre timing slipping on customer end.
FEPL Tamil Nadu approvals still pending, and the planned external investor for a majority stake.
500411|2026-06.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on execution and the Q1 miss, with management calling it the toughest quarter in years. Confident on H2 and the order pipeline, but several forward claims (order inflow, bio-CNG policy, Q2 profit recovery) are not yet backed by booked orders.
key_quotes: A very difficult quarter, felt like was the toughest one, at least relative to expectations for the past few years that we have had.
But this one felt particularly so.
So, net-net, we actually -- outside of this one project -- our project execution adds to our as-sold profitability, not takes away from our as sold.
It was a mistake and not one that we have remotely done in the last 3 years.

500413|2026-03.headline: Thomas Cook (India) Q4 FY26 group revenue fell 10% YoY to INR 17,707 million as Middle East war hit DEI and Desert Adventures, while Sterling and India operations grew.
500413|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 in two phases: the first nine months were relatively stable (top line up 7%, EBITDA up marginally), while Q4 absorbed the Middle East conflict, airfare spikes and rupee weakness, with the Pahalgam/Operation Sindoor disruption earlier in the year. Full-year consolidated income rose 3% to INR 83,982 million (INR 85,578 million per closing remarks), but EBT fell 14% to INR 3,268 million. India operations grew EBT 16% in Q4, and Sterling posted record Q4 numbers. The board approved in-principle demerger of the resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts, with a timeline of Q1 FY28.

INR 1,701 million (31% margin) / INR 1,142 million (21% margin)

segments.commentary: B2C is about 27% of travel portfolio and grew 8% in FY26 and in Q4; short-haul bookings +17% for FY and +21% in Q4, while long-haul remained subdued.

segments.commentary: B2B (about 73% of travel revenue) grew 2% in FY26 but fell 18% in Q4; international DMS revenue +3% in FY and -24% in Q4, with Desert Adventures down 50% in Q4.

segments.commentary: Q4 MICE revenue fell 2% due to about INR 100 crore of government MICE business and about INR 100 crore of Desert Adventures MICE absent from last year; corporate MICE grew 21% in Q4 and 6% for FY26.

segments.commentary: FY26 turnover INR 27 billion (net basis) and revenue INR 1,541 million, +19% YoY; Q4 revenue +28%. Air volume +7.3% in Q4 and +4.8% for FY26.

segments.commentary: 78 resorts with about 3,800 rooms across 65 destinations; Q4 occupancy 64%, ARR +12% to INR 6,347, RevPAR +16%. Cash about INR 3,400 million and debt-free.

segments.commentary: About 50% of revenue from UAE; Q4 revenue INR 194 crore and EBIT negative INR 10 crore. Far East and APAC grew, and management expects Middle East recovery of 50-60% by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did financial services top line and EBIT drop, and is margin being traded for share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 forex EBIT rose 17% and FY EBIT held at about INR 149 crore; the drop reflects mix shift and net revenue reporting with franchise revenue shares, not margin pressure. Float of about INR 16 billion was flat vs December, which management read as customers not spending.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Sterling EBIT been flat at about INR 129 crore for two years despite rising room count?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani cited the end of membership acquisition revenue, a 2-3 month ramp-up lag for new resorts, and upfront costs. Krishna Kumar cited high ROU depreciation from leased resorts. EBITDA margin was 31% and EBIT margin 24%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DEI loss behind us and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram said the corrections are not done and the cost base will reduce over 30-60 days notice periods. He expects Middle East recovery of 50-60% by year-end and said FY26 will not match original plans. Debasis Nandy said top line depends on ground conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Net cash and deployment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy said net cash is close to INR 800 crore, to be used for technology capex, repayment of long-term loans over the next couple of years, and inorganic growth if returns criteria are met. An analyst's build-up gave about INR 730-740 crore, which was confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 outlook for Sterling and monsoon risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani said there are no headwinds so far in Q1; occupancy is expected to rise toward 65-70% over the year. Monsoon risk is being managed by asset protection and a geographically spread portfolio, with Q3 now the strongest quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy said the process is on track for the 12-15 month plan, applications are with NSE and BSE, and completion is expected by Q1 FY28.

Travel EBIT margin trajectory toward 5% as short-haul mix rises and DMS units remain loss-making.

500413|2026-06.headline: Thomas Cook Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell 12% YoY to INR 21,530 million and PBT fell 21% to INR 885 million, driven by Middle East exposure.

Excluding the GCC subsidiaries, group EBIT grew 8%, and India businesses (forex, MICE, corporate travel, domestic) were stable to growing. Sterling Holidays reported its best quarter ever, with revenue up 21% and EBITDA up 21%. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, though it said H2 should be better than H1 if conditions hold.

segments.name: Travel (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 17,106 million, -14% YoY; EBIT INR 405 million, -50%. Domestic +29%, short-haul +6% (+21% excluding Middle East), long-haul sales -28%. MICE +14% to INR 5,420 million; DMS -31% to INR 5,422 million with Desert Adventures revenue -89%.

segments.name: Sterling Holidays
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1.7 billion (+21%), EBITDA over INR 620 million (37% margin), PBT margin 28% (+200 bps). Occupancy 77% (+700 bps), ARR INR 7,809 (+10%), RevPAR +20%; net debt-free with cash above INR 3.7 billion.

segments.name: DEI (Digital Imaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,307 million vs INR 2,097 million; EBIT swung to INR -152 million from INR 106 million. About 50% of global business is in the Middle East; China site closures and Bahamas contract end added pressure. Net assets employed INR 243 crore.

segments.name: Desert Adventures (GCC)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 89% YoY; management estimated its EBIT impact at roughly INR 8-9 crore (about INR 90 million), not confirmed. Cost base did not flex as fast as volumes.

If conditions remain constant, H2 FY27 expected to be better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: How did underlying outbound leisure demand trend in July and early August, and do short-haul destinations carry comparable margins?

qa_highlights.question: Will Thomas Cook pursue more airport forex counters over branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Airports are opportunistic, not a strategy; entry is made only at commercially rewarding terms, as with Delhi Airport.

qa_highlights.question: DEI: what are capital employed, normalised EBIT and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Net assets INR 243 crore; normal-year EBIT margin 6-7%; target 20% ROE. Major technology upgrade done, with periodic upgrades roughly every 10-12 years.

qa_highlights.question: Travel FY27 topline and EBIT margin outlook, and the TCS impact on pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 guidance. Internal EBIT margin range 4-5%. Management said it saw no clear TCS pricing benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the double-digit earnings growth guidance still achievable, and what is the split of GCC subsidiary impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not confirm double-digit growth. DEI EBIT moved from INR 10 crore profit to INR 15 crore loss (INR 25 crore delta). Detailed numbers to be obtained from Investor Relations.

qa_highlights.question: Will DEI cost optimisation show in Q2 results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visible benefits in Q2 and Q3 FY27; revenue recovery in the Middle East will determine earnings quality.

500413|2026-09.headline: Thomas Cook India Q2 FY27 consolidated PBT before exceptionals held at INR 848 million (flat YoY) as income fell 5% to INR 20,030 million.
500413|2026-09.overview: Consolidated total income fell 5% YoY to INR 20,030 million, but PBT before exceptional items was flat at INR 848 million and PBT margin rose to 4.2% from 4.0%. Financial Services was the standout, with revenue up 21% and EBIT margin at 44.1%. The India travel business recovered through the quarter, with the India EBIT deficit narrowing from 31% to 22%, while West Asia-exposed businesses (Desert Adventures, DEI, AlliedTPro) remained well below last year but improved sequentially. Sterling Holiday Resorts delivered its highest-ever Q2 revenue of about INR 1,272 million (+17%), with reported EBITDA diluted by a one-off-like GST input tax credit cost of about INR 40 million.

segments.name: Financial Services (Thomas Cook forex)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +21% with gross turnover INR 39 billion (+7%); EBIT INR 452 million, margin 44.1%. Retail turnover +12%, education forex +33% against a 34% fall in industry education remittances; corporate +10%, travel -6%.

segments.name: India Travel (B2C, domestic, DMS, corporate)
segments.commentary: India EBIT deficit narrowed from 31% to 22%; domestic B2C grew 8%, India DMS grew 16%, corporate travel revenue +11% to INR 446 million. B2C overall fell 17% on long-haul outbound weakness, with Kailash Mansarovar cancellations of INR 185 million.

segments.name: International DMS (Desert Adventures, AlliedTPro, Asian Trails)
segments.commentary: Desert Adventures sales down 67% (vs 89% in Q1); AlliedTPro down 22% (vs 40% gap in Q1); overall overseas DMS revenue -7%, Asian Trails +9%, South Africa private safaris +31%.

segments.name: Sterling Holiday Resorts
segments.commentary: Q2 room nights +23%, occupancy +300 bps, average rate +12%, RevPAR +12%; 7 resorts opened to 83 properties and over 4,000 keys. Q2 EBITDA hit by about INR 40 million GST input tax credit cost not present last year.

segments.name: DEI (Digiphoto)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 147 crore vs INR 130 crore in Q1 and INR 195 crore LY (about -22% YoY); EBIT loss of about INR 1.2 crore vs loss of INR 15 crore in Q1 and profit of INR 2.3 crore LY. UAE revenue back to 40-50% of prior year.

500414|2026-09.headline: Timex Group India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% to INR359 crore and EBITDA 54% to INR66 crore, a record quarter, with product margin down 1.1pp.

E-commerce grew 75% to about INR190 crore, while trade grew 34% to about INR85 crore. Product gross margin fell about 1.1pp YoY on raw material inflation (copper, gold, silver), movement costs and a weaker rupee (USD near INR97 at peak), partly offset by an April price increase of 5-15% on selected SKUs. 500420|2026-06.headline: Torrent Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 55% to INR4,921 crores with 33.8% EBITDA margin after JB merger; semaglutide supply hit India sales.
500420|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR4,921 crores (up 55%) and operating EBITDA of INR1,664 crores (up 61%) at a 33.8% margin, with the JB Pharma merger completed effective 8 July 2026. JB's underlying business grew 10% to INR1,201 crores with a 35.3% margin, helped mainly by cost synergies running ahead of plan. The base India business grew 19% to INR2,157 crores, outpacing the IPM's 12%, but a supply disruption at the injectable semaglutide partner cut sales of about 20% of that brand's monthly contribution for July and most of August. Brazil's growth was held back by a one-time channel inventory reduction, and Germany fell 9% on supplier and tender issues. Management withheld full-year margin and synergy numbers until next quarter, though it said JB's synergy target will be exceeded.

500420|2026-09.headline: Torrent Pharma Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51% to INR4,979 crores, with EBITDA margin at 33.5% and JB integration weighing on JB's international sales.
500420|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR4,979 crores (up 51%) and operating EBITDA was INR1,666 crores (up 54%), a 33.5% margin. Torrent's base business grew 18%, with India base business up 20% against IPM growth of 12%, while the underlying JB business was flat at INR1,086 crores after post-merger integration. JB India branded grew 7% (13% in Q1), while JB international fell 7% due to deferred deliveries from plant and quality integration. Management expects JB growth to return to double digits in H2 and cost synergies (INR450 crores) to be achieved about a year earlier than the original three-year plan.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,181 crores, up 20% vs IPM 12% (PharmaTrac), helped by launches and field force expansion. Curatio grew 34% in Q2 and H1 and is now 7-8% of base India business excluding JB.

segments.name: JB India branded
segments.commentary: Grew 7% in Q2 after 13% in Q1; management expects H2 above the H1 rate of about 10%, with India ahead of double-digit growth.

segments.name: JB international
segments.commentary: Down 7% from deferred deliveries linked to plant network optimisation and quality system alignment; recovery expected to take longer, with total JB growth guided to double digits in H2.

segments.name: Brazil
segments.commentary: Constant currency revenue BRL236 million, up 21% YoY; IQVIA market growth 5.7% vs Torrent 26%. Growth split roughly equally across price, volume and new launches. Management expects mid-teens growth ahead.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Constant currency revenue USD44 million, up 13%, driven by new launches meeting or exceeding share targets. Management expects pricing pressure in H2 as new competitors enter.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Constant currency revenue EUR26 million, down 13%, due to loss of high-value tenders, supplier disruption and government-mandated price cuts. Best case a slight decline in coming quarters, stabilising after 3-4 quarters.

segments.commentary: Philippines, Mexico, Russia and South Africa growing high single digit to double digit; management suggests 6-9% for planning.

Brazil competition is intensifying: local players with larger field forces and rising price competition over the past two to three years. Brazil semaglutide: one local generic launched about three months ago; Torrent expects to launch within 6-9 months.

qa_highlights.question: How will JB recover in India and internationally, and will the international slowdown take longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Mehta said India JB branded was 13% in Q1 and 7% in Q2 as guided. Growth is expected to rise each quarter, with H2 above the 10% H1 rate. International recovery may take longer, but total JB growth should be double digit in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Are cost synergies ahead of plan, and is there upside to the INR450 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Menon said about half of the INR450 crore could be realised this year and most by next year. Management is keeping the INR450 crore target for now and will review any upside in a couple of quarters.

500425|2026-03.headline: Ambuja FY26 volumes hit a record 73.7 Mt (+16%), but Q4 cost ran ~INR4,500/t and management reset FY27 guidance to ~80 Mt with capacity targets pushed out.
500425|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record volume year for Ambuja, with 73.7 million tonnes sold (up 16% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (up 31%, INR887/t). Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above the INR4,000 exit target, driven by acquired-asset underperformance (Sanghi 57%, Penna 46% utilization), freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management reset its growth plan: FY27 volumes ~80 Mt (~8%), capacity target 119 Mt by end-FY27 (vs earlier 140-155 Mt), FY27 capex INR6,000-6,500 crore, and a cost reduction of about INR250/t in FY27 plus INR250/t in FY28. Pricing has not offset cost inflation, with April-over-March hikes of about INR10/bag in a few areas.

Management said it would be happy with half of any industry price hike, given weak demand; price pass-through has not kept pace with cost.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited stabilizing Sanghi and Penna plus about 10 Mt of new capacity commissioning between now and September 2026, which will be needed to reach 80 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook given the INR4,000/t exit target versus the reported INR4,500/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for March exit; the March month was about INR4,100/t normalized, and INR4,500/t is the peak. A reduction of INR150-200/t is expected from fly ash and green energy, and INR250/t is the FY27 average target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Ambuja's fixed cost rising faster than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher branding (about INR70/t for FY26), repairs and maintenance at acquired assets, freight, lower government incentives and higher heat consumption. Acquired assets were said to drag EBITDA by about INR70-80/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is the reset of capacity and timelines a change in ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned but the timeline has moved; capacity was stepped back to 119 Mt by end-FY27. Capital will be deployed only after current projects are completed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 'core' versus 'non-core' working capital movement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core working capital fell from 30 to 20 days; non-core rose, partly from incentives accounted on an as-received basis, and some of the increase could be accounting-driven. ACC's negative operating cash flow reflects receivables from Ambuja under the MSA, which are to be settled via an ICD.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any EBITDA/t guidance or an IRR target for new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No EBITDA/t guidance was given. Karan Adani said the project IRR hurdle is 18% on all-equity funding.

500425|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA INR1,589 crore (16.7% margin, +331 bps QoQ), net cost INR4,241/t, down INR206/t QoQ; trade volumes -2% YoY.
500425|2026-06.overview: Management reported revenue of about INR9,500 crore, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crore, and PAT of INR660 crore for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA per ton of INR931 (grey cement INR911). Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management says is on track for the INR4,250/t full-year guidance despite about INR110/t West Asia-related inflation. Volumes fell sharply: total volume was down about 7% YoY, trade down 2% and non-trade down 21%, as the company deliberately exited low-margin volumes, mainly in South and at acquired assets. Management guided to 8% trade volume growth for FY27 and said July trade volumes were up 8% YoY.

key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
And I would not shy highlighting that we are already seeing an 8% improvement on the trade volumes.
Having a sustainable performance matters more than anything.
Yes, you might be leaving the volume, but you're not leaving value on the table.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity moves from 109 Mt to about 119 Mt by end FY27; Jodhpur 2 Mt commissioned (September quarter), Kalamboli 1 Mt and Warisaliganj 2.4 Mt due Q2, with Dahej 1.2 Mt and Salai Banwa 2.4 Mt already in trials.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 8% trade volume growth for FY27 with July trade up 8% YoY, but Q1 trade was -2% YoY and total volume about -7%, so the back-nine-months ramp of about 12-13% is steep and capacity utilisation is only about 65%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 65% with about 10.2 Mt of capacity already being added to reach 119 Mt, so a fresh capex push is not indicated; FY27 capex is held at about INR6,500 crore and FY28 run rate INR6,000-7,000 crore is already planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed the INR4,250/t cost, 8% volume and 119 Mt capacity guidance without raising it, and flagged a possible INR100/t Q2 cost rise from geopolitical pressure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Trade volume was -2% YoY in Q1 and the 8% FY27 target needs about 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months, while Q2 cost could rise by INR100/t and about 3.5 Mt of ACC capacity is suspended.

rows.label: NSP gap versus UltraTech narrowing
rows.why: Ambuja NSP is about INR100/t below UltraTech in Q1 versus an average premium of about INR50 earlier, and management says NSP is market-driven and expects it to move in line with industry.

rows.label: ACC intercompany loan (ICD) repayment under merger
rows.why: ICDs to the parent are at 8% coupon and within approved limits, with about 3 Mt cement supplied to ACC under MSA, but the treatment was deferred offline.

rows.label: Green power self-consumption and RE build-out
rows.why: About 50% of 45 crore units sold in Q1 expected to be consumed in-house in Q2 (about 20 crore units), power cost down to INR4.9/kWh from INR5.9, and RE capacity 973 MW rising toward 1,122 MW by FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost savings (INR4,250/t guide, INR130-150/t more savings) and commissioning dates, but defensive on the volume decline and the NSP gap to UltraTech; analysts pushed on the steep 8% volume ramp, NSP discount and RMC margin fall to about 7%, and several items were deferred

500425|2026-09.headline: Ambuja Cements Q2 FY27 consol EBITDA INR1,271 crore (~14% margin, INR770/t) on 16.5 Mt volume; 14 expansion projects add ~30 Mt grinding, capex INR14,500 crore.
500425|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 cement volume was 16.5 Mt, revenue INR9,197 crore, EBITDA INR1,271 crore (about 14% margin, INR770/t) and PAT INR236 crore, with the company still debt-free. Trade volumes rose 8.6% YoY and trade share reached 74%, while non-trade (B2B) volumes remained negative, leaving total volume roughly flat. Management announced a 14-project expansion (about 30 Mt grinding, 10.3 Mt clinker) costing about INR14,500 crore, taking capacity to 149 Mt by FY29 and 155 Mt by FY30. Unit cost fell to INR4,410/t (INR4,182/t normalised), with FY27 target of INR4,250/t reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 fuel cost INR1.66/kcal; Q2 FY26 INR1.60/kcal
vs INR6/unit in Q2 FY26 and INR4.3/unit in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Trade (consol)
segments.commentary: Trade volumes up 8.6% YoY; trade share up to 74%; premium products 37% of trade sales (35% last year). West trade volume +14%, North +13%, South +13%, Central +9%, East flat.

segments.name: Non-trade / institutional (B2B)
segments.commentary: Deliberately recalibrated to drop negative-EBITDA volumes; still negative YoY in Q2, with management expecting positive growth in Q3 and Q4. Blended cement share 82% of sales vs 77% a year ago.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete (RMC)
segments.commentary: Quarterly volume 1.07 million cubic metres, up 19% YoY, from a network of about 125 plants; RMC EBITDA margin about 7% per management.

segments.name: Green power / fly ash
segments.commentary: Green power sales about INR136 crore (352 million kWh) in Q2, booked in other operating income; fly ash revenue about INR25 crore. Combined contribution about INR97/t per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cost target of INR4,250/t reiterated; management says ~INR160/t improvement is needed in H2 and that it is on track, subject to no further global fuel escalation.
H2 FY27 volume growth guided to be ahead of industry, at higher single digit (aim for double digit) against industry growth of about 6-7% for FY27.
Capacity to reach 149 Mt by FY29 and 155 Mt by FY30; FY28 cost target of INR4,000/t for combined existing and new capacity.
Capex: about INR14,500 crore for the 30 Mt programme (~INR7,500 crore a year over the next two years). FY27 capex guided at INR6,500-7,000 crore, with INR3,000-3,500 crore in H2.
Merger of ACC and Orient Cement into Ambuja to go to NCLT; completion expected within FY27 and described as EPS accretive.
Realisation: INR10/bag price increase realised in October; further hikes expected. Management sees about INR150/t benefit from trade mix by June 2027.
capex_capacity: Q2 commissioned 4.6 Mt at Dahej (Gujarat), Salai Banwa (UP) and Kalamboli (Maharashtra); 3.2 Mt at Bathinda (Punjab) and Penna Jodhpur (Rajasthan) stabilised with ramp-up in H2; 2.4 Mt at Warisaliganj (Bihar) due Q3 FY27.
Expansion: 30 Mt grinding (West 15.2 Mt, East 11.6 Mt, North 2.9 Mt) and 10.3 Mt clinker (Maratha 4 Mt, Umrangso 4 Mt, Mundra 2.25 Mt).
Execution timelines of about 14 months for grinding units and about 18 months for integrated units; equipment reportedly already ordered and PMC appointed. Around 20 Mt bunched into March-May 2028.
Penna and Sanghi utilisation about 50% in Q2; company-level utilisation about 61-62% in Q2, targeted at about 75% by end FY27.
Clinker capacity 69 Mt with clinker factor about 66%. Debottlenecking at about four plants with Loesche expected to complete in 4-5 months.
demand_pricing: Price held at INR255/bag in the monsoon-hit Q2; INR10/bag realised in October with more hikes expected.
Management says the trade-led push adds about INR40/t so far, rising toward INR150/t by June 2027.
Demand headwinds: weak monsoon with drought declared in several large states (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra, Rajasthan); impact expected with a lag in Q3-Q4.
Brand equity claimed to support a price premium, backed by independent surveys. Competition in East and West expansion regions acknowledged; management says 'there is a market for everyone'.
Fuel: blended fuel cost INR1.87/kcal in Q2 vs spot imported coal INR2.80-2.85/kcal; domestic coal above 60% of mix, imported under 40% (pet coke about 10-12%).

qa_highlights.question: Why revisit expansion now when H1 volumes were negative and demand soft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly performance did not drive the decision; the first capex wave is nearly complete and the second wave (West, East, North) is value-accretive, mostly brownfield and clinker-backed. Earlier guidance of 140 Mt by FY28 and 155 Mt by FY30 is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex needed to reach 149 Mt, and how will debt evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR14,500 crore for 30 Mt, roughly INR7,500 crore a year. Management described the programme as self-sustainable from cash flows, with only interim debt possible.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost guidance of INR4,000/t: does it include new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR4,000/t target for FY28 covers the combined existing and new capacity at 149 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in execution given past delays and bunched-up commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lessons from the first phase, including a contractor issue, and a tighter scheduling plan with 14-18 month build cycles. It did not name specific suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Expected H2 volume growth and Q3 cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 volume growth is guided to higher single digit, aiming for double digit, ahead of industry. The cost path is supported by green power, BCFC, WHRS (18 MW at Sanghi in Q3) and AFR.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate low in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to the proposed merger and the tax shield from Penna and Sanghi, which it said is one driver of EPS accretion.

risks_watch: Execution risk: about 20 Mt of capacity bunched in March-May 2028 on 14-18 month build cycles, with prior contractor issues.
Cost risk: fuel costs rising (spot imported coal INR2.80-2.85/kcal vs blend INR1.87); FY27 target depends on INR160/t H2 improvement and no further escalation.
Demand risk: drought in major states may moderate construction with a lag; non-trade volumes still negative.
Utilisation of acquired Penna and Sanghi assets at about 50% in Q2; management withheld detailed figures until Q3-Q4.
Merger completion via NCLT and EPS accretion claims; Q2 tax rate unusually low on merger-linked tax shield.
Management's previously stated 'aggressive' vs 'calibrated' expansion framing was questioned by analysts and left unresolved.

As a going -- running company, we are giving INR4,000 combination of existing and new.

500440|2026-03.headline: Hindalco Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT fell 51% to INR2,597 crore on Oswego fire, but adjusted PAT rose 10% to INR5,796 crore.
500440|2026-03.overview: Consolidated business-segment EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR10,812 crore, while reported PAT fell 51% to INR2,597 crore due to exceptional items including the Novelis Oswego plant fire. India business segment EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR6,610 crore and PAT rose 11% to INR3,549 crore. Copper EBITDA hit a record INR907 crore on higher by-product (sulfuric acid) realisations, while Novelis adjusted EBITDA was about $498 million ($543/t). Management expects Novelis to recover in FY27 as Oswego hot mill restarts and Bay Minette ramps.

segments.name: India aluminium upstream
segments.commentary: Shipments +2% YoY, revenue +11% YoY, EBITDA INR5,448 crore at $1,756/t. Q4 cost rose about 2.4% QoQ; Q1 FY27 guided about 5% higher, mainly furnace oil.

segments.name: India aluminium downstream
segments.commentary: Shipments 124 KT (+18% YoY), EBITDA INR255 crore (+16% YoY), $226/t, driven by volume, mix and premiumisation.

segments.name: Copper (India)
segments.commentary: Record EBITDA INR907 crore (+48% YoY) on by-product realisations and efficiencies; metal shipments 128 KT (-5%), CCR volumes 91 KT (+11%).

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Shipments 917 KT (-4% YoY) excluding 73 KT Oswego loss; adjusted EBITDA $498 million ($543/t). Impacts: $53 million Oswego fire, $27 million tariffs, offset by $41 million Sierre flood insurance recovery.

guidance_outlook: Novelis: Oswego hot mill to restart in the next few weeks; current-year headwinds expected to substantially recover in FY27; long-term $600/t EBITDA target intact.
Novelis cost programme: FY26 exit run-rate savings raised to $200 million (from $125 million target); 3-year structural cost cut of $350-400 million by FY28 exit.

Novelis Bay Minette 600 KT greenfield plant: cold mill commissioning started, hot mill commissioning from next month, commercial coils in FY28, 18-24 month ramp; start-up costs of about $100-150 million annually expected below EBITDA.
India copper TC/RCs: more than 85% contracted at benchmark; expected close to zero or slightly negative for FY27.
India copper EBITDA: Q1 FY27 similar to Q4 (INR900 crore range) but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3.

India capex FY27 about INR12,000 crore (later framed as INR15,000-17,000 crore for the next year); Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, mainly Bay Minette; consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over next 2 years; net leverage around 2x.
Aluminium market: deficit now 1.5 million t for CY26 (from 0.3 million t), tightest in Q2-Q3 CY26.
Renewable capacity 470 MW at year end, rising to 523 MW by end Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Aditya smelter: first 180 pots by December 2027, next 180 pots by December 2028; management says timelines look firm.

Captive coal: Chakla box cut expected in next 2 months, first coal possibly Q4 FY27; Bandha box cut done but first coal only in FY28 due to high strip ratio; Meenakshi (strip ratio under 1) expected to add substantial volumes in FY29; Chakla Stage 1 forest clearance received.

Downstream: Aditya FRP ramping up; battery enclosure at full ramp-up; Aditya battery foil commissioned; Taloja AC fin facility commissioning; specialty alumina precipitate hydrate commissioned, under customer approval.

Copper: inner grooved tubes (35 KT) in customer qualification; 50 KT Pakhajan e-waste recycling plant to commission in August; copper smelter about 3 years out; battery grade copper foil scaled down to a smaller capacity in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Aluminium prices strengthened in the quarter; West Asia conflict disrupted supply; global market now seen in 1.5 million t deficit for CY26.
India Q4 FY26 aluminium demand about 1.6 million t, +9% YoY; India copper demand 402 KT, +10% YoY.
Q4 FY26 hedges: aluminium 64% at INR2,807/t; currency 26% at INR88/$. FY27 hedges: aluminium 29% at $3,013/t; currency 14% at INR90.13/$.
Sulfuric acid prices high due to Middle East conflict and China export restrictions; management expects Q1 FY27 to be slightly above Q4 but could correct if Strait of Hormuz reopens.
Global concentrate TC/RCs at record lows around -$0.21 to -$0.25/lb; expected to stay negative through FY27.
Alumina sales 211 KT in Q4 FY26; Q1 FY27 guided at about 170 KT.
Midwest premium at about $380/t due to 50% US tariffs; Japan premium up on supply tightness and freight. Domestic vs export realisation gap narrowed; exports may be slightly higher in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q4 copper EBITDA reflect the full sulfuric acid price surge, and how sustainable is the INR900 crore run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 expected in the same range given high sulfuric acid, but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3 and cautioned that Hormuz reopening could correct sulfur prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India and consolidated capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: India FY27 capex about INR12,000 crore, rising to INR15,000-17,000 crore in the following year; Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, falling sharply in FY28 after Bay Minette. Consolidated capex expected to be lower than current levels; FY28 detail deferred to Q3/Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt breakdown and peak?
qa_highlights.answer: India gross debt INR12,200 crore, cash INR18,000 crore (net cash INR6,000 crore). Novelis gross debt INR75,000 crore, cash INR11,000 crore (net debt INR63,000 crore). Consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over the next 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is $600/t Novelis EBITDA assuming current scrap spreads and start-up costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management does not assume current spreads or metal prices; start-up costs sit below EBITDA. The $600/t target is seen as sustainable, not reliant on current tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How do coal captive mines change costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chakla and Bandha expected at similar cost to market coal; Meenakshi substantially lower. Captive mines expected to flatten the cost curve over 15-20 years; meaningful captive volumes only from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis avoid shipping to Canada given tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is mitigating tariffs by using US cold mill capacity, including additional capacity secured at Logan; Kingston (Ontario) mill longer-term planning still pending.

Tariff exposure (Midwest premium, US-Canada flows) and possible relief from governments.

Captive coal ramp-up delays (Bandha high strip ratio) and Aditya smelter timelines.

Battery-grade copper foil and battery demand in India slower than expected.

500440|2026-06.headline: Hindalco Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 58% YoY to INR13,481 crore and PAT 75% to INR7,013 crore, led by record India upstream EBITDA of INR7,390 crore.
500440|2026-06.overview: Consolidated business segment EBITDA rose 58% YoY to INR13,481 crore and PAT rose 75% to INR7,013 crore, with Hindalco India EBITDA up 73% to INR8,606 crore. India upstream aluminium posted a record INR7,390 crore EBITDA (USD2,331/t, 55% margin) on higher LME and favourable macros, while copper delivered a record INR918 crore despite a planned smelter shutdown. Novelis volumes fell 5% YoY to 916 kt and adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to USD516 million, but the Oswego fire outage and elevated US tariffs (USD70 million) weighed on the quarter. Management guided volumes higher in Q2 for downstream aluminium and copper, and said sulphuric acid prices will stay near Q1 levels in Q2.

segments.name: India upstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments up 3% YoY and revenue up 44% YoY; record EBITDA of INR7,390 crore. Hedged about 29% of FY27 aluminium at USD3,004/t and 18% of FX at INR91.63/USD.

segments.name: India downstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments up 3% YoY to 104 kt; EBITDA INR298 crore, up 30%, on volume, mix and premiumisation. Management sees a sustainable downstream margin nearer USD250/t than the USD300 seen in Q1.

segments.name: India copper
segments.commentary: Metal shipments 105 kt, down 16% YoY on a planned smelter shutdown; CCR volumes 96 kt, down 8%. Record EBITDA of INR918 crore; ex-shutdown EBITDA/t would have been around USD1,000.

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Shipments 916 kt, down 5% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA USD516 million including an $18 million net positive from Oswego fires and $47 million insurance proceeds. Cost savings run-rate at USD225 million against a USD350-400 million target by FY28 exit; Oswego mill restarted in June.

Q2 volumes expected higher for both India copper and India downstream aluminium.
India cash cost expected to rise 5-6% QoQ in Q2 on northern-region coal prices during monsoon.
Novelis net leverage expected to fall below 4x, with a level of about 4.5x around end-September; Novelis net debt/EBITDA to start declining in Q4.
Novelis working capital release of USD300-400 million over the next couple of quarters.
Novelis long-term EBITDA/t guidance of USD600 unchanged; Oswego net cash impact seen at about USD600 million after all insurance recoveries.
Consolidated net leverage to remain around 2x; India net debt/EBITDA not expected to change materially as FY27 is a high-capex year.

Copper smelter expansion, Pakhajan scrap melting project (commissioning this year, IRR in high teens) and copper smelter timing under review, with smelter output expected in FY29.
demand_pricing: LME aluminium moved from about INR3,150/t before the Middle East conflict to a peak near USD3,850/t, then eased to USD3,200/t after the ceasefire; management expects a 2026 deficit of about 1 Mt.
India aluminium demand about 1.5 Mt in Q1 FY27, up about 3% YoY; flat-rolled products up more than 10%; electrical segment weak on deferred contractor-led projects.
Indian refined copper demand 359 kt, down 9% YoY; TC/RC at -26 to -30 cents/lb; concentrate tightness expected to persist through 2026.
Alumina prices around USD330-340/t, slightly up from historic lows, and expected to stay in this range until Middle East smelters return.

Novelis faces US Section 232 tariffs of about USD70 million in Q1 (versus USD24 million last quarter) as it imports metal while Oswego is down; management expects some tariff cost for the next couple of quarters.
Japan/Korea MJP premiums elevated due to Middle East supply disruption; expected to ease next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Novelis tariff impact of USD70 million excludable to show EBITDA/t above USD600, and why did it rise from USD24 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Novelis Steve Fisher said it was not excluded from adjusted EBITDA and advised against adding it back; tariffs stem from importing metal while Oswego is down and will persist for a few quarters. Dev Ahuja said third-party costs sit below the line as fire costs, while own-network imports do not, and declined to give specific guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the brand royalty to Birla Group Holdings affect Hindalco?
qa_highlights.answer: Satish Pai said both Novelis and Hindalco will pay a royalty of 0.25% of revenue to Birla Group Holdings, capped at INR225 crore per year, which is below Hindalco's materiality threshold and does not affect dividend or capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD300/t downstream aluminium EBITDA sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Pai said USD250/t is a more sustainable level for the rest of FY27, with the longer-term aluminium downstream target still above USD300/t; more clarity on total downstream (including copper) is due next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis leverage fall well below 4x?
qa_highlights.answer: Dev Ahuja said Novelis will be below 4x, helped by insurance recoveries, working capital release, lower ABL borrowings and higher EBITDA run-rate, after about 4.5x at end-September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Oswego insurance recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dev Ahuja said cumulative cash impact so far is about USD1.4 billion net of recoveries, of which USD300 million has been recovered; the net cash impact is expected to settle at about USD600 million, with a couple of hundred million possibly slipping into FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Pai said 21% of FY28 aluminium is hedged at USD3,160/t, with a target of about USD3,200/t; no further FY27 hedging is being added due to deep backwardation.

500440|2026-09.headline: Hindalco Q2 FY27: consolidated EBITDA up 52% YoY to INR13,869 crore; India copper record INR1,673 crore, with INR350-400 crore called non-recurring.
500440|2026-09.overview: Consolidated EBITDA rose 52% YoY to INR13,869 crore and consolidated PAT rose 59% to INR7,533 crore, with India business EBITDA up 66% to INR9,011 crore. India aluminium upstream EBITDA was INR7,009 crore (up 55%, $2,125/t), while copper posted a record INR1,673 crore that management says includes roughly INR350-400 crore of non-repeatable gains. Management guided copper to an underlying INR1,200-1,300 crore a quarter and flagged aluminium cost up about 5% QoQ on coal, with no relief until Q4. Novelis is recovering from the Oswego fire and Yeongju strike, with tariff headwinds expected to fade by Q4 and deleveraging targeted to start by FY27 end.

segments.name: India aluminium downstream

segments.name: India copper

Bay Minette's first cold-rolled coil was produced in September 2026, with commercial shipments from Q1 FY28. Long-term EBITDA/t guidance of $600 unchanged.

Over INR50,000 crore of expansions under execution in India, with another INR50,000 crore under evaluation; over INR1 lakh crore of growth investment over five years. About INR20,000 crore of the first INR50,000 crore expected to be spent by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited tariffs fading by Q4, a $20 million Yeongju impact in Q3 and then none, $47 million more insurance recoveries by FY27 end, and shipments recovering from Q4 as customer supply chains normalise.

500459|2026-03.headline: PGHH FY26 sales flat at about Rs 4,300 crore while PAT rose 19% to about Rs 850 crore on savings-funded reinvestment.
500459|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of targeted investment: sales were flat at about Rs 4,300 crore, while PAT grew 19% to about Rs 850 crore, helped by a Rs 86 crore savings programme. The call focused on the Integrated Growth Strategy, with Whisper Period Panties, Whisper Nights and Vicks launches cited as proof points. Management acknowledged category growth has been uneven, with feminine hygiene at 7-10% and healthcare at 2-3%, and flagged West Asia-linked commodity and resin cost pressure. Incoming CFO Srividya Srinivasan takes over on July 1. Few hard guidance numbers were given, and several questions on buybacks, investment plans and manufacturing were declined.

Management said the turnaround is complete and set a FY30 target of INR12,000 crore organic revenue (~$1.3bn, 17% CAGR from ~INR6,000 crore) plus ~INR6,000 crore (~$0.7bn) from acquisitions. segments.commentary: Current business ~$90m, targeted at ~$200m by FY30 with ~40% gross margin and a 10% EBITDA target. Seven verticals addressed, ~$3bn TAM; R&D in Bangalore and Limerick, Ireland; flagship product line Emerald.

segments.name: India / Rest of World
segments.commentary: India is 6-7% of revenue (~$50m), targeted at 8-10% of a $2bn business (~$200m). India is a low-margin geography per management; 300+ partnerships and 17 offices / 35 delivery centres cited.

segments.name: Financial services (anchor client)
segments.commentary: A large US bank client has been served for 27 years at ~$100m annual spend, ~$1bn lifetime revenue crossed in the last 10 years, 68% growth since 2016.

guidance_outlook: FY30 target: INR12,000 crore organic revenue (~$1.3bn, ~17% CAGR) plus ~INR6,000 crore inorganic (~$0.7bn), totaling ~INR18,000 crore (~$2bn). Computed at INR95/$.
EBITDA margin: 10% overall target, reached in FY27 per management (9% currently); FY30 EBITDA margin target of 10%+.
Order book expected to reach $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 (guided 50%+ growth in FY27 bookings); average order age 15-18 months.

Acquisitions: ~$200-250m of revenue acquired per year, targeting 2-5% EBITDA margin targets bought at 6-8x and turned to 9-10% in 90-120 days; 70% upfront, 30% earn-out. Brazil (2S) acquisition recently announced.
Debt-to-equity could rise to ~1:1 after the acquisition programme; otherwise debt to stay broadly flat with internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Data centre workforce: 2,100 hires planned in next 12 months (mostly US) to go from ~4,000 total employees to ~7,000.
GCC in Bengaluru to grow from ~600 to ~1,000 people.
Centralised resource management in Plano, Texas; estimating tools Accubid and P6 Primavera; separate project controls team.
Training: 600 people trained on AI; 36 hours of learning per person per year vs 28-hour industry average; 1,500 certifications in data centre business.
Capital allocation priorities: people and training, AI-enabled platforms, working capital, and acquisitions in Europe, APAC, India and Latin America.
demand_pricing: Management says demand outweighs supply in data centre work; prices have 'considerably increased', with cost increases passed through; margins claimed to improve modestly with execution.
Mike Carney stated no business is won on price; win depends on execution and relationships.
Hyperscaler data centre contracts: mainly time-and-materials / design-build; ~25% of project value is unknown at outset; change orders agreed, e.g. ~$2.5m change orders on a $10m initial scope.
US skilled labour market is constrained; inflation expected. Talent on Tap programme trains trade-school hires (~3 weeks) to address it.
Management claims ~0.2% share of the $200bn networking and connectivity opportunity; India data centre market from 1.3 GW to 8 GW (42% CAGR), India IT $171bn (9.2% CAGR per Gartner).

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory for non-TPS businesses, and how acquisitions will be funded (~$200m a year).
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 10% EBITDA across all businesses; management expects to reach 9% to 10% in FY27 with scale. Acquisitions funded mainly by internal accruals plus some debt; ~$200-250m of revenue acquired per year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of hyperscaler exposure in order book and margin difference vs enterprise.
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres ~25% of order book, rising to 35-40%. Margins are stated as not varying by customer type; India is a low-margin geography and data centre operators/multi-tenants carry higher margins than general contractors.

qa_highlights.question: Contract structure for data centre projects (time-based vs fixed price).
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of annuity contracts, fixed-price small projects and cost-plus for large multi-year projects; management says 15-20% of projects are expected to convert to annuity as the business scales to $2bn.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rising and receivable outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: The March quarter revenue skew (62% in March vs 38% in first two months) raised receivables by ~INR580 crore; management expects receivable days to revert to 60-75 from ~90+ as the skew normalises to 45:55.

qa_highlights.question: Hiring split by geography and rupee sensitivity.
qa_highlights.answer: The 4,000 headcount is ~2,000 US, ~1,200 India (500-550 India business, balance GCC), ~300 Europe, ~400 Latin America; hiring is revenue-based and the US accounts for most growth. Plan computed at INR95/$; currency moves affect INR revenue, margin percentages unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to the FY30 plan.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited talent and attrition, unforeseen events and geopolitics; said currency is naturally hedged (earn and spend in same currency) and the main risk is project execution.

risks_watch: Execution on large, multi-year data centre projects where ~25% of value is unknown at start and scope changes are common.
Talent: 2,100 US hires in 12 months in a constrained labour market; wage inflation and attrition.
Working capital: receivable days at ~90+ and the March-quarter revenue skew; watch normalisation toward 60-75 days.
Acquisition integration and the INR6,000 crore inorganic target, funded partly with debt; D/E could rise to ~1:1.
Tax rate normalising from ~10% to 18-20% after about two years, which will weigh on PAT.
Order book conversion: target of $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 and new hyperscaler wins.
500463|2026-03.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional, with aspirational targets described as a 'dream' and 'plan A'. Specific numbers are given for FY30 and order book, but several claims (market sizes, share, margins) are loosely supported and the Q&A on margin, tax and funding was answered in detail.
key_quotes: So, this is our organic plan, primarily the aspiration to go to INR12,000 crores from current INR6,000 crores, almost like doubling that to a $1.3 billion revenue.
We are expecting that when we end this fiscal year, which is March '27, our order book will remain in the range of probably $1.3 -1.4 billion.
Without a hyperscaler being there, it won't happen, because they are the anchor tenants for most of the GPU data centers.
The focus now is the execution.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides 9-10% EBITDA in FY27 from 9% in FY26 (INR570 crore), with TPS targeted at 10% EBITDA and acquisitions turned to 9-10% in 90-120 days; margins are claimed to improve modestly with execution.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plan to add 2,100 data-centre/GSI hires over 12 months (about 4,000 to 7,000 employees) and grow Bengaluru GCC from ~600 to ~1,000; this is headcount capacity, not plants, and no utilisation was disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book ~$800m is guided to $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 (50%+ growth), and FY30 organic revenue target is INR12,000 crore (~17% CAGR from ~INR6,000 crore).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the plan is headcount and acquisitions, with no utilisation disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book growth guided at 50%+ in FY27 and the Brazil acquisition is adding inorganic revenue, but no revenue guidance raise was given and the FY30 targets were newly set at the Capital Markets Day.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivable days at ~90+ versus 60-75 normal, a 2,100-person US hiring push in a constrained labour market, and the tax rate rising from ~10% to 18-20% after about two years all weigh on PAT.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TPS flagship product line Emerald is a named product line with a target of $90m rising to $200m by FY30, but no specific launch date was given.

rows.label: Order book to $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027
rows.why: Order book grew from ~$500m to ~$800m with $1bn booked in FY26, and management guided 50%+ growth in FY27 bookings.

rows.label: Receivable days normalise to 60-75
rows.why: Receivables rose ~INR580 crore QoQ on a 62% March-quarter revenue skew, and management expects the skew to normalise to 45:55, but this depends on the skew changing.

rows.why: D/E fell from 1.2 to 0.6 (debt ~INR800 crore, equity ~INR1,300 crore), but ~$200-250m of acquired revenue per year is to be funded partly by debt.

500463|2026-06.headline: Black Box Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA rose 38% to INR160 crore; FY27 revenue guided at INR7,800-8,000 crore.
500463|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY), with EBITDA of INR160 crore (+38% YoY, margin 9.3%, up 90 bps) and PAT of INR56 crore (+18% YoY). The quarter included about two months of consolidation from the Brazilian acquisition 2S, which contributed about INR60 crore. Order bookings were US$339 million and the order backlog reached about US$950 million (up 83% since the transformation began). Management reiterated FY27 guidance, with FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9.3-9.4%, and said growth would be weighted to H2 and spill into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: up 83% since start of transformation; company said up 83% YoY in opening remarks

segments.name: Hyperscale / data center
segments.commentary: Management expects hyperscale to grow about 25% in aggregate across the business, with data center tenures of 24-36 months. A new US hyperscaler order of US$131 million (about INR1,240 crore) was added, with work on site starting from November.

segments.name: Non-hyperscale enterprise
segments.commentary: Expected to grow at modest double-digit, about 10%, lagging the hyperscale cycle, with enterprise spend expected to follow with a lag.

segments.name: Product business (TPS / KVM, Emerald)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making at EBIT level as revenue grows; management expects about 20% growth in FY27 and says the segment is highly accretive once scale is reached.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue INR7,800-8,000 crore (+23-27% YoY).
FY27 EBITDA INR725-750 crore (+27-32% YoY); EBITDA margin 9.3-9.4% (about +30-40 bps). Medium-term aim is 10% or more at scale.
FY27 PAT INR300-325 crore (+38-50% YoY).

FY27 order bookings US$1.3-1.4 billion (about +32-45% YoY); order backlog at March 31, 2027 of US$1.3-1.4 billion (about +65-75%). Management said the backlog figure may be conservative and gave updated detail after Q2.
Tax rate expected at 10-15% in FY27 and FY28, normalising to about 20% thereafter.
Operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion expected to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Long-term aspiration of INR18,000 crore (US$2 billion) revenue by FY30: about INR12,000 crore organic and INR6,000 crore inorganic.
capex_capacity: Plan to onboard nearly 2,000 professionals to support execution.
Large hyperscale sites are gigawatt-plus; deployment and hiring for the new US hyperscaler order start only from November.
Talent and people investment described as largely done; cash flow expected to turn positive from operations.
Management said supply chain, particularly cables and fibre, improved over the last quarter.
demand_pricing: Management says competition is based on execution capability, scale, and the ability to deploy skilled resources, not on lowest price.
Management estimates the addressable opportunity at US$250-300 billion, with about 60-70% of spending in the US.
Management says the company has executed several hundred megawatts, close to a gigawatt, and is now receiving more invitations to bid (pull rather than push).
Data center orders are described as accretive to margin, and expected to be more accretive at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What was organic revenue growth given 2S was included from May?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said INR60 crore of the INR1,719 crore came from 2S, and the balance is organic. June quarter is seasonally weak for 2S.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow improve given the investment needs suggested by the backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said talent investment is largely complete, operating cash flow should be positive, and cash flow should rise with growth. Working capital still needs funding.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative, given backlog growth ex-long-term projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said most backlog execution falls in Q3 and Q4, and it will spill into FY28. FY27 growth is about 22-25% and FY28 growth should exceed that. Backlog could end higher as new orders come in Oct-Mar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for non-data center businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said non-hyperscale enterprise is expected to grow about 10%, with a lag behind the hyperscale cycle. Overall growth is about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will TPS / product business reach profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the product business is expected to grow about 20% in FY27 and focus on mission-critical products such as KVM/Emerald. Losses should narrow with scale.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance imply depressed Q2/Q3 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said Q4 should be at or above 10%. Investment in training and talent means guidance is kept at 9.3-9.4% for the year, with 10% or more expected at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from hyperscaler capex moderation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said current pipeline shows new projects being announced and no slowdown in conversations. Shifts between sites would be absorbed across multiple geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive moat?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO cited scale, execution capability, customer relationships, and the ability to fund and train staff. He said competition will exist, and the company is aiming to take share.

risks_watch: Guidance depends on H2 conversion: Q1 was described as seasonally soft, and FY27 growth requires about 30-40% sequential or YoY growth in H2.
Margin: management is holding guidance at 9.3-9.4% because of talent and training investment, and 10% is targeted only at scale.
Customer concentration in hyperscalers: any capex moderation or site delay would affect execution and backlog timing.
Product business (TPS) still loss-making at EBIT level.
Working capital and cash conversion needs to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Tax rate is currently low due to carried-forward losses; it is expected to rise to about 20% after FY28.
Transcript notes that several guidance figures were corrected on the call (backlog, bookings, EBITDA, PAT, margin); use the corrected figures stated in the call.
500463|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand and backlog, with explicit caution on margins (guidance held at 9.3-9.4% because of investment in talent) and on H2 execution timing. Management relied on the backlog to support the FY27 numbers and gave limited detail on cash flow and on the product business.
key_quotes: We are in the midst of one of the largest digital infrastructure investment cycles in history.
Winning these engagements is no longer simply about offering at the lowest price. It is about demonstrating consistent execution on mission -critical infrastructure.
Our medium-term objective remains to consistently operate at or above a 10% EBITDA margin while maintaining healthy returns on capital.

Historically, quarter 1 has been a relatively softer quarter for Black Box. We expect stronger revenue conversion and operating leverage in the second half of the fiscal year with this momentum supporting the delivery of the FY27 guidance outlined in our presentation.

But I think it's better to factor in what we are planning to invest and therefore, guiding where Deepak had guided at about 9.3%, 9.4% (inadvertently stated - 9.4% to 9.5%: to be ignored) at this time.

rows.why: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 9.3-9.4% (about +30-40 bps) and said Q4 should be at or above 10%, with 10%+ targeted at scale.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical plant capacity is discussed; growth is via onboarding nearly 2,000 professionals and deployment of a US$131m (about INR1,240 crore) hyperscaler order starting November, so new people capacity rather than plants is what comes online.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record INR1,719 crore revenue (+24% YoY), US$950m backlog and US$339m Q1 bookings, with FY27 revenue guided +23-27% to INR7,800-8,000 crore and growth weighted to H2 and spilling into FY28.
