rows.label: US$131m hyperscaler order starts work in November
rows.why: The new US hyperscaler order of US$131m (about INR1,240 crore) has work on site starting from November, with hiring for it starting then.

rows.label: Backlog and bookings guidance for FY27
rows.why: Order bookings guided at US$1.3-1.4bn and backlog at US$1.3-1.4bn by March 2027, with management saying the backlog figure may be conservative and most execution in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive as talent investment completes
rows.why: Talent investment described as largely done and operating cash flow expected to turn positive, but working capital still needs funding and no cash flow number was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on hyperscale demand, backlog and the US$131m order, and cautious on margins held at 9.3-9.4% for talent investment and on H2 execution timing; analysts pushed on organic growth ex-2S, backlog conservatism, cash flow and the loss-making product business.

500469|2026-03.headline: Federal Bank posted record quarterly net profit of INR 1,145 crore (up ~10% QoQ) in Q4 FY26, with CASA crossing INR 1 lakh crore and GNPA at a decade-low 1.62%.
500469|2026-03.overview: Federal Bank reported Q4 FY26 net profit of INR 1,145 crore, its highest ever quarterly profit, on underlying metrics excluding one-off gains. Growth was led by commercial banking, gold, LAP and CV/CE, while CASA and NRE deposits crossed INR 1 lakh crore each. Asset quality hit decade-best levels, and a one-time INR 456 crore interest gain from an income tax refund was used partly to build a floating provision ahead of ECL transition. Management declined to revise its credit cost, growth or cost-to-income guidance, and said the ECL impact is still being assessed.

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Grew ~6% QoQ and ~26% YoY, described as primary growth engine.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Grew 9% QoQ and 26% YoY, despite downsizing a sub-segment for regulatory alignment; around 14% of advances, LTV below 54%.

segments.name: LAP
segments.commentary: Expanded 8% QoQ; management expects growth to accelerate.

segments.name: Agriculture and microfinance
segments.commentary: Agriculture grew 5% QoQ; microfinance grew 7.28% QoQ, restarted in small way last quarter.

segments.name: CV/CE
segments.commentary: Sharp uptick of 8.5% QoQ.

segments.name: Business banking
segments.commentary: Grew ~6% YoY; deliberately calibrated to protect yield and portfolio health.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional banking
segments.commentary: Essentially flat QoQ; deliberate credit selectivity toward high-rated counterparties.

segments.name: Credit cards
segments.commentary: Growing ~23% YoY; growth skewed to transactors rather than revolvers.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost guidance of 50-60 bps retained, not revised; FY26 credit cost was about 56 bps; management said it will reassess once ECL impact and West Asia situation are clearer.
Cost-to-income guidance range of 53%-56% retained; management said it has done slightly better than guidance in FY26.
Further deposit repricing benefit expected in Q1 and early Q2 FY27; NIM expansion expected from mix, not only repricing.
About 100 branches planned for next year after 39 added in Q4 FY26.
Medium-term CASA ratio target of 36% reiterated as achievable; no numeric loan growth guidance given.
ECL transition impact still being assessed; draft guidance indicates the floating provision can be used during transition.
capex_capacity: 39 new branches added in Q4 FY26; slower branch addition in H1 FY26 due to network study and rebranding.
About 100 branch additions planned for FY27.
Branch network restructuring and relocation to improve productivity of existing branches.
Wealth management business launched during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Retail home loans: unattractive pricing (15-year at ~7.15%); bank not pushing volume, which weighs on overall retail growth; retail book flat YoY.
Wholesale deposits reduced during the year; retail term deposits growing faster than system.
Remittances remain elevated; management sees no change unless significant job losses in UAE.
Corporate: targeting early double-digit growth, focus on mid-market (about 75% of NTB acquisitions) and cross-sell.
Competition described as intense and sometimes irrational in rate-setting.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on loan and deposit growth after balance sheet realignment; staff cost decline and one-time provisions treatment.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CASA and retail term deposit growth exceed system and wholesale deposits fell; no numeric FY27 guidance, only said traction is building. Staff cost impact not quantified. Floating provision is for ECL transition and not linked to any specific asset.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 and whether deposit repricing is done.
qa_highlights.answer: Some deposit repricing left into Q1 and early Q2 FY27. NIM down only about 2 bps over FY26 on full-year basis. Day count impact present in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to Middle East and ECL impact on provisions and credit cost.
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East asset exposure described as not large. ECL impact still being assessed; the guidance of 50-60 bps is under reassessment, not yet changed. Current plans unchanged despite West Asia situation.

qa_highlights.question: LCR level and comfort range.
qa_highlights.answer: LCR at 119%; comfortable at 115-120%, down from 135-140% earlier, which management called a NIM drag.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan LTV and pricing practice.
qa_highlights.answer: Gold valued at lower of 30-day average and prior-day price; margins raised during March volatility; LTV below 54%. No internal cap; will reassess if gold loans approach 20% of book.

qa_highlights.question: Credit card and transactor growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Card book grew about 23% YoY, with transactor growth stronger than revolvers as organic cards go mostly to existing customers.

risks_watch: ECL transition: impact not yet quantified; management said it is still early, and draft guidance may change.
West Asia conflict: possible inflation pass-through from Q1 FY27 and potential remittance or NRI-related stress if job losses occur in the Gulf.
Food inflation rose to 3.87% by March, to be monitored into Q1 FY27.
Falling LCR (119%) may constrain CASA growth if the bank pushes it further; LCR fell about 20 points YoY.
Home loan book drag on retail growth; management says it will not chase pricing at current levels.
One-time INR 456 crore interest gain and INR 115 crore tax reversal inflate reported ROA (1.36% vs 1.24% underlying).
500469|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on liabilities, asset-quality and margin execution, with repeated emphasis on underlying (ex one-off) numbers. Cautious on forward growth and ECL: guidance on credit cost and cost-to-income was left unchanged, and the ECL impact was deferred, citing uncertainty from the West Asia situation.
key_quotes: We delivered INR1,145 crores in net profit, representing nearly 10% sequential growth. Now this is the highest ever quarterly net profit for the bank.
Our NIM story is about multiple levers being pulled, and we are confident that we'll continue to remain agile and build that NIM expansion from here.
This is primarily as a transition to ECL.
Higher LCR than required is also a NIM destroyer.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation are not discussed; the branch rollout is the only expansion and is already in the plan, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.why: Wealth management business was launched in Q4 FY26, but no further product launches or timelines were disclosed.

rows.label: ECL transition impact
rows.why: Impact is still being assessed; draft guidance allows the INR 456 crore-linked floating provision to be used during transition, but the quantum is not yet known.

rows.why: Retail home loans priced at about 7.15% (15-year) are unattractive, the retail book is flat YoY, and management says it will not chase volume at current levels.

rows.why: GNPA at a decade-low 1.62% and NNPA at an all-time low 0.37% with provision coverage up 141 bps QoQ to 76.55%, supporting credit cost stability.

500469|2026-06.headline: Federal Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.57% YoY to INR1,176.93 crores, with NIM at 3.33% and GNPA at 1.52%.
500469|2026-06.overview: Federal Bank reported a strong Q1 FY27, with profit up 36.57% YoY on NII growth of 26.06% and NIM expansion of 13 bps QoQ to 3.33%, achieved with little treasury contribution. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.52%, NNPA at a record-low 0.18%, and fresh slippages down 37.8% YoY. CASA ratio rose 188 bps YoY to 32.23%, and management reiterated the mid-teens growth guidance with a positive bias. Management flagged the ECL transition from 1 April 2027, estimating a one-time impact of 1.5% to 2% of net worth, and noted a rising inflation and West Asia-linked fuel pass-through backdrop.

financial_highlights.change: up 13 bps QoQ, up 39 bps YoY
GNPA down 39 bps YoY; NNPA down 30 bps YoY
down 37.8% YoY, down 13.6% QoQ; slippage ratio 0.61%
balance up 18.26% YoY; ratio up 188 bps YoY

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Grew 22.96% YoY; CV/CE book grew 21.07% YoY, with exposure focused on medium-sized fleet operators rather than single-truck operators.

segments.name: Corporate and Institutional Banking
segments.commentary: Grew 16.12% YoY but only about 6% QoQ; gross CIB book crossed INR1 lakh crores. Management called the quarterly pace opportunistic and not the normal trajectory.

segments.name: Retail banking
segments.commentary: Grew 10.8% YoY overall. Gold loans grew 33% YoY, cards 36% YoY, and loan against property 21% YoY; gold LTV is about 60%.

segments.name: Business banking
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY; slippages down 36% YoY. Management said growth will be pushed from here now that portfolio health is better.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: CA grew 18% YoY, SA 19.3% YoY, and FCNR(B) 37.76% YoY. Average SA cost is about 2.6%.

NIM expected to improve about 5-6 bps per quarter on average over the next 3-4 quarters, not necessarily linear.
ROA expected to improve about 3-4 bps per quarter, per prior guidance, with management reiterating it.
Credit cost: management indicated the lower end of the 50-60 bps guidance band, but did not formally revise it, citing war and monsoon headwinds.
ECL transition effective 1 April 2027: one-time impact of about 1.5% to 2% of net worth; no material ongoing P&L impact expected.
CASA ratio improvement target unchanged; LCR to be operated in the 115-120% range (Q1 average 117%).

Obtained investment-grade international credit rating from S&P, opening access to bonds, ECBs and IBU funding.
demand_pricing: Cost of deposits fell about 11 bps QoQ excluding the Q4 reinvestment-deposit year-end interest effect; a further 2 bps came from IT refund interest and yield on advances fell 3 bps.
Mid-market shift: 75-80% of new corporate customer acquisition is now mid-market, with yield upticks reported.
Low-yield share of book rose to 50.1% from 49.8% QoQ, attributed to opportunistic short-term corporate lending.
Headline CPI averaged about 3.93% in Q1 and reached 4.38% in June; food inflation reached 5.32% in June; RBI repo held at 5.25%, FY27 GDP forecast cut to 6.6%, inflation forecast raised to 5.1%.
Management reported no meaningful stress yet in CV/CE or MSME books, though it is watching the fuel-price and monsoon impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did processing fees fall sequentially, and is NIM sustainable with cost of funds near bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: Processing fees are seasonally lower in Q1 than Q4 because disbursements vary. Management said NIM is supported by liability actions and asset-mix change, and that CASA momentum should persist.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 22 bps QoQ drop in cost of deposits, and is there more to come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 11 bps was the real reduction after excluding the year-end reinvestment-deposit effect, plus about 2 bps from IT refund interest, with yield on advances down 3 bps. Management said a little more deposit-cost relief remains in one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the CASA growth and its mix across retail, commercial and corporate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited doubling of current-account openings vs a year ago, KPI changes favouring liability-side work, and competitive products. CA growth was roughly equal across retail, commercial and corporate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the credit cost guidance be revised given Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 credit cost was 41 bps, is likely to be at the lower end of the 50-60 bps guidance, but is not formally revising it given war and monsoon headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FCNR window affect deposits and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FCNR target, saying it expects its fair share, usually about 2.5%. Cost comparison depends on swap rates, rupee rates and timing; leverage adds asset-side growth, so it is not treated as a deposit-cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the business loan and auto segment growth set to pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named auto and small business loans as segments needing sharper execution. It said auto was hit by internal reorganisation and business loans had risk-metric cleanup, and that guardrails are now in place to push growth.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027 with a one-time net worth hit of 1.5-2%.
Inflation rising to 4.38% in June with fuel pass-through and monsoon risk to MSME, CV/CE and gold-loan books.
Gold loan tonnage reportedly down about 10-11% YoY per an analyst's question; management did not dispute this, and LTV is about 60%.
Current-account seasonality in Q1 and the pace of CASA ratio improvement from 32.23%.
Auto segment underperformance and business loan growth pick-up dependent on execution.
Timing and pricing of FCNR and leverage-linked deposits and ECB/IBU borrowings, sensitive to swap and rupee rates.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided NIM up about 5-6 bps per quarter on average over the next 3-4 quarters (Q1 NIM 3.33%, up 13 bps QoQ), backed by liability actions, lower cost of deposits (about 11 bps real QoQ cut) and asset-mix change; not necessarily linear.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Loan growth guided at mid-teens plus with a positive bias (gross advances up nearly 15% YoY, CV/CE +21%, gold +33%, cards +36%), plus the Standard Chartered card portfolio acquisition, though CIB growth was called opportunistic and business banking growth is yet to pick up.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is likely at the lower end of the 50-60 bps credit cost band (Q1 at 41 bps) and expects a positive bias on loan growth, but has not formally revised guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged war and monsoon headwinds, CPI at 4.38% in June, a cut to FY27 GDP forecast to 6.6%, and gold tonnage reportedly down about 10-11% YoY, none of which were disputed on the call.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Leverage-linked FCNR deposit product already launched with GIFT City IBU limits being allotted and more in the pipeline, and lines being arranged with offshore banks to channel leverage to customers.

rows.label: ECL transition from 1 April 2027
rows.why: One-time net worth impact of about 1.5% to 2% at transition, with management expecting no material ongoing P&L impact.

rows.label: Standard Chartered India credit card portfolio acquisition
rows.why: Acquisition is in progress and cards already grew 36% YoY, so it adds to card-book growth within the window.

rows.label: S&P investment-grade rating
rows.why: Opens access to bonds, ECBs and IBU funding, which gives the bank a new non-deposit funding channel to deploy.
